lines.japanese: ログ
lines.english: LOG

lines.japanese: 記録は残されている。
lines.english: A record remains.

lines.japanese:
書類にも、世界にも。
　だが、それらに頼る必要はない。
　忍自身の記憶だけで充分だった。
lines.english: In the documents, and in the world. But there is no need to rely upon either. Shinobu's own memory is enough.

lines.japanese:
遠い昔に思える。
　だが、まだ十年も経っていない。
　あっという間だった。
lines.english: It feels like the distant past. And yet not even ten years have gone by. It passed in the blink of an eye.

lines.japanese: 永遠にも等しかった―――
lines.english: It was as long as eternity—

lines.japanese: 青空が広がる。
lines.english: Blue sky spread overhead.

lines.japanese:
広大に思えるその世界も、しかし有限である。
　暗鬱とした想像だけは、無限にも広がりそうなのに。
lines.english: That world seemed boundless, and yet it was finite. Only grim imaginings appeared capable of expanding forever.

lines.japanese: 貴宮忍は視線を落とした。
lines.english: Shinobu Atemiya lowered his gaze.

lines.japanese:
そこに、白い家がある。
　建築したばかりと思われる、一軒家だった。
　上品な高級住宅である。
lines.english: A white house stood there. A single-family home that looked newly built. An elegant, expensive residence.

lines.japanese:
無機的で真新しい壁。
　手入れされた庭。
　乱れなく整う芝。
lines.english: Impersonal, immaculate walls. A tended garden. A lawn in perfect order.

lines.japanese:
あまりにも目立つ邸宅であった。
　周囲の家々をその白さで圧倒している。
　目立つ。
lines.english: The house was far too conspicuous. Its whiteness overwhelmed every home around it. It stood out.

lines.japanese:
忍はわずかに眉をひそめた。
　だがいつまでも突っ立ってはいられない。
　ポケットから封筒を取り出す。
lines.english: Shinobu frowned slightly. But he could not stand outside forever. He took an envelope from his pocket.

lines.japanese:
丸められて、くしゃくしゃだ。
　中身は鍵だった。
lines.english: It was rolled up and crumpled. Inside was a key.

lines.japanese:
市販されている中では、比較的セキュリティの高
いキープレートだ。
lines.english: For a commercially available model, it was a relatively secure key plate.

lines.japanese: 鍵を使って、家に入ろうとした。
lines.english: He tried to use the key to enter the house.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと、君！」
lines.english: “Excuse me, young man!”

lines.japanese:
声をかけられた。
　忍の脈拍と心拍数が、少し早まる。
lines.english: Someone called to him. Shinobu's pulse and heart rate accelerated slightly.

lines.japanese: 「はい、なんですか？」
lines.english: “Yes? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「あなた、ここの家の子？」
lines.english: “Are you the boy who lives here?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、そうです」
lines.english: “Yes, I am.”

lines.japanese:
二十代後半、せいぜい三十代前半の女性だ。
　背がすらっと高い。
　美醜の観点からだと、美しい部類に入る。
lines.english: The woman was in her late twenties, or her early thirties at most. She was tall and slender. In terms of looks, she fell into the beautiful category.

lines.japanese:
余分な脂肪がない。モデルを思わせる。
　表情は穏和で、敵意やきつさというものは見られ
ない。
lines.english: She carried no excess fat; she looked like a model. Her expression was mild, without any sign of hostility or severity.

lines.japanese: いや―――
lines.english: No—

lines.japanese:
きつさの痕跡は見られた。
　短い会話、ふと柔和さが消える瞬間があるのは、
笑い慣れていないせいだろう。
lines.english: There were traces of severity. In their brief conversation, her gentleness sometimes vanished— perhaps because she was unaccustomed to smiling.

lines.japanese: 「ここに住んでいる方を、はじめて見たものだから」
lines.english: “I've never seen anyone who lives here before.”

lines.japanese: あらかじめ用意された言葉を再生する。
lines.english: He played back the words prepared in advance.

lines.japanese: 「親が出張していたんです」
lines.english: “My parents were away on business.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、そうだったの」
lines.english: “Oh, I see.”

lines.japanese: 「帰ってくることになったんで、僕だけ一足先に」
lines.english: “They're coming back, so I arrived ahead of them.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、偉いのね」
lines.english: “I see. How responsible of you.”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ」
lines.english: “Not at all.”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、たかみや……さん？」
lines.english: “Let’s see… Takamiya?”

lines.japanese: 『貴宮』と書かれた表札を撫でながら。
lines.english: She ran a hand over the family name on the nameplate.

lines.japanese: 「あてみや、です」
lines.english: “It's Atemiya.”

lines.japanese: 「変わった名前なのね」
lines.english: “What an unusual name.”

lines.japanese: 「平安時代のお姫様の名前なんだそうです」
lines.english: “I'm told it was the name of a princess in the Heian period.”

lines.japanese: 「そう。じゃあなたは貴宮……？」
lines.english: “I see. Then you're…?”

lines.japanese: 「忍です。よろしくお願いします」
lines.english: “Shinobu. It's a pleasure to meet you.”

lines.japanese:
敬礼をした。
　それは、違う。
lines.english: He saluted. That was wrong.

lines.japanese:
女性は面食らっていた。
　忍も気づく。
　すぐに深々と頭を下げた。
lines.english: The woman was taken aback. Shinobu noticed. He immediately bowed deeply.

lines.japanese:
少年らしいおどけだと思ったのか、女性の顔には
微笑が浮かぶ。
lines.english: Perhaps she took it for a boyish joke. A smile appeared on the woman's face.

lines.japanese: 「素敵なお名前ね、忍君」
lines.english: “That's a lovely name, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: そっけなく、棒読みを意識して言う。
lines.english: He consciously spoke in a flat, curt monotone.

lines.japanese: 「私は紅緒といいます」
lines.english: “My name is Benio.”

lines.japanese: 「よろしくお願いします、紅緒さん」
lines.english: “It's a pleasure to meet you, Ms. Benio.”

lines.japanese: 「おかーさん」
lines.english: “Mom.”

lines.japanese:
弱々しい声が、二人の背後から投げかけられた。
　忍は何気なく見やる。
lines.english: A frail voice reached them from behind. Shinobu glanced over without particular interest.

lines.japanese:
少女だ。
　忍より二つ三つほど幼い。
　駆け寄って、母親のふもとに寄り添う。
lines.english: A girl. Two or three years younger than Shinobu. She ran over and nestled at the foot of her mother.

lines.japanese:
まさにふもとだ。
　長身の母親とは、別世界の等身に思えた。
lines.english: The foot was exactly right. Beside her tall mother, the girl seemed built to the scale of another world.

lines.japanese: 「娘のあずさです」
lines.english: “This is my daughter, Azusa.”

lines.japanese: 忍を警戒のまなざしで見ている。
lines.english: She watched Shinobu warily.

lines.japanese: 「……こんにちは」
lines.english: “…Hello.”

lines.japanese:
事務的に挨拶した。
　忍にとって、この少女には何の意味もない。
lines.english: His greeting was purely perfunctory. To Shinobu, this girl meant nothing.

lines.japanese: あずさは非友好的な視線以外に何も返さない。
lines.english: Azusa offered nothing in return but an unfriendly stare.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、またね」
lines.english: “Well, I'll see you again.”

lines.japanese:
笑って、立ち去る。
　あずさも母親に追随した。
　歩幅が違いすぎて、娘は小走りだ。
lines.english: She smiled and walked away. Azusa followed her mother. Their strides differed so much that the girl had to trot.

lines.japanese:
途中、一度だけ忍をかえりみた。
　視線は交差しない。
　忍は考え事をしていたからだ。
lines.english: As they walked away, she looked back at Shinobu just once. Their eyes did not meet. Shinobu was lost in thought.

lines.japanese:
紅緒という母親の、あまりにも儀礼的な笑顔につ
いて。
lines.english: He was thinking about the all-too-formal smile of the mother, Benio.

lines.japanese: 自室。
lines.english: His room.

lines.japanese:
目立った家具はない。
　不要だからだ。
lines.english: There was no furniture worth remarking upon. He had no need for any.

lines.japanese:
荷物も鞄ひとつだけ。
　整理する必要もない。
lines.english: His only luggage was a single bag. There was nothing to put in order.

lines.japanese: 夕方になった。
lines.english: Evening came.

lines.japanese:
忍はずっと待機していた。
　待つことは苦痛ではない。
　慣れている。
lines.english: Shinobu had spent the entire time waiting. Waiting was not painful. He was used to it.

lines.japanese:
つらい時間、苦痛の時間よりも、それは穏やかで
あたたかい。
lines.english: Compared with hours of torment and pain, waiting was calm and warm.

lines.japanese:
先ほど出会った少女のことを思い出す。
　彼女は何を考えているのだろう。
lines.english: He remembered the girl he had met earlier. What was she thinking?

lines.japanese:
その生は、どんな彩りをもって満たされているの
だろう。
lines.english: What colors filled her life?

lines.japanese:
興味がないこともない。
　だが、意味はないのだ。
　忍は機械であることを求められていた。
lines.english: It was not that he felt no interest. But it had no meaning. Shinobu was required to be a machine.

lines.japanese: やがて―――
lines.english: At last—

lines.japanese: 「……ただいま」
lines.english: “…I'm home.”

lines.japanese:
混乱。
　千鳥の声に相違ない。
　声の調子に違和感があった。
lines.english: Confusion. The voice was unmistakably Chidori's. Yet something in its tone felt wrong.

lines.japanese: 「忍、もう来ているの？」
lines.english: “Shinobu, are you here already?”

lines.japanese:
満面の笑みで、千鳥が入ってきた。
　ふくれあがったビニール袋を、二つを下げている。
　いや、それよりも。
lines.english: Chidori entered with a radiant smile. She carried two bulging plastic bags. No—more importantly…

lines.japanese: 「荷物、運ぶの手伝ってくれる？」
lines.english: “Will you help me carry these?”

lines.japanese:
忍は面食らっていた。
　千鳥が違う。
　いつもと違う。
lines.english: Shinobu was taken aback. Chidori was different. This was not how she usually acted.

lines.japanese:
狼狽える。
　千鳥が真顔に戻った。
lines.english: He grew flustered. Chidori’s face turned serious again.
“…Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: いつもの千鳥だ。忍は安堵する。
lines.english: This was the usual Chidori. Shinobu felt relieved.

lines.japanese:
「柔軟になりなさい。この仕事について、説明を繰
　り返す必要がある？」
lines.english: “You must learn to adapt. Do I need to explain this assignment again?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、ありません」
lines.english: “No, you do not.”

lines.japanese: 「私はあなたの姉。ここが自宅。二人は仲良し」
lines.english: “I'm your older sister. This is our home. We're close.”

lines.japanese: だが、千鳥は説明した。
lines.english: But Chidori explained it anyway.

lines.japanese: 「不自然にならない程度に、そう振るまいなさい」
lines.english: “Act that way, but don’t overdo it.”

lines.japanese: 黙って頷く忍。
lines.english: Shinobu nodded in silence.

lines.japanese:
「多少の齟齬は、子供のすることで緩和されるから
　心配はいらないでしょう？」
lines.english: “Any minor discrepancies will be mitigated by the fact that you're a child, so you needn't worry.”

lines.japanese:
齟齬。緩和。知らない言葉だ。
　なんとなく意味はわかる。
　千鳥は気遣わない。
lines.english: Discrepancy. Mitigation. Words he did not know. He understood them after a fashion. Chidori made no allowances.

lines.japanese:
だがそうでなければ、今の立場にはいなかったは
ずだ。
lines.english: But otherwise, she would never have attained her present position.

lines.japanese:
「まあ、それは明日からで結構です。
　私もそのつもりで行動します。
　あなたも留意なさい」
lines.english: “Still, beginning tomorrow will be sufficient. I will conduct myself with that understanding. See that you bear it in mind as well.”

lines.japanese:
留意。これも知らない言葉だ。
　千鳥との会話は、忍に軽いめまいをもたらす。
　言葉の海。忍は小舟。翻弄される。
lines.english: Bear in mind. Another phrase he did not know. Talking to Chidori made Shinobu slightly dizzy. An ocean of words. Shinobu a little boat, tossed upon it.

lines.japanese:
いろいろな言葉を耳にするたび、世界に対する認
識の少なさが浮き彫りにされる。
lines.english: Every unfamiliar word he heard threw the poverty of his understanding of the world into relief.

lines.japanese: １００％と世界と同化できていない。
lines.english: He was not one hundred percent assimilated into the world.

lines.japanese:
あるいは孤独。
　ないしは孤立。
　だからこそ悩む。
lines.english: Perhaps that was loneliness. Or isolation. That was why he struggled.

lines.japanese:
自分は本当に正しいのか。
　彼らは本当に正しいのか。
　またどうやって立証するのか。
lines.english: Was he truly right? Were they truly right? And how was either proposition to be proved?

lines.japanese:
検証に必要とされる時間はどれほどか。
　思索にふければ、忍を襲うのは絶望だけだ。
lines.english: How much time would verification require? Whenever he sank into thought, nothing but despair closed in on him.

lines.japanese:
たかだか百年に満たない人生で、何者になれると
いうのか。
lines.english: What could anyone become in a life that did not even reach a hundred years?

lines.japanese:
忍はそのようなことを考えていた。
　施設しか知らない忍。
lines.english: Such were Shinobu's thoughts. Shinobu, who knew nothing but the facility.

lines.japanese:
だがその胸中には自我と呼ぶべきものが確かにあ
った。
lines.english: Yet there was certainly something within him that could be called a self.

lines.japanese:
生まれつきレールが用意されていた忍はしかし、
漫然と流れに身を任せる以外の生き方を知らない。
　情熱と意志のよりあわせ方を知らない。
lines.english: The rails of Shinobu's life had been laid before him from birth. He knew no way to live but to let himself be carried along their course. He did not know how to braid passion and will together.

lines.japanese: 結果、空虚な人格が形成された。
lines.english: The result was an empty personality.

lines.japanese: 「何か問題は？」
lines.english: “Any problems?”

lines.japanese:
忍は折り目を正して、話す。
　紅緒という母親と接触したことを。
lines.english: Shinobu straightened and spoke. He told her of his contact with the mother named Benio.

lines.japanese:
その不審な態度についても触れる。
　会話中に感じた、病的な気配について。
lines.english: He also mentioned her suspicious behavior. The pathological air he had sensed during their conversation.

lines.japanese: 「……仮面をつけているのね」
lines.english: “…She's wearing a mask.”

lines.japanese: 「かめん？」
lines.english: “A mask?”

lines.japanese: 「世間に顔を向けるため自分を装っているのよ」
lines.english: “She puts on a face for the world.”

lines.japanese:
「それは自然に定まることもあれば、選択的に決定
　されることもあります」
lines.english: “Sometimes that face takes shape naturally; sometimes it is consciously chosen.”

lines.japanese: 「……よくわかりません。どうしたらいいですか？」
lines.english: “…I don't really understand. What should I do?”

lines.japanese:
「近所づきあいをしましょう。深入りしない程度に。
　いい？」
lines.english: “Be neighborly, but don't become too deeply involved. Understood?”

lines.japanese: 「やってみます」
lines.english: “I'll try.”

lines.japanese:
「あなたはまだ世界に触れて日が浅い。慣れないこ
　とも多いでしょうけど……じき身に付くから」
lines.english: “You’re still new to the world. A lot will feel unfamiliar… but you’ll soon get the hang of it.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 敬礼をする。
lines.english: He saluted.

lines.japanese:
「それももうしないで。
　ふざけてやるならともかく、ね」
lines.english: “Stop doing that too. Unless you mean it as a joke.”

lines.japanese: 「でも」
lines.english: “But…”

lines.japanese:
「灰野の指導内容は、これからは忘れなさい。
　軍隊ならともかく、日常では不自然だもの」
lines.english: “From now on, forget what Haino taught you. It may suit the military, but it is unnatural in ordinary life.”
“…Yes.”

lines.japanese:
さて、と千鳥はビニール袋を持ち上げる。
　弾んだ声で、
lines.english: “Now then,” Chidori says, lifting the plastic bags. Her voice turns buoyant:

lines.japanese: 「冷蔵庫に片づけるの、手伝ってくれる？」
lines.english: “Will you help me put these in the refrigerator?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes.”

lines.japanese:
そんな任務ははじめてだ。
　忍と千鳥は、パックの食料品を冷蔵庫に押し込め
る作業に没頭した。
lines.english: He had never been given a mission like this. Shinobu and Chidori devoted themselves to stuffing packages of food into the refrigerator.

lines.japanese: 「食事は？」
lines.english: “Have you eaten?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、まだ」
lines.english: “No, not yet.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、じゃあ……何を食べる？」
lines.english: “I see. Then… what would you like?”

lines.japanese: 問われて、言葉に詰まった。
lines.english: At the question, words failed him.

lines.japanese: 「それは……僕が決めるんですか？」
lines.english: “Am… I supposed to decide?”

lines.japanese: 「食べたいものはないの？」
lines.english: “Isn't there anything you want to eat?”

lines.japanese: 答えられない。
lines.english: He could not answer.

lines.japanese: 「……そうね。そうだったわね」
lines.english: “…Right. Of course.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさい、私も不慣れね」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. I'm new to this too.”

lines.japanese:
「今後の任務では、あなたは判断力を身につける必
　要があるの。そのため自由意志というものを、少
　し積極的に身につけなければならない」
lines.english: “Your future assignments will require you to develop judgment. To that end, you must be somewhat more proactive in acquiring a thing called free will.”

lines.japanese: 「自由意志、ですか？」
lines.english: “Free will?”

lines.japanese: 「そうよ、天才君」
lines.english: “That's right, little genius.”

lines.japanese: 「……わかりません」
lines.english: “…I don't understand.”

lines.japanese: 「食べたいものを、自分で選べる程度で結構よ」
lines.english: “Being able to choose what you'd like to eat will do for a start.”

lines.japanese: パックの一つを千鳥が眺めている。
lines.english: Chidori studied one of the packages.

lines.japanese:
「これにしましょう。それとサラダと……
　飲み物が……これ、でいいのかな」
lines.english: “Let's have this. And a salad… A drink… Will this do, I wonder?”

lines.japanese:
本当にぎこちなく、選んだのだ。
　二人はレンジでチンした食物を、無言で食べた。
lines.english: She was truly awkward about choosing. The two silently ate food warmed in the microwave.

lines.japanese: それから千鳥と忍は、年の離れた姉弟として生きた。
lines.english: From then on, Chidori and Shinobu lived as an older sister and a much younger brother.

lines.japanese: 不器用に生きた。
lines.english: They lived awkwardly.

lines.japanese: 「戻りました」
lines.english: “I've returned.”

lines.japanese: 「どうだった？」
lines.english: “How did it go?”

lines.japanese: 「報告書、作りますか？」
lines.english: “Would you like me to prepare a report?”

lines.japanese: 「いらないわ。言葉でいいわよ」
lines.english: “No. Just tell me.”

lines.japanese: 「では口頭で報告します」
lines.english: “Then I will report orally.”

lines.japanese: 「そうじゃなくて……」
lines.english: “That's not what I meant…”

lines.japanese: 拙い会話をかわし。
lines.english: They held awkward conversations.

lines.japanese: 「忍、ちょっと来てくれる？」
lines.english: “Shinobu, could you come here a moment?”

lines.japanese: 「これは？」
lines.english: “What is this?”

lines.japanese: 「おもちゃよ」
lines.english: “A toy.”

lines.japanese: 「なぜおもちゃが？」
lines.english: “Why is there a toy?”

lines.japanese:
「クラスの友達と、話を合わせるために触っておい
　た方がいいと思って」
lines.english: “I thought you should try it, so you can follow the conversations your classmates have.”

lines.japanese: 「どう使うんですか？」
lines.english: “How do you use it?”

lines.japanese: 「それは……」
lines.english: “Well…”

lines.japanese: 「こう、かな……？」
lines.english: “Like this… perhaps?”

lines.japanese: 「きゃあ！」
lines.english: “Eek!”

lines.japanese: やりとりを重ね。
lines.english: So their exchanges continued.

lines.japanese: 「料理を作ってみたの」
lines.english: “I tried cooking.”
“…You cooked this, Teacher?”

lines.japanese: 「姉さんと呼びなさい」
lines.english: “Call me Sis.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、姉さん」
lines.english: “Yes, Sis.”

lines.japanese: 「とっさに出ないわよ、普段から口にしてないと」
lines.english: “It won’t come naturally in the moment unless you make a habit of saying it.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese:
「いつもコンビニばかりでは、健康に悪いでしょう
　から」
lines.english: “Living on convenience-store food can't be good for your health.”

lines.japanese: 「さあ、食べて」
lines.english: “Go on. Try it.”

lines.japanese: 「どう？」
lines.english: “Well?”

lines.japanese: 「……少し問題があるような気がします」
lines.english: “…I believe there may be a slight problem.”

lines.japanese: 「え、どのあたりに？」
lines.english: “What? Which part?”

lines.japanese: 「味付けが、おかしいみたいです」
lines.english: “The seasoning appears to be wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「え、嘘……あむ」
lines.english: “What? Surely not… Mm.”

lines.japanese: 「ん～～～ッッッ」
lines.english: “Mmmph!”

lines.japanese: 「塩を入れすぎたみたいね」
lines.english: “It seems I used too much salt.”

lines.japanese: 「食べられないこともないです」
lines.english: “It isn't entirely inedible.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、だめ。よしなさい」
lines.english: “No, don't. Stop eating.”

lines.japanese: 奇妙な関係を維持していった。
lines.english: And so they maintained their strange relationship.

lines.japanese:
本鈴が鳴ると、生徒たちは一斉に席につく。
　ざわめきの残滓が、ここそこに残る。
　なかなか教師が来ない。
lines.english: When the bell rang, the students took their seats as one. Remnants of chatter lingered here and there. The teacher was nowhere to be seen.

lines.japanese: 定刻を数分も過ぎて、ようやく扉が開いた。
lines.english: Several minutes after class was meant to begin, the door finally opened.

lines.japanese: 「おはようございます」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese:
何事もなかったかのように、やってきたのは若い
女性教師である。
lines.english: A young woman entered as though nothing were amiss. Their teacher.

lines.japanese:
「今日は特に連絡もありませんから、のんびり行き
　ましょう」
lines.english: “There are no particular announcements today, so let's take it easy.”

lines.japanese: 女教師は出席簿を開く。
lines.english: She opened the attendance book.

lines.japanese: 「出欠を取ります」
lines.english: “I'll take attendance.”

lines.japanese: 繰り返される、単調な応対。
lines.english: The same monotonous exchange, repeated over and over.

lines.japanese:
日常のリズムに、忍は取り込まれる。
　穏やかな朝の時間。
　ふと沙也加の席を見る。
lines.english: Shinobu was drawn into the rhythm of daily life. A tranquil morning. His eyes drifted to Sayaka’s desk.

lines.japanese:
確固たる存在として、彼女はそこにいる。
　何も変わりはしない。
　そう信じている。
lines.english: She was there, solidly and undeniably present. Nothing would change. He believed that.

lines.japanese:
時間は目に見えない。
　変わりないようでいて、瞬間ごとに移ろっていく。
　気がつけば、変わりないはずの今は、過去となる。
lines.english: Time cannot be seen. Though it appears unchanged, it shifts with every instant. Before one knows it, the supposedly unchanging present has become the past.

lines.japanese:
しかし今だけは……ゆるりと過ぎて、軽い眠気を
誘った。
lines.english: For now, though… time drifted by, making him a little sleepy.

lines.japanese:
鼻先を、稀釈された緑の匂いが通過する。
　森林からたどり着いたそれは、忍を沈静する。
lines.english: A faint, diluted scent of green passed beneath his nose. Having traveled from the forest, it soothed him.

lines.japanese:
ほとんど万年といってよい頭痛が、かすかに緩和
されるのが嬉しい。
lines.english: He welcomed the slight easing of the headache that was nearly his permanent companion.

lines.japanese: だから森に近い学校の、授業は決して苦痛ではない。
lines.english: That was why lessons at a school so close to the forest were never painful.

lines.japanese: 「貴宮忍君」
lines.english: “Shinobu Atemiya.”
“…Present.”

lines.japanese:
狙い澄ましたかのような指名で、脆い夢心地は千
々に砕けてしまった。
lines.english: As though aimed with perfect precision, the summons shattered his fragile reverie into a thousand pieces.

lines.japanese:
愛すべき退屈さをもって、四限目が終わる。
　昼食休み。
　争うように学生食堂に行く……ことはない。
lines.english: Fourth period ended in its lovable tedium. Lunch break. They raced one another to the cafeteria… or rather, they did not.

lines.japanese:
誰もが雑談などしながら、のんびりと待っている。
　やがて係の女子二人がやってきて、予防接種のク
ラス順を告げた。
lines.english: Everyone waited around, chatting idly. Before long, the two girls on duty arrived and announced the vaccination schedule for the classes.

lines.japanese:
当クラスは昼休みの後半から。
　それを聞くと、生徒らはそれぞれ食事を済ませる
ため、立ち上がった。
lines.english: Their class was scheduled for the second half of lunch. Upon hearing that, the students rose to go and finish their meals.

lines.japanese:
学食組はダッシュだ。
　今日は不利である。
　一方、弁当組はのんびりしたものだ。
lines.english: The cafeteria contingent broke into a sprint. Today, they were at a disadvantage. Those who had brought lunch took their time.

lines.japanese: 忍は学食組だったが、沙也加に合わせた。
lines.english: Shinobu belonged to the cafeteria contingent, but matched Sayaka's pace.

lines.japanese: 「ゆっくり行こうか？」
lines.english: “Shall we take our time?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 連れだって、廊下に出た。
lines.english: They went out into the hall together.

lines.japanese:
並んで歩く二人は無言。
　忍の半歩後ろを、沙也加が歩く。
　学校全体を包む喧噪が、ＢＧＭとなって流れゆく。
lines.english: They walked side by side in silence. Sayaka kept half a step behind Shinobu. The clamor enveloping the school flowed around them like background music.

lines.japanese:
雰囲気に身をなじませるよう、二人はゆっくりと
歩いた。
lines.english: They walked slowly, as though settling into the atmosphere around them.

lines.japanese: 彼らの目当てはうどんないしはそばである。
lines.english: They were bound for udon or soba.

lines.japanese:
これは人気がない。
　また品切れもない。
　よって焦る必要がない。
lines.english: Neither was popular. Neither ever sold out. Therefore, there was no need to hurry.

lines.japanese: 「顔色、いいみたいね」
lines.english: “You look well today.”

lines.japanese: 「最近は少し」
lines.english: “I've been a little better lately.”

lines.japanese: 「メイクをしている日は、心配だわ」
lines.english: “I worry on the days when you're wearing makeup.”

lines.japanese: 「……バレてましたか」
lines.english: “…You noticed?”

lines.japanese: 「これでも女だもの」
lines.english: “I am a woman, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「だからしていない日は、安心できるわね」
lines.english: “So when you aren't wearing any, I can relax.”

lines.japanese: 「……今日はまあまあ調子が良くて」
lines.english: “…I'm feeling reasonably good today.”

lines.japanese: 「いいことよ、それ」
lines.english: “That's good.”

lines.japanese:
と沙也加は微笑む。
　それが忍を喜ばせるための、事務的な行為だとは
わかっていた。
lines.english: Sayaka smiled. He knew it was a perfunctory gesture meant to please him.

lines.japanese: 「のんびり行きましょう」
lines.english: “Let's take our time.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 食堂までの道のり、それだけの言葉をかわした。
lines.english: Those were the only words they exchanged on the way to the cafeteria.

lines.japanese:
「例文のポイントとしては、この部分が複数形になっ
　ていますから、同格の単数形に繋げるためには選択
　肢Ａ、ＢではなくＣが適切ということになります」
lines.english: “The important point in this sentence is that this element is plural. To connect it to a singular term in apposition, the appropriate answer is not A or B, but C.”

lines.japanese: 「複数形であるか、が解答の鍵になっています」
lines.english: “Whether it’s plural is the key to the answer.”

lines.japanese:
「試験では設問内にこのような指針があるものも多
　いんですが、判断の難しい問題が出ることもあ
　ります」
lines.english: “Many exam questions contain clues like this, but some questions can be difficult to judge.”

lines.japanese: 「たとえば、テキスト８７ページにある―――」
lines.english: “For example, the passage on page eighty-seven—”

lines.japanese: にこやかな千鳥。こんなことは珍しい。
lines.english: Chidori was smiling. That was rare.

lines.japanese:
「このあたりはパターンですから、記憶してしまう
　方がいいですね。後でプリントにまとめておきま
　すので」
lines.english: “These are standard patterns, so you're better off memorizing them. I'll put them together in a handout later.”

lines.japanese:
そんな千鳥を、忍は見つめていた。
　深い感慨があるわけではなく、考えがあるわけで
もなく。
lines.english: Shinobu watched her. Not out of any profound feeling, nor because he had anything in particular on his mind.

lines.japanese: ただ、ぼんやりと見つめていた。
lines.english: He was simply watching her in a daze.

lines.japanese: 「ではこの問いを、ぼーっとしている貴宮君」
lines.english: “Then perhaps Mr. Atemiya, who is staring into space, can answer this one.”
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese:
千鳥先生の急降下爆撃―――
　不幸な目標は、忍だった。
lines.english: Ms. Chidori's dive-bombing run— and Shinobu was its unfortunate target.

lines.japanese: 「はい、減点１。１１２ページの例題３です」
lines.english: “One point off. Example three on page one hundred twelve.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい」
lines.english: “Oh. Right.”

lines.japanese: 慌ててテキストに目を流した。
lines.english: He hurriedly scanned the textbook.

lines.japanese: 「帰ろうか」
lines.english: “Shall we go home?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese:
帰路。
　二人の足音が寄り添う。
lines.english: The road home. Their footsteps kept close company.

lines.japanese: 「今川焼き食べない？」
lines.english: “Want a red-bean cake?”

lines.japanese: 「そうね」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 「奢るよ」
lines.english: “My treat.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 買い食いをしたりもする。
lines.english: Sometimes, they stopped for a snack.

lines.japanese: 「本屋、いいかしら？」
lines.english: “Would you mind if we went to the bookstore?”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ」
lines.english: “Not at all.”

lines.japanese:
たまに寄り道をする。
　冷やかしも多いが。
lines.english: Sometimes, they took a detour. Often without buying anything.

lines.japanese:
お得意様である二人の立ち読みは、咎められるこ
とはない。
lines.english: They were good customers, so no one objected when they stood and read in the shop.

lines.japanese: 「これ、ください」
lines.english: “I'll take this, please.”

lines.japanese:
古びた、工場跡などが立ち並んでいる。
　活動していたのは、昭和の頃だろうか。
　今では煙をあげているものはない。
lines.english: Old, abandoned factories stood in rows. Perhaps they had been active in the Showa era. None of them sent up smoke now.

lines.japanese:
再利用されることなく忘れ去られた、町外れ。
　だが鬱然とした感じはなく、乾いた味わいが漂う。
　ここには人はいない。
lines.english: The edge of town, forgotten and never put to new use. Yet there was nothing gloomy about it. The place had a dry, weathered character. There was no one here.

lines.japanese:
一人で訪れれば、自らの存在さえ忘れてしまいか
ねない。
lines.english: Come alone, and one might even forget one's own existence.

lines.japanese:
人は自身を直接見ることはできないからだ。
　無人が浸透した背景は、自己性を曖昧に喪失させる。
lines.english: No one, after all, can see themselves directly. A backdrop steeped in human absence blurs and dissolves the sense of self.

lines.japanese:
人が人でなくなる道を越えた先、聖域は置かれて
いる。
lines.english: The sanctuary lay beyond a road along which a person ceased to be human.

lines.japanese:
過去を忘れ去るように、通り過ぎていく。
　もう稼働することはない、忘却の果てにある錆色
の建物群を、忍たちは訪う。
lines.english: They passed through as though consigning the past to oblivion. Shinobu and the others sought out the rust-colored buildings at oblivion's farthest edge— buildings that would never operate again.

lines.japanese:
ひときわ大きな工場だった。
　流れた歳月もひときわ長いのか、空気に混じる金
属臭は薄い。
lines.english: One factory was larger than all the rest. Perhaps it had stood idle longer too; only the faintest trace of metal remained in the air.

lines.japanese:
工業機器はほとんど残されていない。
　撤去されたか、売り払われたか。
lines.english: Almost none of the industrial machinery remained. Removed, perhaps, or sold off.

lines.japanese:
名実ともに空洞化した建物には、しかし奇妙さ加
減が見て取れる。
lines.english: The building was hollow in every sense, yet there was something unmistakably strange about it.

lines.japanese:
違和感の正体は、本棚・ソファ・食器棚・不統一
な椅子たち。
lines.english: The source of that dissonance was a bookcase, a sofa, a cupboard, and an assortment of mismatched chairs.

lines.japanese:
乾燥した廃墟に、ぎこちなく生活空間が混入され
ているせいだ。
lines.english: A living space had been awkwardly grafted into the parched ruins.

lines.japanese:
互いに話し合い、触れ、静寂さえもわかちあう。
　昔は秘密基地と呼ばれていた場所。
　今は……さすがにそう呼ばれることはなくなった。
lines.english: Here, they talked, touched, and shared even silence. Long ago, they had called this place their secret base. Now… naturally, they no longer called it that.

lines.japanese:
最大数７の共有空間。
　考えることなく、自らでいられる場所。
　一人で来ることもある。
lines.english: A shared space for no more than seven. A place where they could be themselves without thinking. Sometimes one of them came alone.

lines.japanese:
皆といることもある。
　あずさとともにいることは、特に多かった。
lines.english: Sometimes they all came together. He was there with Azusa especially often.

lines.japanese:
今日のように、沙也加と二人きりでいる時だけは、
少しばかり忍も緊張してしまう。
lines.english: Only when he was alone with Sayaka, as he was today, did Shinobu find himself a little nervous.

lines.japanese:
鞄をガラクタの上に投げ出す。
　ソファを占拠して、さっそく買ってきた本を開く。
lines.english: He tossed his bag onto a pile of junk. Claimed the sofa and immediately opened the book he had bought.

lines.japanese:
しばし物語の世界に引き込まれる。
　どれだけ時間が経過したろうか。
lines.english: For a time, the story drew him into its world. How long had passed?

lines.japanese:
気がつけば、温度を持った芳醇さが間近から漂っ
てきている。
lines.english: By the time he noticed, a warm, mellow aroma was drifting from somewhere close by.

lines.japanese:
数十分ぶりにページから目をはがすと、隣に沙也
加が立っていた。
lines.english: When he finally tore his eyes from the page, many minutes later, Sayaka was standing beside him.

lines.japanese:
工場に来てすぐ、姿を消していたのだが……どう
やら飲み物を作っていたらしい。
lines.english: She had vanished soon after they reached the factory… Apparently, she had been making a drink.

lines.japanese: 「どうぞ」
lines.english: “Here.”

lines.japanese:
珈琲が湯気を立てていた。
　工場で火を使うためには、主にキャンプ用の携
帯コンロを用いる。
lines.english: Steam rose from a cup of coffee. They generally used a portable camping stove whenever they needed a flame in the factory.

lines.japanese:
時間をかけてドリップで淹れてくれたに違いなか
った。
lines.english: She must have spent some time brewing it, one careful pour at a time.

lines.japanese:
沙也加はこうして家事に近いことをはじめると、
丁寧ではあるがやたら時間をかける。
lines.english: Whenever Sayaka began anything resembling housework, she was thorough but took an inordinate amount of time.

lines.japanese: （……年寄りくさい、なんて思っても言えないけど）
lines.english: (She really is like an old lady… not that I could ever say so.)

lines.japanese:
彼女はこう見えて本来、豪快な気質だ。
　細かな作業は得意ではないというが、
　嫌いというわけでもないらしい。
lines.english: For all appearances, she was bold by nature. She said she was no good at fine, fiddly work, though she did not seem to dislike it.

lines.japanese:
人生で焦る必要を感じていないのか、全てにおい
て取り組み方が懇切丁寧。
lines.english: Perhaps she saw no reason to hurry through life; whatever she did, she did with painstaking care.

lines.japanese:
一緒にいると、時間の経過が遅くなったように、
忍には感じられる。
lines.english: When he was with her, Shinobu felt as though time itself slowed.

lines.japanese: まるで老後のように―――
lines.english: As though they were already in their twilight years—

lines.japanese: （……絶対言えない）
lines.english: (…I could never say that.)

lines.japanese: カップを口につけた。
lines.english: He brought the cup to his lips.

lines.japanese: 「……ん、温かい」
lines.english: “…Mm. It's warm.”

lines.japanese:
カップが。
　いったん湯でぬくめてあるようだ。
　本当に、取り組み方が細かい。
lines.english: The cup was. She seemed to have warmed it with hot water first. She really did fuss over every little detail.

lines.japanese: 「おかわりが必要なら、五分前に言って」
lines.english: “If you want another cup, tell me five minutes beforehand.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 実際はその何倍かはかかるんだろうな、と呟く。
lines.english: Under his breath, he observed that in practice it would probably take several times that long.

lines.japanese: 「歴史の本？」
lines.english: “A history book?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。ミステリー」
lines.english: “Yes. A mystery.”

lines.japanese: 本を手前に傾けて、背表紙を見せる。
lines.english: He tilted the book toward himself, showing her the spine.

lines.japanese: 「面白そうね」
lines.english: “It looks interesting.”

lines.japanese:
「あとで読むといいよ、本棚の蔵書にするつもりな
　んで」
lines.english: “You can read it later. I was planning to add it to the books here.”

lines.japanese: 「そうさせてもらおうかしら」
lines.english: “I think I will.”

lines.japanese:
と、隣に腰を下ろす。
　張りを失った布地を通して、彼女の体重を確かな
ものとして感じた。
lines.english: She sat down beside him. Through the sofa’s sagging upholstery, he distinctly felt her weight.

lines.japanese:
単純なようだが、それだけで心は華やぐ。
　自分のカップを無音で口に運ぶ様を、横滑りした
目で観察する。
lines.english: Simple as it was, that alone made his heart lift. He stole a sidelong look as she silently raised her cup to her lips.

lines.japanese:
武家の娘が持つような直線的な凛々しさの上に、
彫像めいた横顔が置かれている。
lines.english: She had the clean, upright bearing of a samurai's daughter, topped by a profile like carved stone.

lines.japanese:
美貌というほどの圧力はない。
　誇り高そうに吊られた目尻だが、斜め下に坂滑り
の視線は、決して人を刺す風ではない。
lines.english: Her beauty was not the kind that imposed itself. The outer corners of her eyes tilted proudly upward, but her gaze slanted down and away, never seeming sharp enough to wound.

lines.japanese:
儚さの強い容色だ。
　見ていると、いつか彼女が消えてしまうのではな
いかという不安に魅入られる。
lines.english: A profound fragility suffused her features. Looking at her, he found himself transfixed by the fear that one day she might simply vanish.

lines.japanese:
生命力の強さが備わっていないのだ。
　這いずってでも生存するという気概。
lines.english: She possessed no great vitality. No resolve to survive even if she had to crawl.

lines.japanese:
生き汚さ。
　生命あるいは目的への執着。
　そういったものが抜けている。
lines.english: The shameless tenacity of the living. An attachment to life, or to some purpose. Such things were absent from her.

lines.japanese:
結果、沙也加の存在感は器の出来に比して、差し
引かれている。
lines.english: The result was that, fine as the vessel was, Sayaka herself seemed somehow less present.

lines.japanese:
学校でも彼女に話しかける者はほとんどいない。
　時折、交際を申し出てくる酔狂な人間もいた。
lines.english: Hardly anyone spoke to her at school. Now and then, some eccentric would ask her out.

lines.japanese:
酔狂というのは、ほとんど沙也加との個人的深交
を結ばず、一方的に好意を伝えてくるものばかりだ
からだ。
lines.english: He called them eccentric because almost none had formed any real personal connection with Sayaka; they merely appeared and declared their feelings.

lines.japanese:
彼女が、そのような軽佻さに応じることは有り得
ない。
lines.english: She could never have responded to such frivolity.

lines.japanese:
ゆえに結果は明々白々なものである。
　酔狂と言えた。
　傾けたカップから、沙也加が白湯を含む。
lines.english: So the outcome was plain from the start. Eccentric really was the only word for them. Sayaka tipped her cup and took a sip of hot water.

lines.japanese:
彼女は時折、それを飲むのである。
　口内から食道に潜る、熱せられた液体を思う。
lines.english: She did this from time to time. He pictured the heated liquid slipping from her mouth and down her esophagus.

lines.japanese: （……いかんいかん）
lines.english: (…No, no.)

lines.japanese:
艶めいた喉の波打ちを契機に、果てのない観察行
為から忍は立ち返った。
lines.english: The sensuous ripple of her throat broke the spell of Shinobu's endless scrutiny.

lines.japanese:
彼女同様、コーヒーを啜った。
　揃って、ほぅ、と息をつく。
　同じタイミングだった。
lines.english: He sipped his coffee in kind. Together they let out a soft sigh. At precisely the same moment.

lines.japanese:
忍が横を見やる。
　すでに彼女の瞳が待ち伏せするかのように置かれ
ていた。
lines.english: Shinobu glanced to the side. Her gaze was already there, waiting as if to ambush him.

lines.japanese:
目が合う。
　忍は微笑する。
　沙也加も微笑する。
lines.english: Their eyes met. Shinobu smiled. Sayaka smiled too.

lines.japanese:
そこに含羞の戸惑いはない。
　やわらかな空気が、二人を浸す。
　幼い少年少女が結ぶ、甘やかな交情を思わせた。
lines.english: There was no shy hesitation between them. A gentle warmth enfolded them both. It called to mind the tender affection between a young boy and girl.

lines.japanese:
家にいてもやることはない。
　余暇はたいてい、工場で過ごす。
　それは忍に限ったことではない。
lines.english: There was nothing to do at home. They spent most of their spare time at the factory. That was true of more than Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
工場は、七人の場所。
　皆で作り上げた憩いの場。
　廃れた場所ではある。
lines.english: The factory belonged to the seven of them. A place of rest they had made together. It was a ruin.

lines.japanese:
かつての繁栄の虚しさが色濃く残り、風化した場
所である。
lines.english: A weathered place still deeply stained by the emptiness of its former prosperity.

lines.japanese:
だが今を生きる青少年らに、まともな楽園など与
えらるはずもない。
lines.english: But no true paradise would ever be granted to the young people of today.

lines.japanese:
ユートピア幻想はとうに過去のものだ。
　崩壊し、残骸と化した。
lines.english: The dream of utopia belonged to the past. It had collapsed and become wreckage.

lines.japanese:
瓦礫の骸に、自分たちだけの小さな、不完全な安
息の地を求めるしかない。
lines.english: All they could do was seek a small, imperfect refuge of their own amid the carcass of the ruins.

lines.japanese:
それが現代という時代である。
　だが忍は満足していた。
　極限の楽園など知らない世代。
lines.english: Such was the modern age. But Shinobu was content. His was a generation that had never known any ultimate paradise.

lines.japanese:
高度成長の末に訪れた、灰色の長き停滞。
　停滞の中から生まれ出た彼らは、希望を体感する
ことなく育った。
lines.english: The long gray stagnation that followed the era of rapid economic growth. Born of that stagnation, they had grown up without ever experiencing hope.

lines.japanese:
明るい未来。
　結婚。出産。豊かな暮らし。
　幸せな家庭―――
lines.english: A bright future. Marriage. Childbirth. A prosperous life. A happy family—

lines.japanese:
言葉としては理解できるが、印象としては幻想神
話の類である。
lines.english: He understood what the words meant, but to him they had the texture of fantasy and myth.

lines.japanese: ゆえに忍にとって、工場の時間は最善のものである。
lines.english: And so, for Shinobu, time at the factory was the best thing there was.

lines.japanese:
使い古されてはいるが。
　天を見上げる。
　首の背が痛くなるほど。
lines.english: Hackneyed though that may sound. He looked up at the heavens until the back of his neck ached.

lines.japanese: 空は鮮やかさの密度を増し、目がチリチリと灼けた。
lines.english: The sky deepened into vivid color until its glare prickled at his eyes.

lines.japanese: どのような時間にも、終わりは来るとわかる。
lines.english: He knew that every span of time must come to an end.

lines.japanese: 来て、しまう―――
lines.english: The end would come all the same—

lines.japanese: 「寒くはない？」
lines.english: “Aren't you cold?”

lines.japanese: 「平気」
lines.english: “I'm fine.”

lines.japanese: 「上着、持ってきたわ」

lines.japanese:
「パンサー？　ああ、柄のこと……柄なんて。

lines.english: “Panther? Oh, the pattern… It's only a pattern. It looks warm.”

lines.japanese:
あたたかいであろう。
　夜遊び用なのだから。
　ためらわせるものは、その派手な柄にある。
lines.english: It would be warm. It was meant for nights on the town. The garish pattern was the source of Shinobu’s hesitation.

lines.japanese: 「……その、いろいろと違うから……」
lines.english: “…It's just… all wrong for me…”

lines.japanese: 「何が？」
lines.english: “Such as?”

lines.japanese: 「キャラとか」
lines.english: “My whole image, for one.”

lines.japanese:
小首をかしげた沙也加だが、結局強引にコートを
忍の肩にひっかけた。
lines.english: Sayaka tilted her head, then draped the coat over Shinobu's shoulders anyway, giving him no choice.

lines.japanese: 「ほら、袖を通さないと」
lines.english: “Here. Put your arms through.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ、大丈夫だから」
lines.english: “No, it's all right. I'm fine.”

lines.japanese: 強めに抵抗する。
lines.english: He put up firmer resistance.

lines.japanese: 「困るわ」
lines.english: “That won't do.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、困るっていわれても……困るよ……」
lines.english: “You say that won't do, but… this really won't do…”

lines.japanese: 「風邪をこじらせてもらっては困るわ」
lines.english: “I can’t have you coming down with a bad cold.”

lines.japanese:
こめられた力が強くなってきた。

lines.english: Her grip tightened. She was plainly determined to get him into it.

lines.japanese: 「ほら」
lines.english: “Come on.”

lines.japanese: 「わかったよう」
lines.english: “All right, all right.”

lines.japanese:
渋々、その大きすぎるコートを着込む。
　袖があまる。
　裾が中途半端に膝を隠す。
lines.english: Reluctantly, he put on the enormous coat. The sleeves hung past his hands. The hem came down awkwardly over his knees.

lines.japanese:
肩幅があってない。
　全体的にもっさりしている。
　撫で肩だ。
lines.english: The shoulders were too broad for him. The whole thing hung shapelessly around him. His shoulders sloped.

lines.japanese:
ヒョウ柄だ。
　コロン臭い。コートに直接ふっているようだ。
lines.english: It was leopard print. It stank of cologne. Shouji seemed to spray the stuff directly onto the coat.

lines.japanese: 「似合うわ。忍はなんでも似合うのね」
lines.english: “It suits you. Everything suits you, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: （どうしてそんなこと言えるんだろう……）
lines.english: (How can she possibly say that…?)

lines.japanese:
年の割に老成した沙也加は、価値観もまた若者離
れしていて、外見にはこだわらない。
lines.english: Mature beyond her years, Sayaka also had values unlike those of other young people and was unconcerned with appearances.

lines.japanese:
それは『どうでも良い』ということでもある。

lines.english: That was another way of saying that she simply did not care. Yet Sayaka herself must truly have believed it suited him.

lines.japanese: 世俗に染まらず育つとは、こういうことだ。
lines.english: This, apparently, was what it meant to grow up untainted by the world.

lines.japanese: （……ダメだ……説得不可能）
lines.english: (…No… it's hopeless. She can't be persuaded.)

lines.japanese:
してみれば忍は、沙也加よりは少し感覚が若いと
いうことになる。
lines.english: By that measure, Shinobu possessed somewhat younger sensibilities than Sayaka.

lines.japanese:
幸か不幸か。
　この苦難から脱出するには、速やかなる帰宅以外
にない。
lines.english: For better or worse. His only way out of this ordeal was to get home as quickly as possible.

lines.japanese: 「確かに……あたたかいね」
lines.english: “It is… warm, I'll give you that.”

lines.japanese: 「そうでしょう」
lines.english: “You see?”

lines.japanese: 「でも」
lines.english: “But—”

lines.japanese:
「ああ、じゃあ着て帰りなさい。章二には私から言
　っておくから」
lines.english: “Oh, then wear it home. I'll tell Shouji myself.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと待って、くださいませんか？」
lines.english: “Could you please wait just one moment?”

lines.japanese: 声が裏返りかけた。
lines.english: His voice nearly cracked.
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「……着て帰るの？　これを？」
lines.english: “…Wear it home? In this?”

lines.japanese: 「そうよ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「き、着て帰ったら、章二がきっと困るよう」
lines.english: “B-but if I wear it home, it'll be a problem for Shouji, I'm sure.”

lines.japanese: 沙也加は携帯を取り出す。
lines.english: Sayaka took out her phone.

lines.japanese: 「もしもし、私よ。工場にあるコートを借りたいの」
lines.english: “Hello, it's me. I'd like to borrow the coat at the factory.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、忍が寒がっていたから」
lines.english: “Yes. Shinobu was cold.”

lines.japanese: （さむがってない……）
lines.english: (I wasn't cold…)

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ借りるわね」
lines.english: “Then we'll borrow it.”

lines.japanese: 電話をしまう。
lines.english: She put away the phone.

lines.japanese: 「いいって言っていたわ」
lines.english: “He said it was fine.”
“…I see.”

lines.japanese: 「今日は誰も来ないみたいね。一緒に帰りましょう」
lines.english: “It doesn't look as though anyone else is coming today. Let's go home together.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうね」
lines.english: “…All right.”

lines.japanese: そして二人は、並んで帰った。
lines.english: And so the two walked home side by side.

lines.japanese:
忍の服装は市街地では極めて目立ったが、沙也加
はいっこうに気にする様子もなかった。
lines.english: Shinobu's outfit made him painfully conspicuous on the streets, but Sayaka showed no sign of caring.

lines.japanese: 別れた瞬間、即刻脱いだものだ。
lines.english: The instant they parted, he tore it off.

lines.japanese: 「ただいま」
lines.english: “I'm home.”

lines.japanese:
帰宅は夜になった。
　キッチンから焦げた匂いがする。
lines.english: It was night by the time he got home. Something smelled burnt in the kitchen.
“What… is this?”

lines.japanese: 惨状であった。
lines.english: The kitchen was a disaster.

lines.japanese:
切断されうち捨てられた野菜、割れた食器、焼け
こげて原形をとどめていない動物性蛋白質（と思わ
れるもの）、べっとりとこびりついた油……。
lines.english: Vegetables hacked apart and abandoned. Shattered dishes. Some kind of animal protein—or what looked like it—burned past all recognition. Grease clinging everywhere in a sticky film…

lines.japanese:
料理という名の破壊活動。その痕跡。
　忍はげんなりした。
　キッチンはエレガントに使うもの。
lines.english: The wreckage left by that destructive enterprise known as cooking. Shinobu's spirits sank. A kitchen was meant to be used with elegance.

lines.japanese:
包丁は投げ出してはいけない。
　割れた食器はすぐ片づける。
　切った野菜はよりわける。床に落としたりしない。
lines.english: Knives should not be left lying about. Broken dishes should be cleared away at once. Cut vegetables should be sorted, not dropped on the floor.

lines.japanese:
飛び散った油はかたまらないうちにぬぐう。
　一枚の雑巾を駆使して、キッチンを蘇生させていく。
lines.english: Spattered grease should be wiped up before it congeals. Armed with a single dishcloth, he brought the kitchen back to life.

lines.japanese: 「なんとか……」
lines.english: “That should… do it.”

lines.japanese:
返す手で、鍋に火をかけ油をなじませる。
　たまねぎを刻む。
　熱した油に、それを落とし込んだ。
lines.english: Without pausing, he heated a pot and coated it with oil. He chopped an onion. Then dropped it into the hot oil.

lines.japanese:
さきほどよりわけた野菜を、適当に刻んで放り込
んでいく。
lines.english: He gave the vegetables he'd sorted out a rough chop and tossed them in.

lines.japanese:
牛肉も入れる。
　炒める。
　薄力粉を入れて、なじませる。
lines.english: In went the beef. He browned it. Then added flour and stirred it through.

lines.japanese:
香草を束にして放り込む。
　その他いろいろ、味付け。
　水を注ぐ。
lines.english: He tied the herbs into a bundle and tossed them in. Seasoned it with this and that. Poured in water.

lines.japanese:
沸騰すると、アクが出てくる。
　ひたすらアクを取る。
　塩こしょうで軽く味付けをする。
lines.english: As it came to a boil, scum rose to the surface. He skimmed and skimmed. Then seasoned it lightly with salt and pepper.

lines.japanese: 「ふう」
lines.english: “Whew.”

lines.japanese:
被害は最小限になった。
　ついでにライスの用意もしておこうと、米をとぐ。
　ジャーに放り込んで自動炊飯にセット。
lines.english: The damage had been kept to a minimum. While he was at it, he rinsed some rice for later. He tossed it into the rice cooker and set it to cook.
“Shinobu?”

lines.japanese: バスタオルを巻いただけの千鳥が出てくる。
lines.english: Chidori emerged wearing nothing but a bath towel.

lines.japanese: 「ただいま」
lines.english: “I'm home.”

lines.japanese: 「おかえりなさい」
lines.english: “Welcome home.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、掃除してくれたんですね……ごめんなさい、
　ちょっと思うところがあって。
　あとで掃除しようと思っていたんですが」
lines.english: “Oh, you cleaned up… I’m sorry. I had something on my mind. I meant to clean up later.”

lines.japanese: 「シチュー、作っておいたので。よかったら」
lines.english: “I made some stew, if you'd like any.”

lines.japanese: 「あとでいただきます」
lines.english: “I'll have some later.”

lines.japanese: 「今日は、何か特別なことは？」
lines.english: “Did anything unusual happen today?”

lines.japanese: 「特に、何も」
lines.english: “No. Nothing in particular.”
“I see…”

lines.japanese: 「シャワー、入ります」
lines.english: “I'm going to take a shower.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese:
千鳥は自宅では、そう話す方ではない。
　忍もそうだ。
　会話は少ない。
lines.english: At home, Chidori was not one for conversation. Neither was Shinobu. They said little to each other.

lines.japanese:
広い家に、いるのは姉と弟のみ。
　貴宮家の食卓は、いつも静かである。
lines.english: Only a sister and brother lived in that large house. The Atemiya dinner table was always quiet.

lines.japanese:
シャワーの後、夕食を済ませ、自室に。
　何もない部屋だ。
　必要なものしかない。
lines.english: After his shower and dinner, he went to his room. It was a bare room. It held only the necessities.

lines.japanese:
学校の準備を済ませると、いきなりすることがな
くなる。
lines.english: Once he had finished getting ready for school, he suddenly had nothing left to do.

lines.japanese:
身体が気怠さに包まれている。
　時計を確認すると、まだ十時だ。
lines.english: His whole body felt listless. He checked the clock. It was only ten.
“Yaaawn…”

lines.japanese: あくび。
lines.english: A yawn.

lines.japanese:
集中力が落ちているらしい。
　忍は寝台に潜り込んだ。
　小学生並の早寝だ。
lines.english: His concentration seemed to be slipping. Shinobu crawled into bed. The bedtime of a grade-schooler.

lines.japanese: 「だって、疲れてる……」
lines.english: “I'm tired, that's all…”

lines.japanese:
自分でも思ったのか、そんないいわけを呟いて……
すぐに寝息を立てはじめた。
lines.english: As though he felt the need to justify himself, he muttered the excuse… and almost immediately began breathing softly in his sleep.

lines.japanese: こうして忍の一日は終わる。
lines.english: And so Shinobu's day came to an end.

lines.japanese: 「……秘密基地？」
lines.english: “…A secret base?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、基地」
lines.english: “Yeah, a base.”

lines.japanese: 表情を輝かせるあずさを、忍は無感情に眺めた。
lines.english: Without emotion, Shinobu watched Azusa’s face light up.

lines.japanese: 「それは、どんな？」
lines.english: “What kind?”

lines.japanese:
「すごくひろいの。大人とかいないし。
　なんかもう使われてないみたいなの」
lines.english: “It's really big, and there aren't any grown-ups. I don't think anybody uses it anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「建物？」
lines.english: “A building?”

lines.japanese: 「うん！」
lines.english: “Yeah!”

lines.japanese: 考え込む。
lines.english: He thought it over.

lines.japanese: 「そのこと、他の誰かに言った？」
lines.english: “Have you told anyone else about it?”

lines.japanese: 「いってないよ。忍くんにだけ」
lines.english: “No. Only you, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「そう」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「案内、してもらえるかな」
lines.english: “Could you take me there?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、行こう！」
lines.english: “Sure! Let's go!”

lines.japanese:
あずさは忍を引いて、寂れた道を歩く。
　郊外に位置する、ちょっとした工場地域に入る。
lines.english: Azusa pulled Shinobu along the deserted road. They entered a small industrial district on the outskirts of town.

lines.japanese: かつては賑わっていたその辺りに、今は人影もない。
lines.english: The area had once bustled with life. Now not a soul was in sight.

lines.japanese:
「いっぱいあるけど、ほとんどカギがかかってて入れ
　ないんだ。けど一つだけ、あいてるのがあってね」
lines.english: “There are lots of them, but most are locked, so you can't get inside. But there's one that's open.”

lines.japanese:
忍は応じない。
　あずさが一方的に話している。
lines.english: Shinobu gave no response. Azusa was doing all the talking.

lines.japanese:
無視されているという意識はないのか、楽しげに
言葉を継ぐ。
lines.english: Perhaps she did not realize she was being ignored. She kept talking happily.

lines.japanese: 「ほら、ここだよ」

lines.japanese: 「……そうか」
lines.english: “…I see.”

lines.japanese: だが忍は安堵の表情を浮かべる。

手招くあずさは、もう半身を建物に滑りこませて

lines.japanese: 「なるほど、基地だ」

lines.japanese: 「秘密基地……か」
lines.english: “A secret base…”

lines.japanese:
遊び、話し、交換し、隠す。

子供なのだから。

lines.japanese: 今日はあずさがいた。

夢中になって目線を走らせていた書物から、ふと

lines.japanese:
工場というこの空間はあまりにも自然すぎた。
　個室は心の一部であると言われる。
　他者のいない場所は、特にその傾向が強まる。
lines.english: This space they called the factory felt almost too natural. A private room is said to be part of the mind. A place without others takes on that quality all the more.

lines.japanese:
心から漏れた様々なものが、部屋の有り様を選択
的に定めていく。
lines.english: The things that leak from the mind selectively shape the room.

lines.japanese:
長い時間をかけて、やがては繭のように居心地の
良い空間。
lines.english: Over time, it becomes a space as comfortable as a cocoon.

lines.japanese: 忍にとっては工場がそうである。
lines.english: For Shinobu, the factory was such a place.

lines.japanese:
この心的空間がいわゆる個室とは異なるのは、異
物であるはずの他者の存在もまた安息の構成要素で
あるところだ。
lines.english: What set this mental space apart from an ordinary private room was that even other people—who by rights should have felt like intrusions— were part of what made it restful.

lines.japanese:
気が付けば人がいる。
　気が付けば人がいなくなっている。
lines.english: He would look up and find someone there. He would look again and find them gone.

lines.japanese:
そのたび寂しさと嬉しさの狭間に揺れる様が、ゆ
りかごを思わせた。
lines.english: Each time, he swayed between loneliness and joy, as though in a cradle.

lines.japanese:
今、空間内にはあずさと忍しかいない。

lines.english: Now only Azusa and Shinobu occupied that space. Though he felt as if Sayaka had been there only moments ago—

lines.japanese:
静かだった。
　静寂は人の存在を浮き彫りにする。
lines.english: It was quiet. Silence threw the presence of another person into relief.

lines.japanese: あずさはソファに座って、膝の上に本を広げていた。

lines.japanese:
本棚の蔵書らしい。

少女に向けた。
lines.english: It appeared to have come from the shelves. Shinobu looked at the slight girl as though dazzled.

lines.japanese:
望郷の念を錯覚する。

　育った部屋の印象だけを記憶しているに過ぎない。
lines.english: He mistook the feeling for homesickness. Shinobu had no memories of a hometown. All he remembered was the impression left by the room in which he had grown up.

lines.japanese:
そんな忍にとって、色づいたふるさとの原景とは、
幼少時代そのものである。
lines.english: For Shinobu, then, the vivid image that stood for home was childhood itself.

lines.japanese:
例えば……あずさである。
　彼女とは長い時間、ともに過ごした。
lines.english: Azusa, for instance. He had spent a great deal of time with her.

lines.japanese: ついこの間まで、少女のつま先は床に届かなかった。
lines.english: Until just recently, the girl’s toes had not reached the floor.

lines.japanese: ……ように思う。

lines.japanese:
ぶらぶらと、中空をかくように振っていた。
　昨日のことのように思い返せる。

lines.japanese: （あずさ……大きくなっているんだ）

lines.japanese: （あのいさましいちびのあずさがなぁ……）
lines.english: (That brave little Azusa…)

lines.japanese: 感慨深い。
lines.english: He was deeply moved.

lines.japanese:
人間である以上、成長は当然のことである。
　そんな単純な事実を、忍は忘れていたようだ。
　あずさが成長してしまう。
lines.english: Human beings grew. It was only natural. Shinobu seemed to have forgotten so simple a fact. Azusa was going to grow up.

lines.japanese: カルチャーショックであった。
lines.english: It came as a culture shock.

lines.japanese:
もやもやと、考えてみる。
　２７歳になった色っぽい紅緒あずさ。
lines.english: He tried, uneasily, to picture it. Azusa Benio at twenty-seven, all grown up and alluring.
“Urgh…”

lines.japanese:
ただただ震えた。
　とても恐ろしい可能性だ。
lines.english: He could only shudder. The possibility was terrifying.

lines.japanese: 変化は破滅であり、旧来の概念を突き崩してしまう。
lines.english: Change meant ruin. It demolished every familiar idea.

lines.japanese: （そもそもあずさの２７歳ってのが有り得ない……）
lines.english: (Azusa being twenty-seven doesn’t even seem possible…)

lines.japanese:
可愛いばかりの我が子が、大人へと成長していく
のを見る、親の気持ちに近いかも知れない。
lines.english: Perhaps this was how a parent felt, watching a child who had once been nothing but adorable grow into an adult.

lines.japanese:
そっと踵を地面につけ、合わせた膝を傾けて、読
書するあずさが大人びて見える。
lines.english: Her heels rested lightly on the floor, her knees pressed together and angled to one side. Sitting there reading, Azusa looked mature.

lines.japanese:
微量の少女性が、そこには備わり始めている。
　寂しく、嬉しく、むずがゆい。
lines.english: The faintest trace of femininity was beginning to emerge in her. It left him lonely, happy, and oddly self-conscious all at once.

lines.japanese:
しかし顔をあげれば、昔と変わらぬアーモンド型
の瞳が愛らしく光る。
lines.english: But when she looked up, the almond-shaped eyes he remembered sparkled as adorably as ever.

lines.japanese:
そんな目を見ると安心する。
　やはり大粒の宝石が、どうしても幼く映るためで
ある。
lines.english: The sight reassured him. Those great jewel-like eyes still made her look unmistakably like a child.

lines.japanese: 「いいや……」
lines.english: “No…”

lines.japanese:
あずさはひょいと本を持ち上げて、忍に掲げて見
せた。
lines.english: Azusa deftly lifted the book and held it up for Shinobu to see.

なかなか明確な記憶は浮き出てこない。

嫌いではなかったものが、様々な体験によって反

lines.japanese:
交友が忍に新たな価値観を与えた。

だからそれまで無価値と断定していたものが、最

lines.japanese: 一連の心変わりを、宿主に意識させずに。

忍には仲間がいる。

lines.english: Shinobu had friends. Friends who mattered to him.

　ら」

と自分はホウキを手に取り、散乱した珈琲豆を掃

lines.japanese: 「このまま、まいとこうか？」
lines.english: “Should we just spread it around?”

lines.japanese: 二つの無邪気な笑みが、合わせ鏡に向かいあった。

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、ばばばーと」
lines.english: “Then—swish, swish, swish!”

lines.japanese:
ホウキの先でかき回す。

lines.english: She stirred it about with the tip of the broom. Sand and powder mingled into a mottled reddish-brown pattern.

lines.english: “I was just thinking you seemed more grown-up somehow.”

ぱたぱたと手を振る姿は、忍のよく知るあずさと

しかし家に一人でいても、切り離されたようで不

lines.japanese:
いつ崩れ去るとも知れない。

lines.english: It could crumble away at any time. What hope could there be for the young people alive today?

lines.japanese:
高度成長期と呼ばれた時代、未来は輝いていたの

lines.english: In the era of rapid economic growth, the future must have shone brightly.

lines.japanese:
疑う余地もなかったろう。

　どれほどの希望が残されていると言えるだろう。
lines.english: No one could have doubted it. But what had become of that promised future, now that the twenty-first century was here? How much hope could anyone claim was left?

lines.japanese:
年月が進むごとに、科学や数学などの物理が、夢

lines.english: With every passing year, the hard facts of science and mathematics brought the end of the dream into sharper relief.

lines.japanese:
経済的繁栄はあったが、それは平地が少ない島国

った。
lines.english: Economic prosperity had come, but it was no more than a mirage—one that made a grotesque idol of the unspoiled land in an island nation with little level ground.

lines.japanese: 決定的な破局もなしに、ユートピア幻想は霧散した。
lines.english: The utopian fantasy dissolved without any decisive catastrophe.

lines.japanese:
最初からそんなものありはしなかったのかも知れ

lines.japanese:
そして無気力の時代に、若者たちは生まれた。

lines.english: The young were born into an age of apathy. Their only forms of rebellion were indulgence and escape.

lines.japanese:

に生きることが見えてくる。
lines.english: Only as they grew older did a third choice finally come into view— living in the real world.

lines.japanese:

lines.japanese: 「うーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「掘り出し物でも売ってるかもよ？」
lines.english: “They might have a bargain or something.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、行こうか」
lines.english: “All right, let's go.”

lines.japanese: 「いこういこう」
lines.english: “Let's go, let's go.”

lines.japanese:
引っ張る力が強くなる。
　小さな機関車に牽引される。
lines.english: The pull on his hand grew stronger. He was being towed by a tiny locomotive.

lines.japanese:
はたから見たら、どういった関係に映るのだろう
か、と考えてしまう。
lines.english: He found himself wondering what their relationship must look like to anyone watching.

lines.japanese:
遠慮のない接触を繰り返す二人だ。
　兄妹か、恋人か。
　そんなところであろう。
lines.english: They were forever touching without the least reserve. Brother and sister, perhaps, or lovers. Something of the sort.

lines.japanese: 「でもおいもは飽きたんじゃー」
lines.english: “But I'm tiiired of sweet potatoes.”

lines.japanese: 「おいもうまし」
lines.english: “Sweet potatoes: delicious.”

lines.japanese:
「しかし最近のおやつは、おいもばかり。これは良
　くない」
lines.english: “But all our snacks lately are sweet potatoes. That is not good.”

lines.japanese: 「栄養満点なのに」
lines.english: “They're packed with nutrients.”

lines.japanese: 「パイにするとかさ、いろいろあると思う工夫」
lines.english: “We could make pies or something. There's gotta be other stuff we can do with them.”

lines.japanese: 「……コストですかね、やっぱり問題は」
lines.english: “…I suppose the problem is cost.”

lines.japanese: 「手間かけると高くなるんだよ」
lines.english: “Anything that takes work costs more.”

lines.japanese:
「むむ、ひたすらいもを食すしかないという
　ことかー」
lines.english: “Hmm. So we’ve got no choice but to keep eating sweet potatoes?”

lines.japanese: 「ネットゲームのようにね」
lines.english: “Like in an online game.”

lines.japanese: 「うは、９９個ショートカット食い」
lines.english: “Whoa, ninety-nine of 'em on a hotkey.”

lines.japanese: 「古典だなぁ」
lines.english: “That's old-school.”

lines.japanese: 「パッケージ版しかやったことないんだよ」
lines.english: “I've only ever played the boxed version.”

lines.japanese: 「こっちもローカル・セッションしかない」
lines.english: “I’ve only played local sessions, too.”

hyperlinks.preview: Network RPGs enjoyed a spectacular boom for a time, but a great many titles folded once they became
