lines.japanese: 「またやらして」
lines.english: “Let me play again sometime.”

lines.japanese: 「いいとも」
lines.english: “Sure thing.”

lines.japanese: 「すとらての方がおもろいと思うんだけどね」
lines.english: “I think stratty games are more fun, though.”

hyperlinks.preview: Azusa's own shorthand for “real strategy game.” She does not understand what the words mean; it is m

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: Azusa's own shorthand for “real strategy game.” She does not understand what the words mean; it is m

lines.japanese: 「……携帯すとらて操作おっつかなくて死ねる」
lines.english: “…I can’t keep up with the controls in mobile stratty games. I just die.”

lines.japanese: 「感情のおもむくままに遊ぶんだよ」
lines.english: “You just play however you feel like playing.”

lines.japanese: 「性格出るなー」
lines.english: “Really brings out your personality.”

lines.japanese: 「あい？」
lines.english: “Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでもないよ」
lines.english: “It's nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、おなかへったねぇ。おやつ不足だ」
lines.english: “Aah, I'm hungry. We're critically short on snacks.”

lines.japanese: 「たまにはビフテキ喰いたい」
lines.english: “I want a steak for a change.”

lines.japanese: 「おやつじゃない……」
lines.english: “That's not a snack…”

lines.japanese: 「じゃがいも食べたくない？」
lines.english: “Don't you want some potatoes?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、いいね」
lines.english: “Oh, that sounds good.”

lines.japanese: 「ふかしたやつ」
lines.english: “Steamed ones.”

lines.japanese: 「……工場でもできるかな？」
lines.english: “…Could we make them at the factory?”

lines.japanese: 「おお、それだ」
lines.english: “Ooh, that's it!”

lines.japanese: 手を打つ。
lines.english: She clapped her hands.

lines.japanese: 「今度見つけたら買い込んでおくね」
lines.english: “Next time I find some, I'll stock up.”

lines.japanese: 「そうしよう」
lines.english: “Let's do that.”

lines.japanese: 「そうしようそうしよう」
lines.english: “Let's do that, let's do that.”

lines.japanese:
口約束に気を良くしたあずさは、追従するように
頷いた。
lines.english: Pleased by the promise, Azusa nodded eagerly in agreement.

lines.japanese: 繋いだ手を前後に振りつつ歩く。
lines.english: They walked on, swinging their joined hands back and forth.

lines.japanese:
ヒョウ柄のコートのせいで、とても間抜けなの
だろうが、忍の視点からは甘酸っぱい光景しか見
えない。
lines.english: The leopard-print coat must have made the whole thing look utterly ridiculous, but from Shinobu's perspective all he could see was a tender, bittersweet scene.

lines.japanese: 「―――したらねー」
lines.english: “—And then, you know—”

lines.japanese:
無邪気に話す。
　いつもの一場面。
lines.english: She chattered innocently. A familiar scene.

lines.japanese:
今でこそ自然になった二人の関係も、最初の頃は
ちぐはぐだった。
lines.english: Natural though their relationship seemed now, it had been awkward in the beginning.

lines.japanese: ケンカなし、いじめなし―――
lines.english: No fights, no bullying—

lines.japanese:
今の平和を大切に思っているということ。
　そして、
lines.english: The words meant that she cherished the peace they had now. And also—

lines.japanese:
……かつてあずさの上に、それらが置かれていた
ことを示しもする。
lines.english: …that once, those things had been visited upon Azusa.

lines.japanese: あずさとの出会いについて考えれば今も心が痛む。
lines.english: It still pained him to think about meeting Azusa.

hyperlinks.preview: This happened when Shinobu first began going to school.

alternatives.preview: On his way home from school, Shinobu heard a scream. An urgent scream.

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: This happened when Shinobu first began going to school.

alternatives.preview: On his way home from school, Shinobu heard a scream. An urgent scream.

lines.japanese:
何よりつらいのは、当時、まだ忍自身が心の痛み
を実感するほど成熟していなかったことである。
lines.english: What hurt most was that, back then, Shinobu himself had not yet been mature enough to truly feel that pain.

lines.japanese:
幼かった。
　言い訳としては、充分正当な理由となる。
　自分は悪くはない。
lines.english: He had been young. It was excuse enough—perfectly legitimate. He was not to blame.

lines.japanese:
客観的にはそう判断できる。
　だとしても……結果辱められたあずさにジャージ
を渡そうとしたことさえ、どこか空々しく思える。
lines.english: Objectively, that was a fair conclusion. Even so… even his offer of a tracksuit to Azusa after her humiliation now seemed somehow hollow.

lines.japanese:
あの時、彼女に言ったように……もっとうまくや
れなかったのかと悔いる。
lines.english: Just as he’d said to her then… he wished he’d handled it better.

lines.japanese:
魂のこもらない冷たい助け手。
　傷ついた少女には、そんなものこそ憎たらしい存
在だったはずだ。
lines.english: A cold helping hand without a soul behind it. To a wounded girl, surely nothing could have been more hateful.

lines.japanese:
今ならわかることが、当時は霧の向こうの概念で
ある。
lines.english: What he understood now had still been hidden from him then, a concept somewhere beyond the mist.

lines.japanese:
取り返しのつかない過去を後悔するほど、あずさ
に思い入れてしまった。
lines.english: He had grown so attached to Azusa that he now regretted a past beyond repair.

lines.japanese: 「……忍くん、もしかしてまた頭痛発生中？」
lines.english: “…Shinobu, is another headache currently in progress?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　そんなことないよ」
lines.english: “Hm? No, I'm fine.”

lines.japanese: あずさが背伸びをして、顔をのぞきこんできていた。
lines.english: Azusa had risen onto her toes to peer into his face.

lines.japanese:
距離五センチ。
　表には出ていないが、少し驚いた。
lines.english: Five centimeters away. It did not show on his face, but she startled him a little.

lines.japanese:
大きな瞳が生きた宝石のようで……そこだけは彼
女のちんまりとした印象を逸脱し、強烈な存在感を
放つ。
lines.english: Her enormous eyes were like living jewels… They alone broke free of the otherwise diminutive impression she gave and blazed with overwhelming presence.

lines.japanese: 「昔のこと思い出してた」
lines.english: “I was remembering the old days.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅん、どんくらい昔？」
lines.english: “Huh. How far back?”

lines.japanese: 「はじめて会った頃だよ」
lines.english: “When we first met.”

lines.japanese: 「うわぁ……」
lines.english: “Oh, wow…”

lines.japanese: 照れ笑いを浮かべる。
lines.english: She gave an embarrassed smile.

lines.japanese: 「そりゃまた恥ずかしいところを……んー」
lines.english: “That's a pretty embarrassing part to remember… Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「勝手に思い出してもらっちゃ困るよー、キミー」
lines.english: “You can't just go remembering things without my permission, mister.”

lines.japanese: 「すいません」
lines.english: “My apologies.”

lines.japanese:
「次からは、もっと仲良くなってからの時代にする
　ように」
lines.english: “Next time, pick a time after we'd gotten to know each other better.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、そうしますボス」
lines.english: “Yes, boss. I'll do that.”

lines.japanese: 「うむうむ」
lines.english: “Good, good.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ特別にドロップあげる」
lines.english: “Then, as a special treat, I’ll give you a candy drop.”

lines.japanese:
あずさはそれを、ポケットからじかに、ワイルド
さ満点に取り出した。
lines.english: Azusa pulled it straight from her pocket with magnificent lack of ceremony.

lines.japanese:
包み紙などという気の利いたものはない。
　生である。
lines.english: No thoughtful little wrapper for this. It was bare.

lines.japanese:
拾ったコインとかバッタ等が突っ込まれ時には潰
れてきた、夢いっぱいのポケットだ。
lines.english: It was a pocket full of dreams, where found coins, grasshoppers, and other treasures had been shoved and sometimes crushed.

lines.japanese: 三粒のドロップを忍に渡す。
lines.english: She handed Shinobu three drops.

lines.japanese:
「せっかく貯めたのに、なんか食べ過ぎるとマズイ
　らしくてさ。食べちゃって」
lines.english: “I worked so hard saving them, but apparently eating too many is bad for you. So you eat them.”

lines.japanese: 「なつかしいなー、これ」
lines.english: “These take me back.”

lines.japanese: 「昔からあるんだ？」
lines.english: “They've been around that long?”

lines.japanese: 「すごく昔からあると思うよ」
lines.english: “For a very long time, I think.”

lines.japanese:
「子供の頃、食事についてきたよ。一日二粒だった
　かな」
lines.english: “We got them with our meals when I was little. Two a day, I think.”

lines.japanese: 「うちのトコ一粒だよ」
lines.english: “We only get one.”

lines.japanese: 「給食についてくるんだ？」
lines.english: “It comes with your school lunch?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yep.”

lines.japanese: 「……食べ過ぎるといけないのは確かだね」
lines.english: “…True enough, eating too many can't be good for you.”
“Are they poison?”

lines.japanese: 「栄養が強くて、過剰症があるんだってさ」
lines.english: “They’re packed with nutrients. Too many can make you sick, apparently.”

lines.japanese: 「だから一気に食べると健康を損なう可能性が」
lines.english: “So eating a lot at once can damage your health.”

lines.japanese: 「こわ。もう食べぬ。捨てるようにする」
lines.english: “Scary. I shall eat no more. I'll throw them away.”

lines.japanese: 「こらこら……一粒なら栄養だよ。というか薬？」
lines.english: “Now, now… One gives you nutrients. Or is it medicine?”

lines.japanese: 忍はそれでもドロップを二粒、もちもちと食べた。
lines.english: Shinobu nevertheless munched his way through two of the drops.

lines.japanese: 「ところでこれ、どうして三粒もあったの？」
lines.english: “Incidentally, why did you have three of them?”
“Hmm…?”

lines.japanese: 「余り？」
lines.english: “Were they extras?”

lines.japanese: 「いんにゃ。貯金して……」
lines.english: “Nope. I was saving them…”

lines.japanese: 「食べないでとっといたんだ？」
lines.english: “You kept them instead of eating them?”

lines.japanese: 「うん……まずいかなぁ……？」
lines.english: “Yeah… Is that bad…?”

lines.japanese: 「……給食の補助なんでしょ？　栄養失調になるよ」
lines.english: “…They’re meant to supplement your school lunch, aren’t they? You’ll end up malnourished.”

lines.japanese: 「平気っぽいよ」
lines.english: “I feel fine.”

lines.japanese: 忍は呆れた。
lines.english: Shinobu was dumbfounded.

lines.japanese: 「そりゃ二日三日くらいなら……お口あけて」
lines.english: “Well, for two or three days, perhaps… Open wide.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、せっかく忍くんにあげようと貯めたのにー」
lines.english: “But I saved them especially to give to youuu.”

lines.japanese: 「気持ちだけもらっとくから」
lines.english: “It's the thought that counts.”

lines.japanese:
すでに二粒ほどもちもちしておいて、気持ちだけ
というのも何だが。
lines.english: It was a little late to say he'd accept only the thought after he'd already munched two.

lines.japanese: 「はい、あーん」
lines.english: “Now, say ahh.”
“…Ahh.”

lines.japanese: 口に最後の一粒を落とした。
lines.english: He dropped the last one into her mouth.

lines.japanese: 「甘いー」
lines.english: “Sweeeet.”

lines.japanese: 「明日の活力の味だ」
lines.english: “The taste of tomorrow's vitality.”

lines.japanese: 「ほっぺしびれます」
lines.english: “My cheeks are tingling.”

lines.japanese: 「……でもさ」
lines.english: “…But you know.”

lines.japanese: 小さく忍は吹いた。
lines.english: Shinobu gave a quiet snort of laughter.

lines.japanese: 「どこも同じようなことしてるんだね」
lines.english: “People everywhere do the same sort of thing, don't they?”

lines.japanese:
「僕らも貯金してたよ、これで。あずさのとはちょ
　っと規模違ったけど」
lines.english: “We saved these too—on a slightly larger scale than you did.”

lines.japanese: 「はあう？」
lines.english: “Huh-wha?”

lines.japanese:
意味がわからない顔。
　幼い頃のあずさそのままで、保護者としては安心
してしまう。
lines.english: Her face said she had no idea what he meant. She looked just like the Azusa of early childhood, and the guardian in him could not help feeling reassured.

lines.japanese: 「二粒のうち、一つは健康のため自分で食べる」
lines.english: “Of the two drops, you'd eat one yourself for your health.”

lines.japanese: 「ふむふむ」
lines.english: “Mm-hmm, mm-hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「で、一つを貯金に回す」
lines.english: “And put the other into savings.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、計画的運用ってやつだ！」
lines.english: “Oh, that's what they call planned investment!”

lines.japanese: 「その通り」
lines.english: “Precisely.”

lines.japanese: 「で、いざという時、ドロップを通貨として支払う」
lines.english: “Then, when the need arose, you'd use the drops as currency.”

lines.japanese: 「……物々交換？」
lines.english: “…Bartering?”

lines.japanese:
「近いね。１ドロップの価値が……１０００円くら
　いかな？」
lines.english: “Something like that. One drop was worth… around 1,000 yen, I'd say.”

lines.japanese:
「甘いものに目がない年代だったからね。たとえば、
　絵のうまい人間に似顔絵を依頼して、１ドロップ
　……とかさ」
lines.english: “We were at an age when we couldn't get enough sweets. You might commission a portrait from somebody who could draw, for example, and pay them one drop… Something like that.”

lines.japanese: あずさの目が輝く。
lines.english: Azusa's eyes lit up.

lines.japanese: 「面白そう」
lines.english: “That sounds fun.”

lines.japanese:
「いろいろな係を一日分交替してもらうのに、
　５ドロップ……とかあったな」
lines.english: “Five drops to get someone to cover your duties for a day… That was another one.”

lines.japanese: 「高いね」
lines.english: “That's expensive.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、それで一日サボれたから」
lines.english: “Well, it bought you a day off.”

lines.japanese: 「でもね、もっと凄いのがあった」
lines.english: “But there was something even more incredible.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なに？」
lines.english: “W-what?”

lines.japanese: あずさはドキドキした。
lines.english: Azusa's heart raced.

lines.japanese: 「……一日外出権２０ドロップ」
lines.english: “…Twenty drops for a day pass.”

hyperlinks.preview: Two men.

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: Two men.

lines.japanese: 「高すぎるよ忍くん」
lines.english: “That's way too expensive, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「凄いんだよこれは」
lines.english: “This one was extraordinary.”

lines.japanese:
「係の交替とは違って、どういうルートを使ってか
　完全に外出自由になる。しかも一切お咎めはなし」
lines.english: “It wasn't like trading chores. I don't know what channels they used, but you would be completely free to go outside. And there'd be no punishment whatsoever.”

lines.japanese: 「施設なんだっけ？」
lines.english: “It was a facility, right?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。全寮制」
lines.english: “Yeah. Everyone lived on-site.”

lines.japanese:
「だから管理ってすごくうるさい。私用外出は禁止
　されてるんで、絶対に出られない。点呼だってあ
　るし、ルームメイトだっているし……」
lines.english: “So they were extremely strict about keeping track of us. Going out for personal reasons was forbidden, and there was no way to get out. They took roll call, and everyone had roommates…”

lines.japanese:
「それに授業だって休むことになっちゃうから、ど
　うしたってバレる。寮だからさ、欠席には医師の
　許可が必要でさ」
lines.english: “You'd have to miss classes too, so they'd inevitably find out. Since we lived there, you needed a doctor's permission to be absent.”

lines.japanese:
「けどこの権利を買うと、それらが全て解決される
　んだ」
lines.english: “But when you bought this pass, all of those problems disappeared.”

lines.japanese: 「おー」
lines.english: “Ooh.”

lines.japanese:
「この権利を買うには、上級生に話をつけないとい
　けないんだけどね」
lines.english: “You did have to make arrangements with an older student to buy one, though.”

lines.japanese:
「きっと上級生たちが根回しをして、うまく取り計
　らっているんじゃないかって噂だったけど……
　結局、真相はわからずじまいだったね」
lines.english: “The rumor was that the older students pulled strings and arranged everything somehow… But I never did learn the truth.”

lines.japanese: 「すごいねー、おもしろそう」
lines.english: “Wow. That sounds like fun.”

lines.japanese:
「外に出ても子供だからさ。何ができるってんじゃ
　ないんだけど」
lines.english: “Of course, we were still children once we got outside. It wasn't as though there was much we could do.”

lines.japanese: 「……世界は、変わったろうね」
lines.english: “…Even so, the world must have looked different.”

lines.japanese:
空を見上げる。
　まだ空の青さに魅せられていた時代が、記憶の向
こうに透けた。
lines.english: He looked up at the sky. Beyond his memories, he glimpsed an age when the blue of the sky could still enchant him.

lines.japanese:
そう―――当時の忍の唯一の慰め。蒼。
　空と海にあった色。
lines.english: Yes—the only solace Shinobu had known then. Blue. The color of sky and sea.

lines.japanese:
「お金使いたかったら、それにも別個にドロップい
　るし」
lines.english: “And if you wanted to spend money, that took extra drops too.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ……いろいろかかるね」
lines.english: “Whoa… Everything had a price.”

lines.japanese: 「ね、その施設ってまだあるの？」
lines.english: “Hey, is that place still there?”

lines.japanese:
「もうないよ。それで僕は、千鳥姉さんのところに
　引き取られたんだ。あの人も、施設出身組だった
　から」
lines.english: “Not anymore. That's why my sister Chidori took me in. She had come out of the same facility.”

lines.japanese:
「そっか。ドロップ缶差し入れでもってったら、忍
　くん後輩の英雄になれるかなーと思ったんだけど
　……ムリそうだね」
lines.english: “Oh. I thought taking them a tin of drops might make you a hero to the younger kids… But I guess that won’t work.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは。あったとしても駄目なんだよ、それ」
lines.english: “Ha ha. Even if it were still there, that wouldn't work.”

lines.japanese: 「なして？」
lines.english: “How come?”

lines.japanese: 「偽札事件……いや、偽ドロップ事件」
lines.english: “The counterfeit-money incident… Or rather, the counterfeit-drop incident.”

lines.japanese:
「先の一日外出権を獲得したヤツの一人がね、外で
　それを買い求めて来たんだよ」
lines.english: “One of the kids who acquired the day pass I mentioned bought some outside.”

lines.japanese: 「その……缶入りのドロップをね」
lines.english: “A tin of drops, that is.”

lines.japanese: 「おおう」
lines.english: “Oho.”

lines.japanese:
「しかし、彼は知らなかったんだ。
　戻る時に施設内の経済を混乱させまいとする上級生
　による、ボディチェックがあることをね」
lines.english: “But there was something he didn't know. To prevent anyone from disrupting the facility's economy upon returning, the older students performed a body search.”

lines.japanese:
「当然、彼は缶を没収され、そして……以後、ドロ
　ップの経済利用を禁止されてしまったのさ」
lines.english: “Naturally, they confiscated his tin, and after that… he was banned from using drops for trade.”

lines.japanese: 「すごい！」
lines.english: “Amazing!”

lines.japanese:
「忍くんの幼年期には、世の中の汚いものがいっぱ
　い詰まってる！」
lines.english: “Your childhood is packed with all the ugly things in the world!”

lines.japanese: 感嘆の言葉だった。
lines.english: She spoke in pure admiration.

lines.japanese: 「…………喜んでいいのかどうか」
lines.english: “…I’m not sure I should be pleased about that.”

lines.japanese: とてもそうは聞こえなかったが。
lines.english: It certainly hadn’t sounded like a compliment.

lines.japanese:
「忍くんは、何かドロップ使った武勇伝とか
　ないの？」
lines.english: “Don't you have any stories of daring exploits you pulled off with drops?”

lines.japanese:
「え？
　いや……僕は何も……毎日二粒食べてました……」
lines.english: “What? No… I didn't do anything… I ate my two drops every day…”

lines.japanese: 「密造したとか」
lines.english: “Like making them in secret.”

lines.japanese: 「作れないって。子供だし」
lines.english: “You can't make them. We were kids.”

lines.japanese: 「デスゲーム主催してドロップ独占したとか」
lines.english: “Or hosting a death game and cornering the drop market.”

lines.japanese: 「どう見られているんだ僕は……」
lines.english: “What kind of person do you think I am…?”

lines.japanese: 「忍くんは、どう使ったのかなーって思って」
lines.english: “I was just wondering how you used yours.”

lines.japanese: 「いや。なんというか」
lines.english: “Well. The thing is…”

lines.japanese: 忍は顔をそむけた。
lines.english: Shinobu turned his face away.

lines.japanese:
「……友達、ひとりもいなかったから……
　全部食べきったよ……」
lines.english: “…I didn't have a single friend… so I ate every last one…”

lines.japanese: 「うおっ！？」
lines.english: “Whoa!?”

lines.japanese: 気まずい空気。
lines.english: An awkward silence.
“……I'm sorry…”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いいよ……」
lines.english: “No, it's all right…”

lines.japanese: いたたまれない。
lines.english: The awkwardness was unbearable.

lines.japanese: 「ま、まあ、今はあたしがいるじゃないですか！」
lines.english: “W-well, you've got me now, don't you!”

lines.japanese:
「そ、そうだね……
　もうロンリーじゃないんだよね！」
lines.english: “Y-yes, I do… I'm not lonely anymore!”

lines.japanese: 「全然ロンリーじゃないよ！」
lines.english: “Not lonely at all!”

lines.japanese: 「仲間っていいね」
lines.english: “Friends are wonderful.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよねー」
lines.english: “They sure are.”

lines.japanese: 「お店で安く売ってたらもっといいのにね！！」
lines.english: “They'd be even better if stores sold them cheap!!”
(…No, that’s not right……)

lines.japanese:
そんなことを話しながら、二人の足は商店街の舗
装された道を踏みしめていた。
lines.english: As they talked, their feet carried them down the paved road of the shopping district.

lines.japanese: 「……おー、テナント、ちょっと埋まってきたね」
lines.english: “…Ooh, a few more shops have moved in.”

lines.japanese: 「そお？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese:
「うん。こないだはあっこのオサレショーウィンドウ
　カラッポだったし」
lines.english: “Yeah. Last time, that stylin' display window over there was empty.”

lines.japanese: 「なんになったんだろ？　美容院か……」
lines.english: “Wonder what it is now? A beauty salon…?”

lines.japanese:
忍を見やって無邪気に言った。
　ようやく商店街らしい様相が、立ちこめてきた。
lines.english: She looked over at Shinobu and said it innocently. At last, the place was beginning to feel like a real shopping district.

lines.japanese:
ほんの一ヶ月前までは、まばらにしか開店してい
なかったのに。
lines.english: Only a month earlier, barely any shops had been open.

lines.japanese: 「人類の進歩はすごいぜ」
lines.english: “Human progress is amazing.”

lines.japanese: 「……デフレが関係あるのか？」
lines.english: “…Maybe it's something to do with deflation?”

lines.japanese: 「……ないと思うよ」
lines.english: “…I don't think so.”

lines.japanese: 人通りの少ない商店街は、どこか別世界めいていた。
lines.english: With so few people about, the shopping district felt like another world.

lines.japanese:
雑踏とは呼べない隙間をそぞろ歩き、やがて気の
向くままに適当な店に目星をつける。
lines.english: They meandered through the sparse foot traffic, then picked out a promising shop on a whim.

lines.japanese: 本屋だ。
lines.english: It was a bookstore.

lines.japanese: 「ここい？」
lines.english: “This place?”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ」
lines.english: “Sure.”

lines.japanese:
あずさは米国人サムライの活躍を描いた人気コミ
ック、忍は死のロングウォークという小説を手に取
った。
lines.english: Azusa picked up a popular comic about the exploits of an American samurai; Shinobu picked up the novel The Long Walk.

lines.japanese: 支払いを（幸いカードが使えた）済ませ、店を出る。
lines.english: They paid—fortunately, the shop accepted cards—and left.

lines.japanese: 「……ありがとー」
lines.english: “…Thanks.”

lines.japanese: 束ねた二冊を口元に当てて、照れくさげに口にする。
lines.english: She held the two books together against her mouth and spoke bashfully.

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。お駄賃」
lines.english: “Don't mention it. Consider it your reward.”

lines.japanese: 「……なんかしたっけ？」
lines.english: “…Did I do something?”

lines.japanese:
もじもじと、妙にいじらしい態度。
　いじりたくなった。
lines.english: She fidgeted, looking strangely endearing. It made him want to tease her.

lines.japanese: （章二の悪影響だな……）
lines.english: (Shouji has been a bad influence…)

lines.japanese: 心の中で正当化し、ことさらさらりと告げる。
lines.english: With that private justification, he said it as casually as he could.

lines.japanese: 「あずさ可愛いから、その分のお駄賃」
lines.english: “Your reward for being so cute.”

lines.japanese: 無反応になった。
lines.english: She became entirely unresponsive.

lines.japanese: 「行こうか」
lines.english: “Shall we go?”

lines.japanese:
無反応のままついてきた。
　ちなみに変色はしていた。
lines.english: Still unresponsive, she followed him. She had, incidentally, changed color.

lines.japanese:
そのことに関するいかなるフォローも、互いに行
うことはなかった。
lines.english: Neither of them made the slightest attempt to follow up on the matter.

lines.japanese: 忍は楽しんだ。
lines.english: Shinobu enjoyed himself.

lines.japanese: 十分くらいして、
lines.english: About ten minutes later,

lines.japanese: 「……あ、いもだ」
lines.english: “…Oh, potatoes.”

lines.japanese: 「ほんとだ」
lines.english: “You're right.”

lines.japanese:
軒先でふかし芋が売られている。
　ここ最近、保温機の中身は芋ブーム。
　芋の素晴らしさが認められたのである。
lines.english: Steamed sweet potatoes were being sold outside a shop. Lately, potatoes had taken over the warming cabinets. The magnificence of the potato had at last received its due.

lines.japanese: 「芋スメルが漂ってきますな」
lines.english: “The smell of potato is upon us.”

lines.japanese: 「スメル言わない」
lines.english: “Don't say ‘smell.’”

lines.japanese: 「おなかがすきますな」
lines.english: “It makes one hungry.”

lines.japanese:
もう赤くはなかった。
　忍は芋を二つ買う。
　大砲のようなサイズのを二つ。
lines.english: She was no longer red. Shinobu bought two potatoes. Two the size of cannons.

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Here.”

lines.japanese:
一本……いや、一門と言ってもいいくらいのシロ
モノだ。
lines.english: Each one was less a potato… than a whole piece of field artillery.

lines.japanese: 「わ、豪気ぃ！」
lines.english: “Whoa! Big spender!”

lines.japanese: と弾けかけた顔が、次には翳っていた。
lines.english: Her face nearly burst with joy, only to cloud over a moment later.

lines.japanese: 「これじゃ……お子様だね、あたし」
lines.english: “This makes me look… like a little kid.”

lines.japanese: 「どしたの突然？」
lines.english: “Where did that come from?”

lines.japanese: 「いや……なんでもないんだけどさ……」
lines.english: “Oh… It's nothing, really…”

lines.japanese: 「欲しそうな顔してたよ？」
lines.english: “You looked as though you wanted one.”

lines.japanese: 「だ～、この顔がこの顔がっ」
lines.english: “Gah! This face, this face!”

lines.japanese: 束ねた本でごつごつと自分の頭を叩く。
lines.english: She thumped herself on the head with the bundled books.

lines.japanese: 「いらないなら二本とも僕がもらおうか？」
lines.english: “If you don't want it, shall I eat both?”

lines.japanese:
顔を上げる。
　大切なことを話すような顔。
lines.english: She raised her face. She wore the look of someone about to say something important.

lines.japanese: 「いらないとは言ってない」
lines.english: “I never said I didn't want it.”

lines.japanese:
近場の自由広場―――というと大げさだが、商店
街が用意したたき火とそれを囲む複数の椅子―――
にて、巨砲を歯で削り食う作業に二人は没頭した。
lines.english: At a nearby public square—a grand name for the bonfire the shopping district had provided and the cluster of chairs around it—the two devoted themselves to gnawing their great guns down to nothing.

lines.japanese:
なんとも巨大な芋である。
　どうかしたのかと質問したくなる、全長２５セン
チ直径は１０センチ近い一品。
lines.english: They were truly colossal potatoes. At 25 centimeters long and nearly 10 thick, each was enough to make a person wonder what on earth had happened.

lines.japanese:
一本一食。そんなボリューム。
　芯までほどよく火が通っていて、固い部分はない。
lines.english: One potato, one meal. That much food. Each was cooked through to the core, without a hard spot anywhere.

lines.japanese:
ほのかな甘み。
　やわらかくほぐれる繊維の歯ごたえ。
　夢中になる。
lines.english: A delicate sweetness. Tender fibers yielding beneath their teeth. They lost themselves in it.

lines.japanese: き
lines.english: primal

lines.japanese: ふかした芋は人を生のままにするのだろうか。
lines.english: Did steamed potatoes strip people down to their primal selves?

lines.japanese: 古代の記憶が呼び覚まされるのかも知れない。
lines.english: Perhaps it awakened some ancient memory.

lines.japanese:
「ふう」
「ふう」
lines.english: “Whew.” “Whew.”

lines.japanese:
二人は同時に、芋に熱せられた体内から、息を吐
き出した。
lines.english: Together they breathed out, their bodies warmed through by the potatoes.

lines.japanese:
のどごし熱し。
　恋に浮かされたような掠れた声であずさが呟く。
lines.english: It went down hot. In a husky voice as though dazed by love, Azusa murmured.

lines.japanese: 「……おいしかった」
lines.english: “…That was delicious.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
加熱された大口径を解体する作業に、二人はだい
ぶ疲労していた。
lines.english: The labor of dismantling that heated, large-caliber ordnance had left them both thoroughly exhausted.

lines.japanese:
少しぼんやりしている。
　続く言葉もなく、流れる風に身をさらす。
lines.english: They sat in a mild daze. With nothing more to say, they let the passing breeze wash over them.

lines.japanese: やがて、
lines.english: At length,

lines.japanese: 「……家に、帰ろうか」
lines.english: “…Shall we go home?”

lines.japanese: 「そだねぇ」
lines.english: “I guess so.”

lines.japanese: 「眠くなってきたよ」
lines.english: “I'm getting sleepy.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、忍くんの本」
lines.english: “Oh, your book.”

lines.japanese: 「……これ、おもろいの？」
lines.english: “…Is this any good?”

lines.japanese: 忍の買った本に目をとめ。
lines.english: Her gaze fell on the book Shinobu had bought.

lines.japanese: 「うん、僕は好きな作家だ」
lines.english: “Yes. I like the author.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。今度貸して」
lines.english: “Huh. Lend it to me sometime.”

lines.japanese: 忍はびっくりしてしまった。
lines.english: Shinobu was taken aback.

lines.japanese: 「……小説なんて読むの？」
lines.english: “…You read novels?”

lines.japanese: あずさはむーとする。
lines.english: Azusa pouted.

lines.japanese: 「よ、読むよう。最近は」
lines.english: “I-I do read. Lately.”

lines.japanese: 「成長したもんだ……」
lines.english: “How you've grown…”

lines.japanese: 「最近はテツガク系かな」
lines.english: “Lately I'm into, y'know, philosophy stuff.”

lines.japanese: 得意げに。
lines.english: She looked very pleased with herself.

lines.japanese:
「あー、文学スノッブのパターンだよね。その一気
　にテツガクから行くところとか」
lines.english: “Ah, the classic literary-snob trajectory. Especially the part where you jump straight into philosophy.”

lines.japanese:
「でも文学スノッブって言われたら、人間オシマイ
　だなぁ……」
lines.english: “But once somebody calls you a literary snob, it's all over, isn't it…?”

lines.japanese: 「うがーん……」
lines.english: “Noooo…”

lines.japanese: 「それ貸してあげるよ」
lines.english: “I'll lend you this one.”

lines.japanese: 「え、いいの？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ためしに読んでみるといいよ」
lines.english: “Yes. Give it a try.”

lines.japanese: 「わ、じゃー借ります」
lines.english: “Wow. Then I'll borrow it.”

lines.japanese:
嬉しげに抱え込む。
　それを見て、忍は理解者の如く頷いた。
lines.english: She hugged it to herself in delight. Shinobu watched her and gave a knowing nod.

lines.japanese: 「あずさはそうでなくっちゃね」
lines.english: “That's the Azusa I know.”

lines.japanese:
あずさは幼少のみぎりより、年齢の低さからか常
に小遣いに不自由する身分であり、なんでも借りて
済ます娘……カリスマと呼ばれていたのである。
lines.english: Since she was little, perhaps because she was so young, Azusa had always been short of pocket money. She made do by borrowing everything… They called her a Loan Star.

lines.japanese:
そんなあずさに、忍はいつでも甘すぎた。
　まるで、成長する必要などないとばかりに―――
lines.english: And Shinobu had always been far too indulgent with her. As if she had no need to grow up at all—

lines.japanese: 「行こうか」
lines.english: “Shall we go?”

lines.japanese: 「うん！」
lines.english: “Yeah!”

lines.japanese: 元気よく立ち上がる。
lines.english: She bounced to her feet.

lines.japanese: 「今日はたくさんお話できたね」
lines.english: “We talked about so much today, didn't we?”
“…Did we?”

lines.japanese: 「楽しかったよ。ふたりっきりっていいね！」
lines.english: “I had fun. It's nice when it's just the two of us!”

lines.japanese:
自然と顔がほころぶ。
　そして歩き出した矢先、
lines.english: He couldn't help smiling. And just as they started walking—

lines.japanese: 「貴宮？」
lines.english: “Atemiya?”

lines.japanese: 声をかけられた。
lines.english: Someone called out to him.
“…Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱりそうだ。お久しぶり」
lines.english: “I knew it. Long time no see.”

lines.japanese: 「ええと……」
lines.english: “Uh…”

lines.japanese:
見覚えのある顔だった。
　しかし具体的にどこで会ったのか、思い出せない。
lines.english: He knew the face. But he couldn't remember where exactly he'd seen it.

lines.japanese: 「……あー、ええと」
lines.english: “…Uh, let's see…”

lines.japanese: 「同期を忘れるなよ。中学でも一緒だったろ」
lines.english: “Don't tell me you've forgotten one of the guys from your year. We went to middle school together too.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだっけ」
lines.english: “Oh. Were we?”

lines.japanese: 「誰さん？」
lines.english: “Who's he?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、さっき話した施設時代の知り合い」
lines.english: “Um, someone I knew back at the facility—the place I was telling you about.”

lines.japanese:
「おお、なかなかのシャンだな。
　沢野だ、よろしくな」
lines.english: “Well, well. She's quite a dish. I'm Sawano. Nice to meet you.”
“A dish……”

lines.japanese: あずさは半分だけ、忍の背中に身を寄せた。
lines.english: Azusa half-hid behind Shinobu's back.

lines.japanese: 「あはは、何それ。かわい」
lines.english: “Ha ha—what's that? Cute.”

lines.japanese: 「ナンパ禁止」
lines.english: “No hitting on her.”

lines.japanese: 「しませんって」
lines.english: “I'm not, I'm not.”

lines.japanese: 「……中学ン時だっけ？　最後に会ったの？」
lines.english: “…Was middle school the last time we saw each other?”

lines.japanese: 「だったっけ？　俺もあまり記憶がない」
lines.english: “Was it? I don't remember too well either.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ同じ町に住んでるし」
lines.english: “Then again, we do live in the same town.”

lines.japanese: 「そうね。すれ違ってるはずだよな」
lines.english: “Yeah. Must've passed each other around town.”

lines.japanese: 「さっき、こっちの子とドロップの話してたんだよ」
lines.english: “I was just telling her about the drops.”

lines.japanese: 「ドロップ？」
lines.english: “Drops?”

lines.japanese: 「あの施設内通貨。一日外出権とか」
lines.english: “That currency we used inside the facility. Day passes and stuff.”

lines.japanese: 「あーあー、あれな。えらい懐かしい話だな」
lines.english: “Ohhh, right. Those. Man, that takes me back.”

lines.japanese: あずさはただ、流れる会話を不安げに追っている。
lines.english: Azusa simply watched the conversation flow back and forth, uneasy.

lines.japanese:
「俺貯めてたなあ。
　結局、ヘタレであまり使わなかったけど」
lines.english: “I used to save mine up. Didn't have the nerve to spend many of them in the end, though.”

lines.japanese: 「全部食べてたよ」
lines.english: “I ate every one.”

lines.japanese:
「……ま、それが利口だよな。あれ、ガキにとっちゃ
　必要な栄養なんだし」
lines.english: “…Well, that was the smart way to go. Kids needed the nutrition in those things.”

lines.japanese: 「懐かしいけど、戻りたいとは思わないな」
lines.english: “I get nostalgic, but I wouldn’t want to go back.”
“…Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
「俺さ、今すっげー楽しいのよ。
　もういない連中には悪いけどさ」
lines.english: “Life's fantastic for me these days. Feel kind of bad saying it, what with the others who aren't around anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese:
「なんだかんだ言って、自分で自分の命、まかなっ
　てる感じがするしな。生きるって素晴らしい」
lines.english: “When all's said and done, I feel like I'm paying my own way through life now. Being alive is wonderful.”

lines.japanese: 「ところでこないだすげえことを思いついたのよ」
lines.english: “You know, I had this incredible thought the other day.”

lines.japanese: 「どんな？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese:
「俺は世の中に生かされてるんじゃなく、自力で生
　きてるんだって」
lines.english: “The world isn't keeping me alive. I'm living under my own steam.”

lines.japanese:
ほんの少し、忍は呆気にとられた。
　呆れたとも言う。
lines.english: Shinobu was a little taken aback. Exasperated, even.

lines.japanese: 「変な顔禁止させてもらっていいか」
lines.english: “Mind if I ban that weird face?”

lines.japanese: 「ごめん……思いの外ハズイ言葉だったんだ」
lines.english: “Sorry… That was a lot more embarrassing than I expected.”

lines.japanese: 「ハズくない！　イカしてる！」
lines.english: “It's not embarrassing! It's badass!”

lines.japanese: 「イカでもタコでもいいけどさ。もう帰ったら？」
lines.english: “Badass, jackass—whatever. Why don't you go home?”

lines.japanese: つれない言葉を沢野は無視した。
lines.english: Sawano ignored the frosty reception.

lines.japanese:
「そう思えば、今の生活だって負い目を感じる必要
　はないだろ。幸せになりすぎてるとしてもな」
lines.english: “Look at it that way, and there’s no reason to feel guilty about the life you have now, even if it’s gotten too good.”

lines.japanese: 「……まあ、そのあたりは人それぞれだし」
lines.english: “…Well, everyone feels differently about that.”

lines.japanese: 「気に留めておいてくれ、大将」
lines.english: “Just give it some thought, chief.”

lines.japanese: ばしりばしりと両肩を叩いた。
lines.english: He smacked Shinobu on both shoulders, one after the other.

lines.japanese: 「ああ……けど」
lines.english: “Yeah… But—”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「こんなに話す方だったっけ？　うちら？」
lines.english: “Did we ever talk this much? You and me?”

lines.japanese:
「いやなに。顔見かけたんで声かけただけだ。
　話したい気分だったし」
lines.english: “Nothing to it. Saw your face and thought I'd say hello. Felt like talking, too.”

lines.japanese: 「そういうことって、あるっしょ？」
lines.english: “You get that sometimes, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ある、かな？」
lines.english: “Do I?”

lines.japanese: 「うむ。じゃあな。お達者」
lines.english: “Indeed. Farewell, then. Take care.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ……じゃあ」
lines.english: “Uh, yeah… See you.”

lines.japanese:
少年はさっと身をひるがえすと、遠くで待ってい
る仲間らしき少年のところに走り去った。
lines.english: The boy wheeled around and dashed off to another boy waiting in the distance, apparently a friend.

lines.japanese: 「……けっこういい人だったの？」
lines.english: “…Was he a pretty decent guy?”

lines.japanese:
「んー、あまり記憶がない……
　ほとんど話したことないかも……」
lines.english: “Mm, I don't remember much… I don't think we ever talked very much…”

lines.japanese: 「ノスタル弁慶なのかな」
lines.english: “Maybe he's a memory-lane lion.”
“A what?”

lines.japanese:
「懐かしい過去を一緒に過ごしてると、仲間意識が
　強くなるという」
lines.english: “They say sharing memories of the old days strengthens your sense of fellowship.”

lines.japanese: 「すごい言葉作ったなまた」
lines.english: “That's quite a phrase you've coined this time.”

lines.japanese: 「さ、帰ろ！」
lines.english: “Come on, let's go home!”

lines.japanese: 手を引かれる。
lines.english: She tugged him by the hand.
“…Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
手首に巻き付いた指を、そっと絡め取る。
　五本の指を互いに噛ませて、暮れかけた街並みに
没入していく二人―――
lines.english: He gently threaded his fingers through those curled around his wrist. Their fingers interlaced, and together they disappeared into the streets as twilight fell—

lines.japanese:
いつも通りの時間。目が覚める。
　五時。
　運動着に着替えて外に。
lines.english: Same time as always. He woke. Five o'clock. He changed into workout clothes and stepped outside.

lines.japanese:
朝靄に包まれた街を走る。
　肌寒い空気、規則的な呼吸、息が白い。
　いつものコースをいつものペースで走る。
lines.english: He ran through the streets shrouded in morning mist. The air chilled his skin; his breathing kept a steady rhythm; his breath plumed white. Same route, same pace as always.

lines.japanese:
寝起きの体が、少しずつ覚醒していく。
　頭も。
lines.english: His body, still groggy from sleep, gradually woke. His mind, too.

lines.japanese:
曲がり角を右折する。
　交差点で、あずさが走ってきた。合流。
lines.english: He turned right at the corner. At the intersection, Azusa came running up. They fell in together.

lines.japanese: 「おはよい」
lines.english: “Good morniiing!”

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「ひっ、はっ、ひっ、はっ……」
lines.english: “Hh, hah, hh, hah…”

lines.japanese: 「ペース早いんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Aren't you going a little fast?”

lines.japanese:
「どうしてっ……そんな、平気、なのかな……
　忍くんは……」
lines.english: “How come… you're fine… Shinobu…?”

lines.japanese: 「要領」
lines.english: “Knack.”

lines.japanese: 「くるひー……」
lines.english: “It huuurts…”

lines.japanese: 「マイペースでいきなよ」
lines.english: “Set your own pace.”

lines.japanese: 「だって、おいてかれる……」
lines.english: “But you'll leave me behind…”

lines.japanese: 「これ以上だらだらしても、何もならないからね」
lines.english: “Any slower than this and it won’t do us any good.”

lines.japanese: 「あうあ……」
lines.english: “Auuugh…”

lines.japanese: あずさはなんとかついてきた。
lines.english: Azusa managed to keep up.

lines.japanese:
ちょうど町内を一周して自宅前に戻ると、事後の
体操を済ませる。
lines.english: After completing a lap around the neighborhood and returning to his house, they finished with their cooldown stretches.

lines.japanese: 「ひはー、ぜはー……死んだ……」
lines.english: “Hhhahh, hhhahh… I'm dead…”

lines.japanese: あずさは動けない。
lines.english: Azusa couldn't move.

lines.japanese: 「そのうち慣れるよ」
lines.english: “You'll get used to it.”
“Aaagh…”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、筋肉をほぐさないと」
lines.english: “Come on. You need to loosen those muscles.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん、あー……しんど……」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Aah… This is brutal…”

lines.japanese: のたくたと、あずさ。
lines.english: Azusa moved sluggishly.

lines.japanese: 「……ん？　あずさ、これどうしたの？」
lines.english: “…Hm? Azusa, what happened to your arm?”

lines.japanese: 「んあ？」
lines.english: “Nnuh?”

lines.japanese:
「腕のところ、赤くなってる……
　これ、注射のあと？」
lines.english: “Your arm's all red here… Is this from a shot?”

lines.japanese:
ちょうど二の腕のあたりだ。
　細かな刺傷が密集している。
lines.english: Right around the upper arm. A dense cluster of tiny puncture wounds.

lines.japanese: 「これって……？」
lines.english: “What is this…?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、それ注射のあと」
lines.english: “Oh, those? They're from shots.”

lines.japanese: 「こんなにたくさん？」
lines.english: “This many?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。何度も」
lines.english: “Yeah. Over and over.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ……なんか……」
lines.english: “I see… That's…”

lines.japanese: 「なに、ヘン？」
lines.english: “What? Is it weird?”

lines.japanese:
あずさはきょとんとして、傷口を改める。
　その様子に、挙動不審な部分はない。
　心にやましいところのある人間の態度ではない。
lines.english: Azusa blinked blankly and looked over the marks again. There was nothing suspicious in the way she acted. It was not the behavior of someone with something to hide.

lines.japanese:
本当に注射なのだろうと思える。
　ただこの痕からすると、思いつくのはハンコ注射だ。
lines.english: They did seem to be genuine injection marks. But looking at the pattern, the first thing that came to mind was a multipuncture vaccination.

lines.japanese: 「あずさ、ＢＣＧ予防接種とか受けたの？」
lines.english: “Azusa, did you get a BCG vaccination or something?”

lines.japanese: 「なにそれ？」
lines.english: “What's that?”

lines.japanese:
「ハンコみたいな形をした……
　それって普通の注射なの？」
lines.english: “The kind shaped like a stamp… Was this really just a regular shot?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ。何度も失敗しちゃって」
lines.english: “Yeah. They kept messing it up.”

lines.japanese: 「…………ああ、そういうこと」
lines.english: “……Oh. That explains it.”

lines.japanese:
技量の未熟な者も現場には存在し、そしていずれ
は上達しなければならない。
lines.english: Even on the job, some practitioners were inexperienced, and sooner or later they had to learn.

lines.japanese:
その礎となる不幸な人間というものが、まず必要
なのである。
lines.english: First, though, they needed some unfortunate soul on whom to build their skills.

lines.japanese: 「でもこれ、だいぶ前だーね。子供の頃だよ」
lines.english: “But this was ages ago. Back when I was little.”

lines.japanese: 「最近じゃないんだ」
lines.english: “So it's not recent.”

lines.japanese: 「最近だと、学校で受けるやつくらいだね」
lines.english: “These days, it's just the ones we get at school.”

lines.japanese: 「あと、残っちゃってるんだ」
lines.english: “And the marks are still there.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、柔肌にばばーんと」
lines.english: “Yep. Bam! Right on my tender skin.”

lines.japanese: 「いたましいね」
lines.english: “Tragic.”

lines.japanese:
「色素がちんちゃくしたという説が有力で、葉子ちゃ
　んが言うには遊びすぎて黒くなったちく―――」
lines.english: “The leading theory is hyperpigmentation, and Youko says it's a nipple gone dark from too much fooling arou—”

lines.japanese: 忍はしなやかに鼻フックを決めた。
lines.english: With fluid grace, Shinobu executed a nose hook.

lines.japanese: 名誉のため映像記録停止―――
lines.english: For the sake of her honor: video recording paused—

lines.japanese: 「ふがー！？」
lines.english: “Fngaaah!?”

lines.japanese: 「エレガント方向で是非」
lines.english: “Let's keep this elegant, please.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、その方向に行くっ！　行くからっ！」
lines.english: “I-I'll keep it elegant! I will!”

lines.japanese:
あずさの顔は、無事に偶蹄類から人類へと舞い戻
った。
lines.english: Azusa's face made it safely back from the even-toed ungulates to humanity.

lines.japanese: 記録開始―――
lines.english: Recording resumed—

lines.japanese:
「さ、早朝から馬鹿やってないで背中合わせよう。
　あずさの好きなやつ」
lines.english: “All right, enough fooling around this early. Let's do the back-to-back stretch. The one you like.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん！」
lines.english: “Oh, okay!”

lines.japanese: 二人の背中をくっつけて、腕を絡める。
lines.english: They pressed their backs together and linked arms.

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫、かな？」
lines.english: “Are you okay now?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、もう平気」
lines.english: “Yeah, I'm fine now.”

lines.japanese:
あずさが前屈する。
　とはいえ、体格が違う。
lines.english: Azusa bent forward. The trouble was, their builds were very different.

lines.japanese:
忍も決して大柄ではないが、あずさはあまりにも
小さすぎた。
lines.english: Shinobu wasn't particularly big himself, but Azusa was far too small.

lines.japanese:
地面につま先をつけたまま、あずさに体重を預け
るにとどめる。
lines.english: He kept his toes planted on the ground and merely let Azusa support part of his weight.

lines.japanese: 「むぎぃ」
lines.english: “Mngh!”

lines.japanese:
それでも潰れてしまいそうな様子だ。
　あずさは、自分が頑張って忍を天に持ち上げてい
ると思っている。
lines.english: Even then, she looked liable to be crushed. Azusa believed she was lifting Shinobu bodily into the heavens through sheer effort.

lines.japanese: 思っている……幸福に。
lines.english: She believed it… blissfully.

lines.japanese: 「今度はこっちだね」
lines.english: “My turn now.”

lines.japanese: 「ぐーんってやってよ」
lines.english: “Give me a biiig stretch.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ、はい」
lines.english: “Sure. Here we go.”

lines.japanese: ぐーん。
lines.english: Streeetch.

lines.japanese: 「うわぁお！」
lines.english: “Woooow!”

lines.japanese: 両脚を天に跳ね上げる。
lines.english: She flung both legs skyward.

lines.japanese: 「あおいそらー！」
lines.english: “Blue skyyy!”

lines.japanese:
じたばたと足を振る。
　負担は下に行く。
lines.english: Her feet kicked and flailed. The strain fell on the person underneath.

lines.japanese:
それなりに鍛えている忍は、どうということもな
く姿勢を維持できている。
lines.english: Shinobu kept himself in reasonable shape and could hold the position without any real trouble.

lines.japanese: 多少きついが。
lines.english: Though it did take some effort.

lines.japanese: 「忍くんの背中に寝そべってるみたい」
lines.english: “It's like I'm lying down on your back.”

lines.japanese: 「前みたいに、頭から落ちないように」
lines.english: “Just don't fall headfirst like last time.”

lines.japanese: 「逆上がりの要領で着地するもん」
lines.english: “I’ll land like I’m doing a backward flip.”

lines.japanese: 「危ない危ない。たぶん頭と頭ぶつかるし」
lines.english: “No, no. That's dangerous. We'd probably crack our heads together.”

lines.japanese: 「だって気持ちいいんだもん、ここ」
lines.english: “But it feels so nice up here.”

lines.japanese:
ずいぶんと長い時間、あずさは忍の背中に乗って
いた。
lines.english: She stayed there on Shinobu's back for a remarkably long time.

lines.japanese: 千鳥が出てきた。ゴミ袋を手にしている。
lines.english: Chidori came outside with a garbage bag in hand.

lines.japanese: 「お姉さん先生、おはようございまーす！」
lines.english: “Morning, Teacher-Sis!”

lines.japanese: 「おはようございます、紅緒さん」
lines.english: “Good morning, Miss Benio.”

lines.japanese: 「お借りしてまーす！」
lines.english: “I'm borrowing him!”

lines.japanese: 「ええ。どんどん甘えてやってくださいね」
lines.english: “Of course. Feel free to lean on him all you like.”

lines.japanese: 「甘えまーす！」
lines.english: “I will!”

lines.japanese: 「頑張りなさいね、忍」
lines.english: “Good luck, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、わかってるよ姉さん」
lines.english: “Yeah. I know, Sis.”

lines.japanese: 溌剌とした顔を向けた。
lines.english: He looked over at her, bright-eyed and energetic.

lines.japanese: 「シチューおいしかったわ。ごちそうさま」
lines.english: “The stew was delicious. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、おそまつさま」
lines.english: “Not at all. It was nothing special.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、忍くんのシチュー？　食べたい！」
lines.english: “Oh, Shinobu's stew? I want some!”

lines.japanese: 「まだ余っているから、食べていったら？」
lines.english: “There's still some left. Why don't you have some before you go?”

lines.japanese:
「あー……でもダメだ。帰らないと。
　勝手に外で食べたら怒られちゃう」
lines.english: “Ahh… No, I can’t. I have to go home. I’ll get in trouble if I eat somewhere else without asking.”

lines.japanese:
早送りでしおれる花のように、あずさは全身で枯
れた。
lines.english: Azusa wilted from head to toe like a flower in fast-forward.

lines.japanese: 「そう……なら持って帰ったらどう？」
lines.english: “I see… Then why don't you take some home?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうしようかな……いい？」
lines.english: “Oh. Maybe I will… Is that okay?”

lines.japanese: 「僕はいいよ、もちろん」
lines.english: “Sure. Of course I don't mind.”

lines.japanese: 「もらうもらう！　食べる食べる！」
lines.english: “I'll take it, I'll take it! I'll eat it, I'll eat it!”

lines.japanese: 「良かった。二人では食べきれないものね」
lines.english: “Good. The two of us can't finish it all.”

lines.japanese: 「たくさん作った方が味が出るんだよ」
lines.english: “Stew comes out better when you make a big pot.”

lines.japanese: 「お手伝いする」
lines.english: “I'll help!”

lines.japanese:
「二人とも遅刻しないように、お話はほどほどに切
　り上げてね」
lines.english: “Don't let all this talking make you late for school. Be sure to wrap it up soon.”

lines.japanese: 千鳥はゴミの回収所までひょこひょこ歩いていった。
lines.english: Chidori walked off toward the garbage pickup point in little bobbing steps.

lines.japanese: 「ちょうどおなかもすいてきました」
lines.english: “As it happens, I’m getting hungry.”

lines.japanese: 「最高の調味料だ」
lines.english: “Hunger's the best seasoning.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、でもいい風。ずっとこうしていたいよー」
lines.english: “Ahh, but the breeze feels so good. I want to stay like this forever.”

lines.japanese: 「それは……」
lines.english: “That would…”

lines.japanese: 「あたし、重い？」
lines.english: “Am I heavy?”

lines.japanese: 「いいや、軽いよ。羽みたい」
lines.english: “No. You're light. Like a feather.”

lines.japanese: 「空に、のぼれるかな……」
lines.english: “Do you think I could rise into the sky…?”

lines.japanese: ぼんやりと口にする。独白に近い。
lines.english: She said it dreamily, almost to herself.
“The sky—”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「空を、よく見ておくといいよ」
lines.english: “Take a good look at the sky.”

lines.japanese: 「どんな空かな？」
lines.english: “What kind of sky is it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、青いね」
lines.english: “Mm. It's blue.”

lines.japanese: 「他には？」
lines.english: “What else?”

lines.japanese: 「透けてる感じ。じっと見てるとゾクゾクする」
lines.english: “It feels transparent. If I stare at it, it gives me shivers.”

lines.japanese: 「自分が空の一部になったみたいになって」
lines.english: “Like I'm becoming part of the sky.”

lines.japanese: 「……そういう感性って、健全だ」
lines.english: “…That's a healthy way of seeing things.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「僕らの中で、あずさが一番いい子だってことだよ」
lines.english: “It means you're the best kid out of all of us.”

lines.japanese:
「えー、そうなんだ？　学校ではいつも叱られてま
　すよ？」
lines.english: “Really? But I'm always getting scolded at school.”

lines.japanese: 忍は声を出して笑う。
lines.english: Shinobu laughed aloud.

lines.japanese: 「そんなもんだよ」
lines.english: “That's how it works.”

lines.japanese: そのとき、
lines.english: At that moment—

lines.japanese: あずさの腹部が鳴った。
lines.english: Azusa's stomach growled.

lines.japanese: 「……ぎゃー」
lines.english: “…Nooo.”

lines.japanese: 「背中を通して伝わってきた」
lines.english: “I felt that through your back.”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃあー」
lines.english: “Noooo!”

lines.japanese:
空腹の表現として、おなかと背中がくっつくと言
うが、腹部の音は背中を通じて忍に伝わっていた。
lines.english: They said hunger made your stomach stick to your backbone; in Azusa's case, the growl had traveled through her back and into Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 「おりる、すみやかに……」
lines.english: “I am getting down. Immediately…”

lines.japanese: 「よっと」
lines.english: “Hup.”

lines.japanese: ようやく忍は解放される。
lines.english: At last, Shinobu was free.

lines.japanese: 「言い訳しません。ハラペコなのです……」
lines.english: “No excuses. I am famished…”

lines.japanese: 「今、何か容れ物に入れてくるよ。待ってて」
lines.english: “I'll put some in a container and bring it out. Wait here.”

lines.japanese: 「あいすみません」
lines.english: “Much obliged.”

lines.japanese: あずさはふらついた。
lines.english: Azusa swayed on her feet.

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの？」
lines.english: “What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「のけぞっていたんで、頭に血が……」
lines.english: “I was bent back so long, all the blood went to my head…”

lines.japanese: 肩をすくめて、忍は家に戻る。
lines.english: Shinobu shrugged and went back inside.

lines.japanese: 「おまちど」
lines.english: “Sorry to keep you.”

lines.japanese: 紙袋を渡す。
lines.english: He handed her a paper bag.

lines.japanese: 「いただきますです」
lines.english: “I shall receive it gratefully.”

lines.japanese:
合掌したまま頭を下げ、厳粛に厳粛に受け取るあ
ずさ。
lines.english: With palms still pressed together, Azusa bowed and accepted the bag with the utmost, utmost solemnity.

lines.japanese:
「忍君のシチュー、ごはんにかけてもおいしいから
　好き」
lines.english: “I like your stew. It’s good poured over rice, too.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そんな風に食べるんだ……」
lines.english: “Oh. So that's how you eat it…”

lines.japanese:
料理人の機微は味音痴によって四捨五入されてし
まう。
lines.english: The subtleties of a cook's craft were rounded clean away by a palate deaf to flavor.

lines.japanese:
「忍君は、あたしの食欲もそれ以外も満たしてくれ
　る……」
lines.english: “Shinobu, you satisfy my appetite and everything else, too…”

lines.japanese: などと呟き、うんうんと頷く。
lines.english: So she murmured, nodding sagely to herself.

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Come again?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ううん、なんでもない」
lines.english: “Oh—no. Nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「と、そろそろ戻らないと、学校まずいよ？」
lines.english: “Anyway, if you don't head back soon, aren't you going to be late for school?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
ハイペースで走りきった影響か。
　あずさは心持ち、ふらふらとした足取りで、帰路
についた。
lines.english: Maybe it was the effect of having run the whole course at such a fast pace. Azusa set off for home, her steps just a little unsteady.

lines.japanese:
危なっかしい。
　忍が朝のトレーニングをしていることを知り、自
分も参加すると主張してはや一週間。
lines.english: She looked as though she might fall over. It had already been a week since she learned about Shinobu's morning training and declared that she was joining him.

lines.japanese: 「……頑張るなぁ」
lines.english: “…She sure works hard.”

lines.japanese:
今でこそ鼻フックを決めることもできる関係だが、
かつては両者の間にも溝があった。
lines.english: Nowadays they were close enough for him to give her a nose hook, but there had once been a gulf between them.

lines.japanese:
出会いが出会いということもある。
　拒絶からはじまる出会い。
　そして再会があった。
lines.english: Perhaps it was because of the way they had met. A meeting that began with rejection. And then, a reunion.

lines.japanese:
思い出す。
　思い出す。
lines.english: He remembered. He remembered.

lines.japanese:
いろいろなことを脳裏に描く。
　目蓋の裏に、セピア色を吹きつけて。
lines.english: He conjured scene after scene in his mind, washing the backs of his eyelids in sepia.

lines.japanese:
今日からは、集団登校が義務づけられている。
　千鳥とともに集合場所に行くと、数名の母親が立
っていた。
lines.english: Beginning today, walking to school in a group was mandatory. When Shinobu and Chidori reached the meeting place, several mothers were standing there.

lines.japanese: 見張りといったところか。
lines.english: Supervisors, more or less.

lines.japanese: 「おはようございます。貴宮と申します」
lines.english: “Good morning. My name is Atemiya.”

lines.japanese:
「おはようございます。話はうかがっています。
　紅緒です」
lines.english: “Good morning. I've heard about you. I'm Benio.”

lines.japanese: 「弟の忍です」
lines.english: “This is my younger brother, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「よろしくお願いします」
lines.english: “It's a pleasure to meet you.”

lines.japanese: 頭を下げる。子供らしく。
lines.english: He bowed. Like a child.

lines.japanese: 「忍君。こんにちは」
lines.english: “Hello, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「あずさ、来なさい！」
lines.english: “Azusa, come here!”

lines.japanese:
凛然とした口調で、娘を呼びつけた。
　忍が声の投げかけられた方向を見る。
　少し離れた場所で子供たちが集まっていた。
lines.english: She summoned her daughter in a commanding tone. Shinobu looked in the direction she had called. A group of children had gathered a short distance away.

lines.japanese: 彼らの視線は、闖入者の忍に注がれている。
lines.english: Every eye was fixed on the intruder, Shinobu.

lines.japanese: （いやな空気だな……こういうの）
lines.english: (I don't like this sort of atmosphere…)

lines.japanese:
子供は残酷だ。
　いまだ情けを学びきってない。
　値踏みするかのような視線が気になった。
lines.english: Children were cruel. They had not yet fully learned compassion. He disliked the appraising quality of their gaze.

lines.japanese: さて。
lines.english: Now then.

lines.japanese:
一人集団の外に立っていた、一人の少女がやって
くる。
lines.english: A lone girl who had been standing apart from the group came over.

lines.japanese: 表情を少しも変えず、母親の隣に立つ。
lines.english: Without changing her expression in the slightest, she stood beside her mother.

lines.japanese:
「娘のあずさです。
　わからないことは、この子に聞いてください」
lines.english: “This is my daughter, Azusa. If there's anything you don't understand, ask her.”

lines.japanese: あずさは微妙に、忍から目線を外していた。
lines.english: Azusa's gaze slipped subtly away from Shinobu.

lines.japanese: （この子……あのときの）
lines.english: (This girl… from that day.)

lines.japanese: あずさと呼ばれた少女も、気づいているのだろうか。
lines.english: Had the girl called Azusa recognized him as well?

lines.japanese: 視線を合わせようとしない。
lines.english: She would not meet his eyes.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ忍、いってらっしゃい」
lines.english: “Have a good day, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「迷惑をかけないようにね」
lines.english: “Don't make trouble for anyone.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Okay.”

lines.japanese: あずさが無言で歩き出す。忍もついていく。
lines.english: Azusa began walking without a word. Shinobu followed.

lines.japanese:
振り返ると、千鳥と奥様方が挨拶をかわしていた。
　千鳥の笑顔が、目についた。
lines.english: When he looked back, Chidori was exchanging greetings with the mothers. Her smile caught his attention.

lines.japanese: 「……こっち」
lines.english: “…This way.”

lines.japanese: だが忍は止まったままだ。
lines.english: But Shinobu still had not moved.

lines.japanese: 「おい、こっちだってば」
lines.english: “Hey, I said this way.”

lines.japanese: 「……わかった」
lines.english: “…All right.”

lines.japanese:
忍は視線を戻し、歩き出した。
　こっちも何もない。
　通学班にまざればいいのだ。
lines.english: Shinobu turned back and began to walk. “This way” had nothing to do with it. He simply had to join the school group.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ちょっと……っ」
lines.english: “H-hey…”

lines.japanese:
追い抜かれたあずさが、小走りに並ぶ。
　見ず知らずの少年少女たちにまざる。
lines.english: Having been overtaken, Azusa trotted to catch up. They merged into the group of unfamiliar boys and girls.

lines.japanese:
声をかけてくる者はいなかった。
　新入りを意識している空気だけが、伝わってくる。
lines.english: No one spoke to him. Only the atmosphere told him that everyone was conscious of the newcomer.

lines.japanese: 「よろしく」
lines.english: “Nice to meet you.”

lines.japanese:
事務的に忍は言った。
　誰に言ったわけでもない。
　全体に呼びかけた。
lines.english: Shinobu spoke in a businesslike tone. The words were not addressed to anyone in particular. He offered them to the group as a whole.

lines.japanese:
儀式にも似た挨拶によって、わずかに空気が弛緩
した。
lines.english: The almost ceremonial greeting eased the tension in the air, if only slightly.

lines.japanese:
忍は自分が無関心をもって受け入れられたことを
感じ取った。
lines.english: Shinobu sensed that the group had accepted him with indifference.

lines.japanese:
暴れるでもなく、笑うでもない、目立たない少年
として。
lines.english: As an inconspicuous boy who neither misbehaved nor laughed.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、行くよ」
lines.english: “All right, let's go.”

lines.japanese:
時間が来て、あずさが先頭に立つ。
　皆が従った。
　噛み合わない歯車のような通学班だ。
lines.english: At the appointed time, Azusa took the lead. Everyone followed. The school group moved like gears that failed to mesh.

lines.japanese:
忍は自然、最後尾に。
　互いに言葉なく歩く。
　妙によそよそしい集団登校。
lines.english: Shinobu naturally fell in at the rear. They walked without a word to one another. A strangely distant procession to school.

lines.japanese: もともと打ち解けたグループではなかったのだろう。
lines.english: They had probably never been a friendly group to begin with.

lines.japanese:
忍という異物もまた、すぐに埋もれてしまうに違
いなかった。
lines.english: Shinobu, the foreign body among them, would doubtless disappear into the group before long.

lines.japanese: 無言の行進が、学校に向かって刻まれていく。
lines.english: The silent procession measured out its way toward the school.

lines.japanese: これでいいと忍は思った。
lines.english: This was fine, Shinobu thought.

lines.japanese:
学校が終わる。
　無意味とも思える半日を過ごすようになって、も
う一週間が経つ。
lines.english: School ended. A week had passed since these seemingly meaningless half-days had begun.

lines.japanese:
帰宅するため、忍は草原を横切る。
　さん、さん、と草を踏む音。
　生理的に心地よいリズム。
lines.english: On his way home, Shinobu crossed the meadow. Swish, swish—the sound of grass beneath his feet. A rhythm that pleased him at some bodily level.

lines.japanese:
心地よい何か。
　忍は最近、それを自覚しつつある。
　人は快楽のために生きている。
lines.english: Something pleasant. Lately, Shinobu had begun to recognize such things. People lived for pleasure.

lines.japanese:
ありとあらゆる快楽がある。
　人に親切にして喜ばれたり、たくさんの家族に囲
まれて幸せに暮らす、といった快さも含めて。
lines.english: Pleasure came in every conceivable form. It included helping someone and making them happy, or living happily surrounded by a large family.

lines.japanese:
心地よい現在に生きるため、努力し腐心する。
　草を踏む行為が、小さな幸せを忍に与えるように。
lines.english: People labored and racked their brains for the sake of a pleasant present. Just as the act of stepping on grass gave Shinobu this little happiness.

lines.japanese:
気配がした。近い。
　以前、草原で行われた蛮行を忍は目撃している。
lines.english: He sensed a presence. Close by. Shinobu had already witnessed an atrocity in this meadow.

lines.japanese:
だが今回については、より小規模の……単独の気
配であると思われた。
lines.english: But this time the presence seemed smaller in scale… a lone presence.

lines.japanese:
判断と選択は一瞬。
　忍は気配のもとに接近する。
　一目して立ち去るつもりで。
lines.english: Judgment and choice were instantaneous. Shinobu approached the source of the presence. He intended to take one look and leave.

lines.japanese:
草地に踏み込めば音が出る。
　気をつけて歩いた。
　覗き込むと、小さな影が寝そべっていた。
lines.english: Stepping into the grass would make noise. He walked carefully. When he peered closer, he found a small figure lying there.

lines.japanese: （このあいだの女の子……）
lines.english: (The girl from the other day…)

lines.japanese:
向こう側を向いて、腕枕で横たわっている。
　眠っているのかどうか。
lines.english: She lay facing away from him, her head pillowed on one arm. Was she asleep?

lines.japanese:
疑問に応じるように、左手が跳ね上がった。
　指先でむしりとった草を、パッと空に捨てた。
lines.english: As though answering the question, her left hand sprang up. She flung a fistful of grass she had plucked into the air.

lines.japanese: ……起きている。
lines.english: …She was awake.

lines.japanese:
その無意味な行為を、あずさは幾度も繰り返す。
　むしっては投げ、むしっては投げ。
　千切られた草が体にかかっても気にしない。
lines.english: Azusa repeated the pointless act again and again. Pluck and throw, pluck and throw. She paid no attention when the torn grass fell across her body.

lines.japanese:
無心に、機械を思わせて生命を刈り取り続ける。
　彼女はなぜ寝入るのか？
　満足のいく解が出ない。
lines.english: Mindlessly, mechanically, she went on cutting down life. Why had she lain down here? No satisfactory answer presented itself.

lines.japanese:
あまりにも不可解だからだ。
　単独で誰もいない草原に寝る。
　物理的にあり得ないことではないのだろう。
lines.english: The act was too incomprehensible. Lying alone in an empty meadow. It was not physically impossible, of course.

lines.japanese: だが―――
lines.english: But—

lines.japanese:
普通はやらない。
　それとも一人遊びに疲れ果てての結果だろうか？
　忍は周囲を見渡す。
lines.english: People did not ordinarily do it. Or had she exhausted herself playing alone? Shinobu looked around.

lines.japanese:
あずさは身一つだ。
　ボールなどの遊具の一つもない。
lines.english: Azusa had nothing but herself. Not so much as a ball or toy.

lines.japanese:
ひるがえって草原には、かけのぼるための木の一
本もない。
lines.english: For that matter, the meadow did not contain so much as a tree to climb.

lines.japanese:
視界が通るようにとの措置だが、もちろんそれは
外部から施設を見張るためのものではない。
lines.english: The land had been cleared to preserve sightlines, though naturally not so outsiders could watch the facility.

lines.japanese: 忍も詳しくは知らない。
lines.english: Shinobu did not know the details.

lines.japanese:
ただ街で行われるあらゆる経済活動をも凌駕する
莫大な金額が、この施設では日夜動いているのだと
いう。
lines.english: All he had heard was that vast sums—more than all the economic activity in the city—moved through this facility day and night.

lines.japanese:
口頭で何億規模の運用が雑談まじりに定められ、
若手研究員が配属最初の仕事として命じられる各部
署へ配達の、そのサンプル容器一つ一つが大企業の
lines.english: Hundreds of millions could be allocated by word of mouth in casual conversation, while each sample container a junior researcher delivered between departments as a first assignment was procured at a cost rivaling a major corporation’s

lines.japanese: 月間利益にも匹敵するコストで調達される。
lines.english: monthly profit.

lines.japanese:
別世界。
　草原は緩衝地帯のよう。
　異世界と現世界の狭間。
lines.english: Another world. The meadow was like a buffer zone. Between that world and this one.

lines.japanese:
そこにいる少女。
　立ってはおらず横たわる少女。
　何かを暗示しているようにも思えた。
lines.english: The girl within it. A girl not standing, but lying down. It almost seemed to symbolize something.

lines.japanese:
彼女に友人はいない。
　居場所はない。
　するべきこともない。
lines.english: She had no friends. No place to belong. Nothing she ought to do.

lines.japanese:
ただ生きているだけである。
　誰にも見つからないはずの胞衣のような場所、う
ずくまって身を縮める。
lines.english: She did nothing but live. Curled small inside this afterbirth of a place where no one was meant to find her.

lines.japanese:
回帰する場所は大地しかないと言わんばかりに。
　―――孤独する。
lines.english: As if the earth were the only place she could return to. —She gave herself over to solitude.

lines.japanese:
忍は引き返す。
　報告の必要もないだろう。
　無音の足取りで、施設側に歩いていく。
lines.english: Shinobu turned back. There was probably no need to report this. He walked noiselessly toward the facility.

lines.japanese:
そっと、少女あずさは身を起こした。
　まるで最初から存在に気づいていたかのように、
立ち去る忍の小さな背を見やった。
lines.english: Slowly, the girl Azusa sat up. As though she had known he was there from the beginning, she watched Shinobu's small back recede.

lines.japanese: くすんだ瞳が物憂げに伏せられる。
lines.english: Her clouded eyes lowered, heavy with melancholy.

lines.japanese:
再び少女は、寝床に潜る仕草で、草原に朽ち倒れ
ていく。
lines.english: Once more, as though burrowing into bed, the girl let herself sink and decay into the meadow.

lines.japanese: 彼女には何もない。
lines.english: She had nothing.

lines.japanese:
帰宅。
　合い鍵を使ってドアをあける。
　これは鍵っ子というらしい。
lines.english: Home. He unlocked the door with his spare key. Apparently, this made him a latchkey kid.

lines.japanese:
両親が働いているなどして自宅にいないため、子
供がいつも一人で家にいるという状態。
lines.english: A child who was always home alone because both parents worked or otherwise remained absent.

lines.japanese:
忍は思う。
　他の鍵っ子は、どのようにして孤独な時間を消費
しているのだろうか？
lines.english: Shinobu wondered. How did other latchkey children spend all those lonely hours?

lines.japanese: 忍には想像することもできない。
lines.english: Shinobu could not even imagine it.

lines.japanese:
リビング。
　真新しい自宅からは、いまだ建材の匂いが薄れない。
lines.english: The living room. The smell of building materials had yet to fade from the new house.

lines.japanese:
最初は頭痛に悩まされたが、今では麻痺したよう
に何も感じない。
lines.english: At first it had plagued him with headaches, but now he felt nothing, as though numb.

lines.japanese: （住んでいるのが二人だけだから、かな）
lines.english: (Is it because there are only two of us living here?)

lines.japanese:
冷凍庫をあけると三日分のパック弁当がスペース
を埋め尽くしていた。
lines.english: When he opened the freezer, three days' worth of packaged meals filled every inch.

lines.japanese:
二人とも調理などとは縁がない。
　いつものように一つを取り出し、電子レンジを使
って加熱した。
lines.english: Neither of them had anything to do with cooking. As always, he took out one package and heated it in the microwave.

lines.japanese: カップのみそ汁を添えて、一人、昼食を済ませる。
lines.english: He added a cup of miso soup and ate lunch alone.

lines.japanese:
忍は味の知覚が遅かった。
　だからだろうか。
lines.english: Shinobu's sense of taste had been slow to develop. Perhaps that was why.

lines.japanese:
味気ない冷凍食品でさえ、鮮烈な印象を与えたも
のだ。
lines.english: Even insipid frozen food once left a vivid impression upon him.

lines.japanese:
不満はない。
　学校に通うことで得た知識に、家族の手による家
庭料理という概念があった。
lines.english: He had no complaints. Among the things he had learned at school was the concept of meals cooked at home by a family.

lines.japanese:
確かに、興味がないといえば嘘になる。
　愛情がスパイスになるというのは眉唾としても、
家庭ごとの味が無数にあるということへの驚き。
lines.english: It would be a lie to say he felt no interest. Even if the notion that love was a seasoning seemed dubious, he marveled at the countless flavors belonging to countless homes.

lines.japanese: 全てを味わうことのできない、絶対の有限さ。
lines.english: A hard, absolute limit: no one could taste them all.

lines.japanese:
一人が生きる世界は一人分の世界。
　一人の人間が全能のものとなって、味を極め尽く
すなど考えられない。
lines.english: One person could live in only one person's world. No individual could become omnipotent and exhaust every possible flavor.

lines.japanese:
なのに世界は途方もなく大きく、確かにそこにあ
り続けた。
lines.english: Yet the world went on existing, impossibly vast, undeniably there.

lines.japanese: そして貴宮忍は一人だった。
lines.english: And Shinobu Atemiya was alone.

lines.japanese: 少年には何もない。
lines.english: The boy had nothing.

lines.japanese:
同種の孤独をまとう二人は、それでもしばらくは
他人同士だった。
lines.english: The two children wore the same kind of loneliness, yet for a while they remained strangers.

lines.japanese:
子供同士はすぐ友達になれるなどと言われる。
　が、二人が自覚的にとどまっていた領域は、大人
が他者に対して取る距離と同じだった。
lines.english: People said that children became friends at once. But the distance these two consciously maintained was the same as that which adults kept from other people.

lines.japanese:
紅緒あずさと、貴宮忍。
　学年も違うし性格も違う。
　関係を作る機会もない。
lines.english: Azusa Benio and Shinobu Atemiya. Different grades, different personalities. No opportunity to build a relationship.

lines.japanese:
通学班の少年少女は互い不仲で、通学中はいつも
無言。
lines.english: The boys and girls in the school group disliked one another and always walked in silence.

lines.japanese:
会話をする流れさえ、生まれたことはなかった。
　だから学校に通うようになって一週間になるのに、
忍には一人の友人もできない。
lines.english: Not even the opening for a conversation had ever arisen. So although a week had passed since he began school, Shinobu had not made a single friend.

lines.japanese:
そんな相互孤立も、じきに慣れた。
　クラスではうまくやっていた。
lines.english: He soon became accustomed to their mutual isolation. He managed well enough in class.

lines.japanese:
誰とも親しくはなれなかったが、誰からも目の敵
にされることもなかったからだ。
lines.english: He had become close to no one, but no one had singled him out as an enemy either.

lines.japanese:
＋－０。
　現状維持なら落胆する必要はない。
lines.english: Plus or minus zero. So long as the status quo held, there was no reason for disappointment.

lines.japanese: （……寂しいけど……ね）
lines.english: (…Though it's lonely.)

lines.japanese:
感情を表に出すこともない忍は、感情の起伏が少
ない子供に見られる。
lines.english: Because Shinobu never showed his feelings, people saw him as a child with few emotional ups and downs.

lines.japanese:
（それで……
　また誰と遊ぶでもなく医者に通うわけだ）
lines.english: (And now… I'm off to the doctor again, without having played with anyone.)

lines.japanese: ため息をついた。
lines.english: He sighed.

lines.japanese:
（行きは集団登校なのに、帰りは個別なのってどう
　なんだろ？）
lines.english: (What's the point of walking to school in a group if everyone goes home alone?)

lines.japanese:
些細な疑問を胸に、少年は近道の草原を横切って
いく。
lines.english: With that small question in his heart, the boy crossed the meadow that served as a shortcut.

lines.japanese:
ここが好きだった。
　大きな施設の背に位置していて、学区ではちょっ
とした穴場になっている。
lines.english: He liked it here. It lay behind the great facility, a little-known corner of the school district.

lines.japanese:
そして草原を横切ることで、大幅に近道ができる。
　夏日だった。
lines.english: Crossing the meadow also shortened the journey considerably. It was a summer day.

lines.japanese: 降り注ぐ日光は殺人的といえるレベルになっている。
lines.english: The sun beat down with murderous intensity.

lines.japanese:
例年にない酷暑が、毎年のものになって何年経つ
だろう。
lines.english: How many years had passed since unprecedented heat became an annual occurrence?

lines.japanese:
忍にとっては生まれついてのことだが、昨日には
異質と思っていた概念が、今日には常識になるのが
世の常だ。
