というとこれはもう神秘体験にも近い。
　想像の範囲を大きく超えているはずである。
lines.english: To dine at a restaurant before a movie on a date— that bordered on a mystical experience. It had to lie far beyond anything she could imagine.

lines.japanese: 「どこがいい？　希望のお店はある？」
lines.english: “Where would you like to go? Do you have a place in mind?”

lines.japanese: 近場では、いい食事ができる場所は多くない。
lines.english: There were not many places nearby that served a good meal.

lines.japanese:
駅の手前には、ファミリーレストランが一つと全
国チェーンの珈琲ショップ、それにファーストフー
ドくらいのものである。
lines.english: On this side of the station there was only one family restaurant, a national-chain coffee shop, and a fast-food place.

lines.japanese: アーケード方面に行くとまた雰囲気が変わる。
lines.english: Toward the shopping arcade, the atmosphere changed again.

lines.japanese:
飲み屋・パチンコ屋・理髪店・美容院・日用雑貨
店・コンビニ・ケーキ屋・クリーニング店と統一性
がなくなる。
lines.english: Bars, pachinko parlors, barbers, beauty salons, general stores, convenience stores, cake shops, and dry cleaners— there was no longer any pattern to the place.

lines.japanese:
残念ながら、飲食店は居酒屋系が多く高級レスト
ランはない。
lines.english: Unfortunately, most places to eat were taverns, and there were no fine restaurants.

lines.japanese: 地元密着型の商店街なのである。
lines.english: It was a shopping district that catered to locals.

lines.japanese: 「うーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese:
さて、あずさの理想に近いのはどれか？という問
題になる。
lines.english: The question, then, was which came closest to Azusa's ideal.

lines.japanese: 「……向こう口に行けば、中華の高級店があるね」
lines.english: “...There's an upscale Chinese place on the other side of the station.”

lines.japanese: 「中華かー」
lines.english: “Chinese, huh.”

lines.japanese: 線目になって、あずさは中華を想った。
lines.english: Azusa's eyes narrowed to slits as she contemplated Chinese food.

lines.japanese: 「いまいちビジョンがわかない」
lines.english: “I can't quite picture it.”

lines.japanese: 「昔、章二と斎と三人で入って酷い目にあったよ」
lines.english: “I went there once with Shouji and Itsuki. We had an awful time.”

lines.japanese: 「ひどいめって？」
lines.english: “Awful how?”

lines.japanese:
「予想以上の高級店で、一番安いメニューが２０００
　円の蟹チャーハンだった」
lines.english: “It was far fancier than we expected. The cheapest item was crab fried rice for two thousand yen.”

lines.japanese:
「他のお客さんは身なりのいい年配の人ばかりで、
　ラフな格好の客は僕らだけで恥をかいた」
lines.english: “Every other customer was well-dressed and older. We were the only ones in casual clothes. It was humiliating.”

lines.japanese:
「追い出されなかっただけでもマシだよね。
　ただあの時よりは、今日は入りやすいかも」
lines.english: “We were lucky they didn't throw us out. Though it might be easier to go in today.”

lines.japanese: 「章二いないし」
lines.english: “Because Shouji isn't here.”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう」
lines.english: “Exactly.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、味は良かった。うまかった」
lines.english: “Oh, the food was good. Delicious.”

lines.japanese: 「うーーん……」
lines.english: “Hmmm...”

lines.japanese: いまいちパッとしないらしい。
lines.english: The idea did not seem to excite her.

lines.japanese: 「あとは……別チェーンのファミレスがあるよね」
lines.english: “Otherwise... there's that other family-restaurant chain.”

lines.japanese: あずさの顔が輝く。
lines.english: Azusa's face lit up.

lines.japanese: 「そういえばファミレス二人で入ったことないね」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, we've never gone to one with just the two of us.”

lines.japanese: 「ん、確かに」
lines.english: “True.”

lines.japanese: 「すいてるかな？」
lines.english: “Think it’ll be quiet?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、そんなには混んでないかと」
lines.english: “I doubt it'll be too crowded.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあそこ！」
lines.english: “Then let's go there!”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。行こうか」
lines.english: “Sure. Let's go.”

lines.japanese:
あずさが忍の手を取った。両手で握って、引っ張
った。
lines.english: Azusa took Shinobu's hand. Gripping it in both of hers, she tugged him forward.

lines.japanese:
少しばかり無邪気すぎるあずさの気持ちが、忍に
はよくわかる。
lines.english: Shinobu understood the eagerness behind it—an eagerness just a little too childlike.

lines.japanese: 「ところで、お母さんにバレなかった？」
lines.english: “By the way, your mother didn't find out?”

lines.japanese: 「これはバレても平気だよ」
lines.english: “It'll be okay even if she does.”

lines.japanese: 「だって、もう子供じゃないもん」
lines.english: “I'm not a child anymore.”

lines.japanese: 満面の笑顔で言うのだ。
lines.english: She said it with a radiant smile.

lines.japanese: 「……だ、黙るの？」
lines.english: “...Y-you're just going quiet?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや」
lines.english: “Oh, no.”

lines.japanese:
「まあ子供とか関係なくて、デートだからねぇ……
　一応これ」
lines.english: “It's not about whether you're a child. This is a date... technically.”

lines.japanese: 「親としては気になるところじゃないかな」
lines.english: “I imagine a parent would be concerned.”

lines.japanese: 「見つからないと思うんだ、お母さん仕事してるし」
lines.english: “I don’t think she’ll see us. My mother’s working.”

lines.japanese: 「……そういや、仕事場ってどのあたりなの？」
lines.english: “...Where does she work, anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「駅向こうのビルデング」
lines.english: “In a bilding across the station.”

lines.japanese: 「……近いじゃん」
lines.english: “...That's close.”

lines.japanese: 「こっち側だったら平気」
lines.english: “We'll be fine on this side.”

lines.japanese:
「……その楽観がいつも破滅を招くんじゃない
　かなぁと」
lines.english: “...Isn't that optimism what always leads to disaster?”

lines.japanese: 「怒られるたびに門限制限されてるし」
lines.english: “Every time you get in trouble, they move your curfew earlier.”
“Ughh...”

lines.japanese:
「一年ごとに延びるはずの門限がさ、本来だったら
　七時半になってるはずが、なぜか今でも六時前後
　というのはどういうことですか」
lines.english: “Your curfew is supposed to get later every year. It ought to be seven thirty by now, so why is it somehow still around six?”

lines.japanese:
「そうなんだよね……大人になったら変えてくれる
　って約束なんだけど……このままだと大人になっ
　ても門限六時のままだ」
lines.english: “I know... She promised she'd change it when I grew up, but at this rate I'll still have a six o'clock curfew after I'm an adult.”

lines.japanese: 「いつから大人なんだろうね」
lines.english: “When do you become an adult, anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「身長１５０以上とか」
lines.english: “Once you're over 150 centimeters tall?”

lines.japanese: 「越えてる。越えてるよもう」
lines.english: “I am. I'm already over that.”

lines.japanese: 「そうね、じゃあ」
lines.english: “Right. Then...”
“An eighty-centimeter bust—”

lines.japanese: 「ほろ苦いよ」
lines.english: “That's bittersweet.”

lines.japanese: あずさは空を見上げた。むやみに青い空。
lines.english: Azusa looked up at the sky. A needlessly blue sky.

lines.japanese: 「青すぎる……」
lines.english: “Too blue...”

lines.japanese: 「青春って言うくらいだからね」
lines.english: “Well, blue is the color of youth.”

lines.japanese: 「沙也加ちんだって８０はないよ？」
lines.english: “Saya isn't eighty centimeters either, is she?”

lines.japanese: 「あるよ」
lines.english: “She is.”

lines.japanese: 「絶対ないよー」
lines.english: “No way.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、あるものは仕方ない」
lines.english: “A fact's a fact. Nothing to be done about it.”

lines.japanese: 「どうして知ってるの？」
lines.english: “How do you know?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、大事なのはサイズじゃないか……」
lines.english: “Oh. Size isn't what matters...”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そうだ、そうだ」
lines.english: “Right. Exactly.”

lines.japanese: 「形だね」
lines.english: “Shape is.”

lines.japanese:
押し黙った。
　忍のフォローはいつもこんな結末だ。
lines.english: She fell silent. Shinobu's attempts at reassurance always ended this way.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese:
反応がない。
　見ると、あずさは両手で自分の胸を揉んでいた。
lines.english: No response. When he looked, Azusa was squeezing her chest with both hands.

lines.japanese: 「何してんの……」
lines.english: “What are you doing...?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、あっ？」
lines.english: “What? Oh?”

lines.japanese: 慌てて手を離す。
lines.english: She hurriedly pulled her hands away.

lines.japanese: 「かゆかった」
lines.english: “It was itchy.”
“...R-right.”

lines.japanese: 沈黙。
lines.english: Silence.

lines.japanese: 「だいたい、どうして沙也加が出てくるの？」
lines.english: “Why did Sayaka come up in the first place?”

lines.japanese: あずさの顔に困惑が浮かんだ。
lines.english: Azusa looked puzzled.

lines.japanese: 「なんとなく」
lines.english: “No reason.”

lines.japanese:
忍の曖昧な笑み。
　それを見て、あずさが居心地悪そうに面を伏せた。
lines.english: Shinobu gave a noncommittal smile. Azusa saw it and lowered her eyes, suddenly uncomfortable.

lines.japanese: 「二人ってさあ……やっぱり……」
lines.english: “You two... Are you really...?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ行こう。戦いはまだはじまったばかりだ」
lines.english: “Come on. Our battle has only just begun.”

lines.japanese: 「わきゃ、きゃ……っ」
lines.english: “Wah—hey...!”

lines.japanese:
引っ張っていく。
　いろいろなものを有耶無耶にしながら。
lines.english: He pulled her along, leaving all manner of things unresolved.
“—Azusa.”

lines.japanese:
硬質の声だった。
　あずさの体が、ぴんと伸びて固まる。
　電流でも流されたように。
lines.english: The voice was hard-edged. Azusa's body snapped straight and rigid, as though an electric current had passed through it.

lines.japanese:
鍵を閉めて、門を抜ける。
　雪でも降りそうな寒空だった。
　暑さよりは、寒さの方が我慢しやすい。
lines.english: He locked the door and passed through the gate. Under the cold sky, it felt as though it might snow. Cold was easier to endure than heat.

lines.japanese:
そう忍は思う。
　あまり暑いと頭痛がするからだ。
lines.english: So Shinobu thought. Too much heat gave him headaches.

lines.japanese:
脳の血管が膨張しているせいだという話だが、頭
を冷やしても気休めほどにしか効果がない。
lines.english: They said it was caused by dilation of the blood vessels in his brain, but cooling his head offered little more than reassurance.

lines.japanese:
肉体とは思い通りにならないものらしい。
　心ほどではないが―――
　門を出る。
lines.english: The body, apparently, refused to do as it was told. Not quite as stubbornly as the heart, but— He stepped through the gate.

lines.japanese:
このタイミングで、あずさと出会うことが多い。
　が、今日は少女の姿は見られなかった。
　かわりに、
lines.english: He often encountered Azusa at just this moment. Today, however, the girl was nowhere to be seen. In her place—

lines.japanese: 「忍君」
lines.english: “Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「おはようございます」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: あずさの母親がいた。
lines.english: Azusa's mother was there.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「あずさがね、風邪を引いてしまったようで」
lines.english: “It seems Azusa has caught a cold.”

lines.japanese: 「そうですか、大変ですね」
lines.english: “I see. That's too bad.”

lines.japanese:
「たいしたこともないのだけれど、休ませることに
　したの」
lines.english: “It's nothing serious, but I decided she ought to stay home and rest.”

lines.japanese: 「そうですか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese:
「悪いんだけど、今日はあずさ抜きで通学してくれ
　る？」
lines.english: “I'm sorry to ask, but will you go to school without Azusa today?”

lines.japanese: 「わかりました」
lines.english: “Of course.”

lines.japanese:
「ごめんなさいね。急なことだったから、他の人に
　連絡する暇がなくて」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. It came on so suddenly, I didn't have time to contact anyone else.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、皆にはそう伝えておきます」
lines.english: “Yes. I'll let everyone know that.”

lines.japanese:
会話が途切れた。
　冷ややかな空気が合間に滑りこむ。
　忍は居心地の悪さに身じろぎする。
lines.english: The conversation lapsed. Chill air slipped into the silence between them. Shinobu shifted uncomfortably.

lines.japanese: 「娘には良くしてくれているようね」
lines.english: “You seem to have been very good to my daughter.”
“...Not at all.”

lines.japanese:
「そんなことないでしょう。
　あの子を見ていればわかるもの」
lines.english: “Oh, I think you have. I can tell just from looking at her.”

lines.japanese: 「あの子は迷惑をかけてはいない？」
lines.english: “She hasn't been causing you any trouble, has she?”

lines.japanese: 「決してそんなことは」
lines.english: “Nothing of the kind.”

lines.japanese: 「それはそれは」
lines.english: “Is that so.”

lines.japanese: 「でも」

目線を合わせて、忍は硬直する。
　探る目。
　何を―――？
lines.english: Their eyes met, and Shinobu went rigid. Her gaze probed him. For what—?

lines.japanese:
「まったく、迷惑をかけていないということはない
　はずです」
lines.english: “Surely it isn't true that she's caused you no trouble whatsoever.”

lines.japanese: 「どうかしら？」
lines.english: “Well?”

lines.japanese: 「……まったく、迷惑じゃないです」
lines.english: “...She hasn't been any trouble at all.”

lines.japanese: 「そう」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 感情の動きを察知させないイントネーションだった。
lines.english: Her intonation betrayed not the slightest flicker of emotion.

lines.japanese: 「もし困ったことがあったら、報告してね」
lines.english: “If you ever have any difficulties, be sure to report them to me.”

lines.japanese: 報告―――
lines.english: Report—

lines.japanese:
およそ親が娘のことを知る時に、用いる言葉だろ
うか。
lines.english: Was that a word a parent would use when asking about her own daughter?

lines.japanese: 「……今のところ、困っていることはありません」
lines.english: “...At present, I have no difficulties.”

lines.japanese:
「はじめて会ったときは多少、つっかかられました
　けど」
lines.english: “When we first met, she did pick a bit of a fight with me, but...”

lines.japanese: 女の目が光る。
lines.english: The woman's eyes flashed.

lines.japanese: 「……つっかかられた？」
lines.english: “...She picked a fight with you?”

lines.japanese: 即座に失言を悟る忍。
lines.english: Shinobu knew at once that he had misspoken.

lines.japanese:
「うちの子と最初に会ったのは、あなたが最初に通
　学する時だったわね」
lines.english: “The first time you met my daughter was on your first day going to school, wasn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「……通学中につっかかられたということ？」
lines.english: “...Are you saying she picked a fight with you on the way to school?”

lines.japanese:
あまり言及しない方が良い。
　そう判断した。
lines.english: It would be wiser not to say too much. That was his judgment.

lines.japanese: 「いえ、あの前に彼女とは一度会っていたんです」
lines.english: “No. I'd met her once before then.”

lines.japanese:
「ただもう記憶もほとんどないので……
　それにつっかかられたと言っても、何かされた
　わけではないんです」
lines.english: “I barely remember it anymore... And when I say she picked a fight, I don't mean she actually did anything to me.”

lines.japanese: 「そうね……ならいいのだけど」
lines.english: “I see... Then I suppose it's all right.”

lines.japanese: 「一度会っていた、というのは？」
lines.english: “What do you mean, you'd met once before?”

lines.japanese: 「草っぱらで……偶然」
lines.english: “In a field... By chance.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうだったの」
lines.english: “...I see.”

lines.japanese:
追及の意志が緩んだことが、調子から察せられた。
ほっとする。
lines.english: He heard the pressure ease from her tone. He felt relieved.

lines.japanese:
忍は得体の知れない感触に当惑していた。
　母親が娘の罪悪を掘り起こそうとしているのか？
lines.english: Shinobu was bewildered by an unnamable sensation. Was this mother trying to dig up some sin her daughter had committed?

lines.japanese: 確証も持てないまま、不安定に疑惑を持てあました。
lines.english: With no evidence to settle it, he did not know what to do with the suspicion.

lines.japanese:
その倫理的な問題が真実だとして、どういった感
情に結びつけていいのか判然としなかったからだ。
lines.english: Even if there really was something morally wrong here, he could not tell what he ought to feel about it.

lines.japanese: 「学校はどう？」
lines.english: “How is school?”

lines.japanese: 「だいぶ慣れました」
lines.english: “I've grown fairly used to it.”

lines.japanese: 「友達は？」
lines.english: “And friends?”

lines.japanese: 「……できました」
lines.english: “...I've made some.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、いいわね。男の子って」
lines.english: “I see. That's good. Boys...”

lines.japanese: あずさの母は微笑した。
lines.english: Azusa's mother smiled.

lines.japanese: 「そうですか？」
lines.english: “You think so?”

lines.japanese: 「もちろんそうよ。頼れるもの」
lines.english: “Of course. You can depend on them.”

lines.japanese: 「僕、まだ子供です」
lines.english: “I'm still a child.”

lines.japanese: 「いつか大人になるわ」
lines.english: “You'll grow up someday.”

lines.japanese:
穏和な言葉。
　若干の疲労が滲んでいる。だがそれだけではなか
った。
lines.english: Gentle words. A faint fatigue bled through them. But that was not all.

lines.japanese:
もう一種類だけ含まれた成分は、しかし忍には理
解しがたい深度を持っていた。
lines.english: There was one other element in her voice, but its depths were beyond Shinobu's understanding.

lines.japanese: （……なんだろう……これ……）
lines.english: (...What is this...?)

lines.japanese:
身体にまとわりつく、母親の視線。
　あずさの母親は長身だ。
　忍より高い。
lines.english: The mother's gaze clung to his body. Azusa's mother was tall. Taller than Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
視線は上から落ちてくる。
　見下すようであっても、おかしくはない。
　だが今の彼女の視線に蔑みはない。
lines.english: Her gaze descended from above. It could easily have seemed as though she were looking down on him. Yet there was no contempt in her eyes now.

lines.japanese: むしろ全面的な肯定、いや―――媚態。
lines.english: Rather, it was total affirmation—or no: seduction.

lines.japanese: （この人……）
lines.english: (This woman...)

lines.japanese:
細い体。
　モデルのような体系だが、少し痩せすぎではない
かと思える。
lines.english: A slender body. She had the figure of a model, though he thought she might be slightly too thin.

lines.japanese:
脂肪のクッションがない肉体は脆い。
　極度の痩躯に、綱渡りを見るにも似た危うさを感
じるのは、そんなためだろう。
lines.english: A body without a cushion of fat was fragile. Perhaps that was why her extreme thinness filled him with the same unease as watching a tightrope walker.

lines.japanese:
細い筋肉が肉体を覆っている。
　おそらくは軽く鍛えていたのだろう。そんな肉の
付き方だ。
lines.english: Fine muscle sheathed her frame. She had probably kept up some light training. Her build suggested as much.

lines.japanese:
しかし健康体というよりは、切羽詰まったような
体つきに見えた。
lines.english: Yet rather than health, her figure suggested a person driven to the brink.

lines.japanese:
娘を育てるということは、過大なストレスを生む
のかも知れない。
lines.english: Perhaps raising a daughter placed an excessive amount of stress on a person.

lines.japanese: 「寒いですね」
lines.english: “It's cold today.”

lines.japanese:
年上の女性から、熱っぽい視線を向けられて忍は
混乱した。
lines.english: The fevered gaze of an older woman had left Shinobu confused.

lines.japanese:
返答は直前の会話とは連結しない、いささか不自
然なものであった。
lines.english: His reply had nothing to do with what they had just been saying. It sounded a little awkward.

lines.japanese:
「そう？　私は暑いくらいなんだけれど……
　忍君も風邪を引いているのかしら？」
lines.english: “Is it? I feel almost too warm... Perhaps you're coming down with a cold as well?”

lines.japanese:
手が伸びてくる。
　忍は危機に直面したと感じた。
lines.english: A hand reached toward him. Shinobu felt himself confronted by danger.

lines.japanese: 寒気を払うかがり火。しかし触れれば炎にまみれる。
lines.english: A bonfire to drive off the cold. But touch it, and the flames would engulf him.

lines.japanese:
彼女がなぜ寒くないのか判明した。
　心としての密度が高く、圧縮されているため熱量
を有するのだ。
lines.english: He understood why she did not feel the cold. Her heart was compressed to such density that it possessed its own heat.

lines.japanese:
バイタリティ、と言い換えてもいいだろう。
　体つきに不釣り合いな、心。
　額に手が触れた。
lines.english: One might call it vitality. A heart out of all proportion to that body. Her hand touched his forehead.

lines.japanese:
平気のはずである。
　だとしても身が竦む。
　彼女が自分に危害を加えることはあり得ない。
lines.english: There ought to have been no danger. Even so, he froze. There was no possibility that she would harm him.

lines.japanese:
だとしてもその気になったら実現できるのだ。
　脳内、ストレス物質がどっと分泌されるのがわかる。
lines.english: Even so, if she chose to, she could. He could feel stress chemicals flooding his brain.

lines.japanese:
実銃を向けあって遊ぶようなものだ。たまったも
のではない。
lines.english: It was like a game in which they pointed real guns at each other. He couldn't stand it.

lines.japanese:
相手が突然狂って、引き金を動かしてしまう可能
性は０ではないのだ。
lines.english: The possibility that the other person might suddenly go mad and pull the trigger was not zero.

lines.japanese: 相手が突然狂う。
lines.english: The other person suddenly going mad.

lines.japanese:
そんな出来事が、いつ起きても不思議ではないの
が今の世だ。
lines.english: In the world as it was now, it would be no surprise if that happened at any moment.

lines.japanese:
やがて何事もなく手が離れた。
　おそろしく冷たい手だった。
　血流に不備でもあるのだろうか。
lines.english: Eventually her hand withdrew without incident. It had been frighteningly cold. Was there something wrong with her circulation?

lines.japanese: 過剰なダイエットの弊害としてそういう症状は聞く。
lines.english: He had heard of such symptoms as a consequence of excessive dieting.

lines.japanese:
かろうじて危険域の手前で踏みとどまる、低燃費
の肉体。
lines.english: A fuel-efficient body, barely holding itself short of the danger line.

lines.japanese: 「熱はないようね」
lines.english: “You don't seem to have a fever.”

lines.japanese:
遥か頭上から相聞歌のように声が降ってきた。
　あずさの母親はおそろしく長身なのだ。
lines.english: Her voice drifted down from far above like a verse exchanged between lovers. Azusa's mother was terrifyingly tall.

lines.japanese:
愛情。
　熱量。
　紅緒あずさ。
lines.english: Affection. Heat. Azusa Benio.

lines.japanese:
結びついて恐ろしくなった。
　この女性は、欠けている。
lines.english: Joined together, the three became terrifying. This woman was missing something.

lines.japanese: 「あの」
「なぁに？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese:
性的な優しい声。
　忍は迷う。
　問いかけていいものかどうか。
lines.english: A gentle, sensual voice. Shinobu hesitated. He did not know whether he should ask.

lines.japanese:
結果、あずさ自身にも余波が行くようなことにな
るのではないか。
lines.english: Might the fallout reach Azusa herself?

lines.japanese:
一瞬のうちに厳選した言葉を、体内から外に押し
出す。
lines.english: In that single instant, he chose his words with exquisite care and forced them out.

lines.japanese:
それは細部を気にするあまり、ややぎこちない問
いかけとなった。
lines.english: He had been so careful over the details that the question came out a little awkward.

lines.japanese: 「詳細は掴みきれていないんですが」
lines.english: “I don't yet have a complete grasp of the particulars, but...”

lines.japanese:
「……娘さんに少なからず虐待の痕跡があることを、
　ご存じですか？」
lines.english: “...Are you aware that your daughter bears more than a few signs of abuse?”

lines.japanese:
口にした瞬間、世界が塗り変わる。
　ぴしゃり、と空気が鳴る錯覚に満ちて。
lines.english: The instant he spoke, the world was painted over. The air seemed to crack like a slap.

lines.japanese: 「あの」

沈黙の刃が言葉を断ち切る。
　発言する気力さえ引き裂かれた。
lines.english: The blade of her silence severed his words. It tore away even his will to speak.

lines.japanese:
なぜあずさを短髪にさせているのか。
　なぜ厳しく躾るのに娘への迫害に無頓着なのか。
lines.english: Why did she make Azusa keep her hair short? Why, while disciplining her daughter so harshly, was she indifferent to the girl's persecution by others?

lines.japanese: 情緒が鈍い母親なのか。
lines.english: Was she simply emotionally insensitive?

lines.japanese: 違う。
lines.english: No.

lines.japanese:
理性が全力で否定する。
　目の前の鋭利な母親が、そんな可愛らしいもので
あるはずはない。
lines.english: His reason rejected the idea with all its strength. The keen-edged mother before him could not possibly be anything so innocuous.

lines.japanese:
焼けただれた鉈のような印象。
　ぞっとする。
　向けられる熱視線が焦げ臭いほどに感じられる。
lines.english: She gave the impression of a fire-scarred machete. A shudder ran through him. Her fevered gaze seemed hot enough to smell of scorching.

lines.japanese: 「私が娘を、見ていないとでも？」
lines.english: “Do you imagine I don't pay attention to my daughter?”

lines.japanese:
耳を澄まさねば聞き取れないほどの声量に、凶悪
な苛立ちが混ぜられていた。
lines.english: Her voice was so low he had to strain to hear it, yet vicious irritation ran through every syllable.

lines.japanese:
蛇には蛇なりの愛情がある。
　確かそれが、たった一つの情緒を司る細胞だけの
ものだったとしても。
lines.english: Even a serpent possesses a serpent's love. Even if that love resides in a single cell governing a single emotion.

lines.japanese:
この母親もまた、娘に関心を抱いている。
　自分がそうと信ずるやり方で。
lines.english: This mother, too, took an interest in her daughter. In the manner she believed was right.

lines.japanese:
だがやり方自体が歪んだものであったなら―――
その呪縛からあずさを救うには、途方もない時間と
手間が必要になる。
lines.english: But if the manner itself was warped— then freeing Azusa from its curse would demand an unimaginable amount of time and labor.

lines.japanese:
「私はいつだって、あの子のことを思っているわよ。
　あなたに言われるまでもなく」
lines.english: “I am always thinking of that girl. I hardly need you to tell me to.”

lines.japanese:
「だから忍君がわざわざあの子のことを心配する
　必要はないわね」
lines.english: “So there is no need for you to go out of your way to worry about her, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「しかし……」
「あの時だって―――」
lines.english: “Even then—”

lines.japanese: 眼光が力を増した。
lines.english: Her gaze intensified.

lines.japanese:
隠すことのない鋭い感情を露出し、水晶体が発熱
するかのように赤く熾る。
lines.english: Sharp emotion stood naked in her eyes, glowing red as though her lenses themselves were giving off heat.

lines.japanese:
強い。
　強い、眼差し。
　刃物。
lines.english: Powerful. A powerful gaze. A blade.

lines.japanese:
忍の心に突き刺さる。
　皮膚という絶縁効果の高い防壁を、それは易々と
突き抜けてくる。
lines.english: It drove into Shinobu's heart. It passed with ease through the highly insulating barrier of his skin.

lines.japanese:
人は向けられる憎悪を、強念を、感じ取ることが
できるのだから。
lines.english: For a person can sense hatred directed at him—can feel the force of another's will.

lines.japanese: 忍は限界を悟る。
lines.english: Shinobu knew he had reached his limit.

lines.japanese: 「あの子には、これ以上の心配は必要ないもの」
lines.english: “That girl needs no further concern.”

lines.japanese:
「そうでしょう？　もう充分に愛情を注いでいる。
　母子家庭でありながら、不自由にさせたことはな
　いわ」
lines.english: “Isn’t that so? I’ve already given her enough love. Though ours is a single-parent home, I have never allowed her to go without.”

lines.japanese:
「もちろん子供だから、生活に制限があるのは当然
　です。それはあなたの家もそうなのでしょう？」
lines.english: “Of course, she is a child, so restrictions on her life are only natural. The same is true in your home, isn't it?”

lines.japanese:
「私はあの子を一人でも生きていける人間に育てる
　義務があるの。それが親というものなの」
lines.english: “I have a duty to raise her into a person capable of surviving on her own. That is what it means to be a parent.”

lines.japanese:
「それでも誰にも誉められたりはしないわ。
　そして求めたりもしない」
lines.english: “And still, no one praises me for it. Not that I ask them to.”

lines.japanese:
「私の人生はあずさを育てるためにあるといっても
　いいし、疑ったことも不満に思ったこともありは
　しない」
lines.english: “You might say my life exists to raise Azusa, and I have never doubted that fact or felt dissatisfied with it for a moment.”

lines.japanese:
「……確かに、時には厳しく当たることもあるわ
　ね。だとしても必要なことなの」
lines.english: “...Certainly, there are times when I treat her harshly. Even so, it is necessary.”

lines.japanese:
「私はそれが親によるものである限り、体罰を躊躇う
　べきではないと考えているの」
lines.english: “I believe that so long as it comes from a parent, one should not hesitate to administer corporal punishment.”

lines.japanese:
「痛みのない教育なんてありはしないもの。時に鞭
　は必要だし、それを一様に虐待と区切ってしまう
　ことは間違っているわ」
lines.english: “There is no such thing as education without pain. Sometimes the rod is necessary, and it is wrong to label all such punishment abuse.”

lines.japanese:
「もし痛みを教えなかったら、口だけの教えで学ば
　せることができなかったら……大人になってから
　取り返しのつかない間違いをするかも知れない」
lines.english: “If a child is never taught pain—if words alone cannot make her learn... then she may grow up and make a mistake that can never be undone.”

lines.japanese:
「今、体罰に対して叫んでいる人たちはそういうこ
　とはまるで考えていない」
lines.english: “The people who make such a clamor over corporal punishment today never think of that at all.”

lines.japanese:
「とにかく最初に目に付いた虐待を撲滅させることに
　は熱心だけれど、それによって子供が適切な痛みを
　学ぶ機会を失う事については、まるで無頓着なの」
lines.english: “They rush to eradicate whatever abuse happens to catch their eye, yet remain utterly indifferent to the fact that this may deprive a child of the opportunity to learn an appropriate measure of pain.”

lines.japanese:
「だって仕方ないでしょう？　うちには父親がいな
　いのだから。片親なのだから。教育に不備が出る
　のも当然よ」
lines.english: “It cannot be helped, can it? There is no father in our home. I am raising her alone. Of course there will be deficiencies in her education.”

lines.japanese:
「それでも２４時間子供を見て、家事もこなして、
　生活費も稼げというの？」
lines.english: “And yet they expect me to watch a child around the clock, keep house, and earn our living as well?”

lines.japanese:
「物理的にできないことだってあるのに、彼らはそう
　いったことは見たがらないのね」
lines.english: “Some things are physically impossible, but those people would rather not see that.”

lines.japanese:
「ただ、世話が不十分であると言う。それが可能か
　どうかの背景も見ないで、なんとか悪い方向に結
　論づける」
lines.english: “They simply call the care inadequate. They refuse to look at whether adequate care was ever possible, then somehow contrive to reach a negative judgment.”

lines.japanese: 「うちには父親がいないことには触れないのね」
lines.english: “They never mention that there is no father in our home.”

lines.japanese:
「１０あったものが５になったのよ？　５でなんとか
　やりくりしないといけないのに。彼らは言うのね。
　あなたの教育には５の力が足りませんって」
lines.english: “We had ten, and now we have five. I have to make those five suffice. But then they tell me, Your parenting is five measures short.”

lines.japanese:
「良い夫がいれば工夫のしようもあったでしょうね。
　ただうちの人は、私たちのことを気味悪がってい
　たし、望むべくもない願いなのかしら？」
lines.english: “With a good husband, perhaps we could have found ways to manage. But mine found the two of us disturbing, so perhaps that was too much to wish for.”

lines.japanese:
「それでも生きていてくれる間は、経済的には困る
　ことはなかったのに」
lines.english: “Still, while he was alive, at least we had no financial difficulties.”

lines.japanese:
「私だって手に職があるから、今だって生活費くら
　いなら稼げるのよ。だけどね、子供の情操教育に
　全ての労力を割くことは難しいわ」
lines.english: “I have a trade of my own, so even now I can earn enough for our living expenses. But it is difficult to devote all my strength to cultivating a child's emotional life.”

lines.japanese:
「そこを責められても困るのよ。だったら、
　あなたが手伝ってくれない？　と言いたいわ」
lines.english: “I cannot accept being blamed for that. What I want to ask is— why don't you help me, then?”

lines.japanese:
「人の方法を糾弾するのだから、当然代案くらいは
　提示するべきでしょうに」
lines.english: “If they mean to condemn another person's methods, surely they ought at least to offer an alternative.”

lines.japanese:
「自分が責任持てないのだったら何も言うべきでは
　ないって、あなたにだってわかるでしょう？」
lines.english: “If you can’t take responsibility yourself, you shouldn’t say anything. You understand that too, don’t you?”

lines.japanese: 忍の返答を待たず、女はまくしたてる。
lines.english: Without waiting for Shinobu's answer, the woman rushed on.

lines.japanese:
「……でもこういう人たちはね、育ち損ねた子供が
　他人を傷つけた時には、こうも言うのよ」
lines.english: “...But when a child who has grown up wrong hurts another person, these same people will turn around and say this.”

lines.japanese:
「痛みを知らない子供の、心の闇が悲劇を生んだ……
　とね」
lines.english: “A tragedy was born from the darkness in the heart of a child who never knew pain... That is what they say.”

lines.japanese:
「右に行けば右に行ったことを叩く、左に行けば左
　に行ったと責める。まるで狂気の扇動者ね」
lines.english: “Go right and they attack you for going right; go left and they condemn you for going left. They are nothing but inciters of madness.”

lines.japanese:
「世の中はいつからこんな風になってしまったのか
　しら」
lines.english: “I wonder when the world became this way.”

lines.japanese:
「誰も責任を取るつもりはないくせに、人のするこ
　とには当然の権利とばかりにくちばしを突っ込み
　たがる」
lines.english: “None of them means to accept responsibility, yet they thrust their beaks into other people's affairs as though it were their natural right.”

lines.japanese:
「彼らは敵が欲しいのね。味方を率いて、勇ましく
　立ち向かいたいのよ。闘争心を制御できないの」
lines.english: “They want an enemy. They want to rally their allies and make a brave stand. They cannot control their appetite for conflict.”

lines.japanese:
「だから積極的にそれを見つけ出そうとする。大きな
　戦いのうねりに乗っていたいのよ」
lines.english: “So they actively seek an enemy out. They want to be swept along by the surge of some great battle.”

lines.japanese:
「そうして彼らは、私たちのような攻撃しやすい社
　会的弱者を狙うのね」
lines.english: “And so they take aim at the socially vulnerable—at people like us, who are easy to attack.”

lines.japanese:
「滑稽だと思わない。まるで麻薬だもの。社会的正
　義という気持ちよいうねりに乗りたい。そういう
　ことでしょう。怒ることは心地よいものね」
lines.english: “Don't you find it absurd? It's like a drug. They want to ride that pleasant swell called social justice. That's all it is. Anger feels good, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「他者を糾弾することは」
lines.english: “So does condemning someone else.”

lines.japanese:
「私の夫もそうだった。私のすることに対して自動
　的に罵りの言葉を吐いた。客観的な言葉じゃない、
　私のすること全てに難癖をつけた」
lines.english: “My husband was the same. He would spit abuse at everything I did as if by reflex. Nothing objective—he found fault with every single thing I did.”

lines.japanese:
「でも私たちはずっと我慢してきたわ。
　なぜかわかる？」
lines.english: “But we endured it all that time. Do you know why?”

lines.japanese:
「どんなに無関心であっても、いざという時に家の
　中に男性がいるのは心強いことだからよ」
lines.english: “Because no matter how indifferent he might be, in an emergency it is reassuring to have a man in the house.”

lines.japanese:
「あなたのお姉さんも同じ思いを抱いてらっしゃる
　んじゃない？」
lines.english: “Perhaps your sister feels the same way. Don't you think?”

lines.japanese:
「でもあなたのところはいいわ。忍くんという男の子
　がいるもの。
　今は若くても、いつか頼れるようになる」
lines.english: “But your household is fortunate. It has a boy named Shinobu in it. You may be young now, but one day they will be able to rely on you.”

lines.japanese:
「最初の子供は男の子が良かったの。子供を何人作っ
　たとしても、一番早く私を助けてくれる存在になっ
　てくれるから。夫よりも私についてくれるから」
lines.english: “I wanted my first child to be a boy. No matter how many children I had, he would be the first to grow into someone who could help me. And he would take my side over my husband's.”

lines.japanese:
「女の子はそういうところは駄目ね。私が厳しくす
　ると、怯えてしまうもの。夫にはそういう役目だ
　ってあるはずなのに、うちの人は何もしなかった」
lines.english: “Girls are no good that way. If I am stern, they grow frightened. That ought to have been one of my husband's roles, but my husband did nothing.”

lines.japanese:
「あずさに手を触れもしなかった。気味悪がっていた
　から。そんな義務を果たさない父親だから―――」
lines.english: “He never even touched Azusa. He found her disturbing. A father who would not fulfill even that duty—”

lines.japanese: だから―――
lines.english: Therefore—

lines.japanese:
続く言葉を予測して、身が竦む。
　しかしギロチンは落とされず、忍は居心地の悪い
瞬間に捨て置かれた。
lines.english: Anticipating what would come next, Shinobu froze. But the guillotine did not fall, leaving him stranded in the discomfort of that suspended moment.

lines.japanese:
「……あなたに話すようなことではなかったかしら。
　ごめんなさいね」
lines.english: “...Perhaps this wasn't something I should have told you. I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ」
lines.english: “It's all right.”

lines.japanese: 切れ切れの声で、そう応じるだけが精一杯だった。
lines.english: That broken reply was all he could manage.

lines.japanese:
「別にあなたを非難したいわけじゃないの。私はあ
　なたのこと好きだもの。だからこそ、あなたには
　私の教育について悪く思って欲しくはないのよ」
lines.english: “I don't mean to criticize you. I like you, you know. That is precisely why I don't want you to think poorly of the way I educate my daughter.”

lines.japanese:
“好き”という言葉が、特に濃密に発音された気
がした。
lines.english: The word ‘like’ seemed to be pronounced with particular intensity.

lines.japanese: 血の気が引いて、視野全体がうっすらと青ざめる。
lines.english: The blood drained away, and his entire field of vision took on a pale blue cast.

lines.japanese: 「普段は、こんなんじゃないのよ？」
lines.english: “I'm not usually like this, you know?”

lines.japanese:
しかしその微笑みは、いかなる怒気よりも凄みを
持っている。
lines.english: Yet her smile carried more menace than any display of anger could have done.

lines.japanese:
忍はもう対峙する気力を失っていた。
　一刻も早く、相手を刺激しないようにこの場を離
れたい。
lines.english: Shinobu no longer had the strength to face her. He wanted to leave at once, without doing anything that might provoke her.

lines.japanese:
タイミングをはかっていた。
　大砲の前に立っている気分だ。
　いつ発射されるかわからない。
lines.english: He watched for his chance. He felt as though he stood before a cannon. He did not know when it might fire.

lines.japanese:
幾度となく首肯し、理解もできずに肯定し、やが
ていても立っても居られなくなる。
lines.english: He nodded again and again, agreeing without understanding, until he could no longer bear to stay.

lines.japanese: やや唐突に、
lines.english: Rather abruptly—

lines.japanese: 「いってきます」
lines.english: “I'm off, then.”

lines.japanese: しかしあずさの母は変化を見せず、
lines.english: But Azusa's mother showed no change.

lines.japanese: 「今度遊びに来てね」
lines.english: “Come and visit us sometime.”

lines.japanese:
駆け出さないよう、全力で自分を押さえつけて、
忍はその場を離れる。
lines.english: Using all his strength to keep himself from breaking into a run, Shinobu left her behind.

lines.japanese:
突然、背後から抱きしめられそうな気がした。
　想像だけで、首筋が総毛立つ。
lines.english: He had the sudden feeling that she might embrace him from behind. The thought alone made every hair on his neck stand on end.

lines.japanese:
子供でもいいのだ。
　そう。
　子供でもいいのだ。彼女は。
lines.english: A child would do. Yes. For her, even a child would do.

lines.japanese:
男であれば。
　あずさの母親に足りていないのは父性なのだから。
lines.english: So long as it was male. What Azusa's mother lacked was fatherhood.

lines.japanese:
父性―――いや、違う。
　男性そのもの。
lines.english: Fatherhood—no, that was wrong. A man himself.

lines.japanese:
彼女はそれを得てはじめて成立する。
　だが無論、本命は夫であり恋人であり愛人である
はずだ。
lines.english: Only by possessing one could she become whole. But naturally, the true object must be a husband, a lover, a paramour— someone of that kind.

lines.japanese:
対等に対になっている誰かであるはずだ。
　そして、
　紅緒家は母子家庭なのである。
lines.english: Someone paired with her as an equal. And yet— the Benio household was a mother-and-daughter home.

lines.japanese: 「今日も休み？」
lines.english: “Staying home again today?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ごめん……」
lines.english: “Yeah. Sorry...”

lines.japanese: 扉の向こうから、あずさの声だけがする。
lines.english: Only Azusa's voice came from beyond the door.

lines.japanese:
一センチも開いていない扉の向こうに、見慣れた
前髪がかすかに露出していた。
lines.english: The door wasn't even a centimeter ajar, but through the gap he could just make out a familiar fringe of hair.

lines.japanese:
しかし顔は見えない。
　見せようとしない。
lines.english: But he could not see her face. She was making sure he couldn't.
“...A cold?”
“Y-yeah...”

lines.japanese:
「心配だなぁ。別に声は変わっていないようだけど
　……他にはどこがひどいの？」
lines.english: “I’m worried. Your voice doesn’t sound any different, though… What else is bothering you?”

lines.japanese: 「え、えーと……頭痛とか……いろいろ」
lines.english: “U-umm... My head hurts, and... stuff.”

lines.japanese:
腑に落ちないためらいを感じた。
　昨日今日のつきあいではない。
　いつも隣にいたのだ。
lines.english: He heard a hesitation that didn't sit right. They had known each other far longer than a day or two. She had always been beside him.

lines.japanese:
機微だって読める。
　あずさが隠し事をしている気がしてならない。
　それはほとんど確信に近い。
lines.english: He could read the smallest shifts in her mood. He couldn't shake the feeling that Azusa was hiding something. He was almost certain.

lines.japanese: 近いのだが、押し切るほどのものでもない。
lines.english: Almost—but not enough to press the matter.

lines.japanese: 「わかったよ。じゃ今日は僕らだけで行くさ」
lines.english: “All right. We'll go without you today.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんね……」
lines.english: “I'm sorry...”

lines.japanese:
「顔だけ見せてくれる？
　なんとなく落ち着かないから」
lines.english: “Will you at least let me see your face? I just feel a little uneasy.”

lines.japanese: 向こう側で、あずさは呻いた。
lines.english: Beyond the door, Azusa groaned.

lines.japanese: 「……ごめん、無理」
lines.english: “...Sorry. I can't.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese:
「……ちょっとひどい顔してるから……
　見られたくない。恥ずかちい」
lines.english: “...My face looks kinda awful right now... I don't want you to see. It's embawassing.”

lines.japanese:
「扁桃腺が腫れてるの？
　それって医者に行ってる？」
lines.english: “Are your tonsils swollen? Have you seen a doctor?”

lines.japanese:
「ううん、そういうのとは違う。大丈夫。
　いつもすぐに戻るから」
lines.english: “No, it's not that kind of thing. I'm fine. It always goes back to normal real quick.”

lines.japanese:
「……ただちょっと今回はひどいっぽいので……
　ごめん」
lines.english: “...It just seems a little worse this time... Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「仕方ないね……」
lines.english: “I suppose it can't be helped...”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ帰り、お見舞いとかは？」
lines.english: “Should I come check on you after school?”

lines.japanese: 「やめといた方がいい？」
lines.english: “Better not?”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさい……」
lines.english: “I'm sorry...”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ、仕方ない」
lines.english: “It's all right. It can't be helped.”

lines.japanese:
「じゃせめてしっかり休んで、早く元気になっても
　らおうかな」
lines.english: “Then at least get plenty of rest, so you can hurry up and get well again.”

lines.japanese: あずさは少しだけ元気そうな声を出した。
lines.english: Azusa sounded a little livelier.

lines.japanese: 「うんっ」
lines.english: “Okay!”

lines.japanese: 「まずそうだったら医者に行くんだよ？」
lines.english: “If it starts looking bad, go see a doctor, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「あい」
lines.english: “'Kay.”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫かなぁ～？」
lines.english: “Will you really be okay?”

lines.japanese:
「へいきへいき。ヤバかったら行くってば！　ほら、
　遅刻しちゃうから忍くんもう行った方がいいよ」
lines.english: “I'm fine, I'm fine. If it gets really bad, I'll go! Now come on, you'd better leave or you'll be late.”

lines.japanese: 「……んー、わかった。じゃまた」
lines.english: “...Mm. All right. See you.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、明日かあさってか……また」
lines.english: “Yeah. Tomorrow, or the day after... See you.”

lines.japanese:
紅緒家の玄関を出る。
　一度だけ扉を見やる。
lines.english: He left the Benio house. He glanced back at the door just once.

lines.japanese: 「……風邪ね」
lines.english: “...A cold, huh.”

lines.japanese: 呟き、いつもの通学路を歩み出した。
lines.english: He murmured the words and set out along his usual route to school.

lines.japanese:
玄関脇の壁に寄りかかって、幼い忍があずさを待
っている。
lines.english: Young Shinobu leaned against the wall beside the front entrance, waiting for Azusa.

lines.japanese:
二人の交友がはじまって、だいぶ時は流れた。
　友達と一緒にいる空気にも、少し慣れた。
　少しだ。
lines.english: Much time had passed since their friendship began. He had grown a little more accustomed to what it felt like to be with a friend. A little.

lines.japanese:
軽い緊張と戸惑いは、なかなか剥離していかない。
　今まで人とは、事務的に付き合ってきた。
　以外の生き方を知らなかった忍だった。
lines.english: A slight tension and uncertainty stubbornly refused to fall away. Until now, his dealings with people had been strictly impersonal. Shinobu knew no other way to live.

lines.japanese:
無味無臭、歓喜のともなわない生。
　赤子の頃、無意識に発散する原感情でしかないと
思っていた。
lines.english: A life without taste or scent, untouched by joy. He had thought joy no more than a primal emotion vented without thought in infancy.

lines.japanese:
人付き合いの難しさを、忍は実感している。
　やがて隣家の門が軋んだ音を立てて開き、少女が
ひょこひょこと出てきた。
lines.english: Shinobu was beginning to grasp how difficult human company could be. Before long, the neighboring gate creaked open, and a girl came bobbing out.
“...Here I am.”

lines.japanese: 目線を合わせない挨拶をかわし、二人は歩き出す。
lines.english: They exchanged greetings without meeting each other's eyes, then began to walk.
“...Hand.”

lines.japanese: ぎこちなく指を絡ませる。
lines.english: Their fingers intertwined awkwardly.

lines.japanese:
手と手が組み合わない、それはまったく拙劣な握
手だった。
lines.english: Their hands would not fit together; it was an utterly inept handshake.

lines.japanese:
不格好で不器用で、親愛をないがしろにしてしま
うような、接続だった。
lines.english: An awkward, ungainly connection, as though the affection behind it hardly mattered.

lines.japanese:
だとしても友人なのだから、手を繋がねばならな
いのだ。
lines.english: Even so, they were friends, and friends were supposed to hold hands.

lines.japanese: しかし二人にとって、これ以上の譲歩はありえない。
lines.english: Neither of them could concede any more than this.

lines.japanese:
もっと深く繋ごうと甘えた方が負けだ。
　勝ち負けの概念が支配する。
　理由を、幼い二人は考えたこともない。
lines.english: Whoever showed a need for a closer bond would lose. The notion of victory and defeat ruled them. The two children had never considered why.

lines.japanese:
それは苦痛を回避するためだ。
　歩み寄って拒絶される傷みを、二人は知っている。
　忍は知識で身につけた。
lines.english: It was a means of avoiding pain. Both knew the hurt of reaching out only to be rejected. Shinobu had learned it in theory.

lines.japanese:
あずさは経験で身につけた。
　他者は暴君。
　思うままに攻撃を仕掛けてくる。
lines.english: Azusa had learned it firsthand. Other people were tyrants. They attacked whenever the whim took them.

lines.japanese: 体が痛いばかりか、心にも痛烈な一撃を加えてくる。
lines.english: They hurt the body and struck cruel blows against the heart as well.

lines.japanese:
他者とは皆そうだ。
　悲鳴をあげても効果はない。
　叩かれるか、個室に隔離されるだけだ。
lines.english: All other people were the same. Screaming did no good. It only got you hit, or shut away in a room by yourself.

lines.japanese:
だから黙る。
　無表情になる。
　話さない。
lines.english: And so you kept silent. Let your face go blank. Did not speak.

lines.japanese:
過剰に攻撃的になれば、出る杭だ。
　打たれる。
　一度マークされたら終わりだ。
lines.english: Grow too aggressive and you were the nail that stuck up. You got hammered down. Once they marked you, it was over.

lines.japanese:
虎視眈々と狙われる。
　他者は甘い顔を見せることもある。
lines.english: They watched for their chance to strike. Sometimes other people showed you a kindly face.

lines.japanese:
うかうかと近づけば、それが罠であることを身と
魂をもって知ることになる。
lines.english: Let your guard down and venture closer, and you would learn in body and soul that it was a trap.

lines.japanese:
エディプス期を脱した子供が、最初に学ぶのは疎
外と反感と侮蔑……他者性なのである。
lines.english: The first things a child learns upon leaving the Oedipal stage are alienation, hostility, contempt—in short, otherness.

lines.japanese: 二人は互いに警戒している。
lines.english: The two were wary of each other.

lines.japanese:
友人ではある。
　だが警戒している。
　信じ切れていない。
lines.english: They were friends. But they were wary. Neither could trust the other completely.

lines.japanese:
人付き合いなんてごめんだと思っている。
　だがまだ、完全には捨てきれない。
　嫌だ嫌だと思いつつ、これが最後と手を伸ばす。
lines.english: They wanted nothing to do with human company. Yet they could not abandon it entirely. Hating it, dreading it, they reached out again as if for the last time.

lines.japanese: その結実が、忍とあずさの二人である。
lines.english: The fruit of those efforts was the pair of them: Shinobu and Azusa.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ」

lines.english: “Mm?”

lines.japanese: 「今日学校で、けっとばされた」
lines.english: “I got kicked at school today.”

lines.japanese: 「そう」
lines.english: “I see.”
“...Are you hurt?”

lines.japanese: 「してない」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「ならいい」
lines.english: “Then it's fine.”
“Yeah...”

lines.japanese:
強ばった会話。
　仲睦まじいとは、お世辞にも言えないだろう。
　だが必要だった―――
lines.english: A rigid conversation. No one could have called them affectionate, however charitable. But this was necessary—

lines.japanese:
二人の遊びは笑顔のともなわないものだ。
　いや、遊びでさえない。
　楽しむ余地もない。遅れていた二人だ。
lines.english: There were no smiles in their play. No—it was not even play. There was no room for enjoyment. They had both fallen behind.

lines.japanese: 面して、触れて、語ることに没頭するしかなかった。
lines.english: All they could do was devote themselves to facing one another, touching, and speaking.

lines.japanese:
からっぽの肺に、大慌てで新鮮な空気を取り入れ
るように。
lines.english: Like empty lungs frantically drawing in fresh air.

lines.japanese: 「……おかあさんは、おかあさんだから」
lines.english: “...Mom's my mom, so...”

lines.japanese: 母性について、あずさは肯定した。
lines.english: Azusa affirmed motherhood itself.

lines.japanese:
逆らうという選択肢があるなんて、思ってもみな
かった。
lines.english: It had never occurred to her that defiance might be an option.

lines.japanese:
「私設に子供はたくさんいた。親のいない子供ばか
　り。その中で、僕は一番可愛がられてた。だから、
　仲間には嫌われてた」
lines.english: “There were lots of children at the institution. None of them had parents. I was the one they doted on most. That's why the other children hated me.”

lines.japanese:
優遇されていたと忍は言った。
　幼い彼は無知のあまり、正反対の理解しか持ち得
なかった。
lines.english: Shinobu said he had been favored. In his childish ignorance, he could only understand it as the precise opposite of the truth.

lines.japanese:
「お父さんは家を出て行ったんだよ。だから、お母
　さんは仕事に戻らないといけなくなったんだって」
lines.english: “My dad left home. That's why Mom had to go back to work, she said.”

lines.japanese:
「あたし、お父さんの顔は知らない。お父さんって
　言葉も、ずっと知らなかった。きいても、おこら
　れた。だからよくわかんない……お父さんって」
lines.english: “I don't know what my dad looks like. For a long time, I didn't even know the word ‘dad.’ If I asked, Mom got mad. So I don't really understand... what a dad is.”

lines.japanese:
先天的な欠損を、独力で自覚することは難しい。
　人に接し自らと比較して、はじめて違いを認識で
きる。
lines.english: It is difficult to recognize an inborn absence on one's own. Only through meeting others and comparing oneself to them can a person perceive the difference.

lines.japanese:
そしてたいていは、当事者を嫌な気分にさせるも
のだ。あずさもそうだった。
lines.english: And in most cases, that realization is an unpleasant one for the person concerned. So it was for Azusa.

lines.japanese:
「引っ越してきてから、はじめてちゃんとした一人
　部屋もらったんだ。でも、どうしていいのかぜん
　ぜんわからなくて……何もないんだ」
lines.english: “I didn't get a real room of my own until I moved here. But I have no idea what I'm supposed to do with it... There's nothing in it.”

lines.japanese:
どこまでを自分のものとしていいのかは、難しい
問題だ。
lines.english: Where to draw the boundary of what one may call one's own is a difficult problem.

lines.japanese:
その線引きにはおおむね倫理が用いられる。
　貴宮忍はいまだ倫理を持たない。
lines.english: That boundary is generally drawn by ethics. Shinobu Atemiya did not yet possess any.

lines.japanese:
少しずつ。
　少しずつ。
　互いを語る言葉は、深みを帯びていった。
lines.english: Little by little. Little by little. What they told each other grew deeper.

lines.japanese:
談笑のない、禅問答のような語らい。
　互いに異性として認識できる年齢であったなら、
また違ったアプローチへと変化したのかも知れない。
lines.english: A conversation without laughter, like a Zen dialogue. Had they been old enough to be conscious of each other as the opposite sex, their approach might have taken some different form.

lines.japanese:
二人で閉じる方法は、異性間では一つしかないた
めだ。
lines.english: For members of opposite sexes, there was only one way to seal themselves off together.

lines.japanese:
未分化の時期であったからこそ、二人は交友を成
立させることができた。
lines.english: Only because they had not yet differentiated in that way could the two establish a friendship.

lines.japanese:
当時、二人はまだ聖域を持たなかった。
　語らう場所は、その都度変わった。
lines.english: In those days, they did not yet possess a sanctuary. The place where they talked changed each time.

lines.japanese:
たいていはあの草原だったが、時には忍の部屋だ
ったり、校庭だったりした。
lines.english: Usually it was that field, but sometimes it was Shinobu's room or the schoolyard.

lines.japanese:
人間関係は場の強度に支援される。
　学校。職場。サークル。
lines.english: Human relationships are sustained by the strength of a place. School. The workplace. A club.

lines.japanese:
ある特定のベクトルのもとに集い、場所的な承認
を付与されて、堅牢なものとなる。
lines.english: People gather beneath a particular vector, and the sanction of place makes their connection firm.

lines.japanese: だから二人の日々は、脆く不安定なものだと言えた。
lines.english: Thus the days the two shared could be called fragile and unstable.

lines.japanese: そんな時期、忍はあずさと母に触れた。
lines.english: It was during that time that Shinobu came into contact with Azusa and her mother.

lines.japanese:
母親が不在であることをあずさが告げた。
　忍はあずさの部屋を見たいと告げた。
lines.english: Azusa told him her mother was away. Shinobu told her he wanted to see her room.

lines.japanese:
あずさは少しためらってから、申し出を承諾した。
　そして忍は紅緒家の敷居を踏んだ。
lines.english: After some hesitation, Azusa agreed to his request. And Shinobu crossed the threshold of the Benio home.

lines.japanese: ―――あずさの母がいた。
lines.english: —Azusa's mother was there.

lines.japanese: 「あら、忍君？」
lines.english: “Oh, Shinobu?”

lines.japanese:
あずさがドアを開けると、腕を組んで立っていた。
　あずさは凍り付いた。
lines.english: When Azusa opened the door, her mother stood there with folded arms. Azusa froze.

lines.japanese:
「まあ、遊びに来てくれたのね。でも、ごめんな
　さい」
lines.english: “Oh, you’ve come to visit. I’m sorry, though.”

lines.japanese:
柔和な表情だった。
　近所で評判通りの顔だった。
　女手一つで娘を育てる、立派な女性―――
lines.english: Her expression was gentle. It was the face the neighborhood knew and praised. An admirable woman raising her daughter alone—

lines.japanese:
清潔な家。
　高収入。
　人格。
lines.english: A spotless house. A high income. Character.

lines.japanese:
非の打ち所のない。
　ただ一つの欠落。
lines.english: Beyond reproach. One thing alone was missing.

lines.japanese:
夫。
　あるいは男。
lines.english: A husband. Or a man.

lines.japanese: 配偶者のいるべき場所が、どの程度欠けているのか。
lines.english: How much of a void did a missing spouse leave?

lines.japanese:
外から見てわかることではない。
　形のあるものではない。
　愛し合ってないのに仲睦まじい夫婦がいる。
lines.english: You could not judge it from outside. It had no visible form. Some couples were affectionate without loving each other.

lines.japanese:
素っ気なくも深く繋がった恋人がいる。
　美しい花がある。花の美しさという様なものはない。
lines.english: Some lovers seemed distant yet were bound together at the deepest level. Beautiful flowers exist. There is no such thing as the beauty of flowers.

lines.japanese:
忍は身じろぎできなかった。
　あずさは停止していた。
　無数にエラーを吐き出しているのはわかった。
lines.english: Shinobu could not move. Azusa had shut down. He could tell that she was throwing error after error.

lines.japanese:
目の前にあるあずさの後頭部が、微動だにしない
のが不気味だった。
lines.english: The back of Azusa's head before him did not stir by so much as a hair, and the stillness was uncanny.

lines.japanese: 「あずさ、今日は家にいる日だったでしょう？」
lines.english: “Azusa, today was a day you were meant to stay at home, wasn't it?”

lines.japanese:
「約束を破るような子に育てたつもりはないのよ、
　あずさ？」
lines.english: “I don't remember raising a child who breaks her promises, Azusa.”

lines.japanese:
気付いてしまった。
　母の視線は、あずさを見ていない。
lines.english: He realized it. Her mother wasn't looking at Azusa.

lines.japanese:
少しずれて上方、子供二人の頭上のあたりを、ま
るでそこに何かに話しかけるように射抜いていた。
lines.english: Her gaze pierced a point just above them, somewhere over the children's heads, as though she were addressing something there.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさいね、忍君。あずさがいけないのよ」
lines.english: “I'm sorry, Shinobu. Azusa is at fault.”

lines.japanese:
先ほどから、あずさの母親はまばたき一つしてい
ない。
lines.english: Azusa's mother had not blinked once this entire time.

lines.japanese:
煌々と輝く瞳が、なぜか空洞のようだった。
　化粧がムラになって、地肌が透けている部分がある。
lines.english: For all their brilliant shine, her eyes somehow resembled empty sockets. Her makeup lay unevenly, revealing patches of bare skin.

lines.japanese:
頬の奥に空洞があるマネキンとしか形容できない。
　他にはおかしな部分はない。
lines.english: She could only be described as a mannequin with hollows behind its cheeks. Nothing else about her was strange.

lines.japanese:
ほんの少しの表面の乱れと、強靱な意志力で凝固
させられた表情。
lines.english: The faintest disturbance on the surface, and an expression frozen solid by sheer force of will.

lines.japanese: 結果、形容のできない破壊がそこに起こっていた。
lines.english: The result was an indescribable devastation.

lines.japanese: こんな異様で凄惨な概念を忍は知らない。
lines.english: Shinobu had never conceived of anything so grotesque and horrific.

lines.japanese: 「約束を破って、男と遊ぶだなんて」
lines.english: “Breaking your promise so you can play with a man.”

lines.japanese:
虚空を戒める視線が、二人の頭上に火球となって
いく。
lines.english: The gaze that chastised empty air gathered into a ball of flame above their heads.

lines.japanese: 熱。
lines.english: Heat.

lines.japanese:
忍は自分が嫌な汗をかいていることに気付いた。
　熱波が向けられていたためだ。
　竦みあがる。
lines.english: Shinobu realized he had broken out in a clammy sweat. A wave of heat was bearing down on him. He cowered.

lines.japanese:
矮小な精神が、警報を発している。
　戒めの鎖を引きちぎり、全てを終わらせたく
なる―――
lines.english: His petty mind sounded an alarm. He wanted to tear apart the chains of restraint and bring everything to an end—

lines.japanese:
できもしないことだ。
　甘んじて、立ち尽くすしかない。
lines.english: An impossibility. He could only submit and stand rooted to the spot.

lines.japanese:
「最近、お洋服を汚さなくなったと思ったら、男に
　頼っていたのね」
lines.english: “I wondered why you'd stopped dirtying your clothes lately. So you'd been relying on a man.”

lines.japanese: あずさの肩が、哀れなほど過敏に震えた。
lines.english: Azusa’s shoulders trembled with a sensitivity that was pitiful to see.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさいね、忍君」
lines.english: “I'm sorry, Shinobu.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese:
それでも他人事だと考えていた。
　彼女はあずさを非難しているのだと。
　そうではなかった。
lines.english: Even then, he had believed this did not concern him. That the woman was condemning Azusa. He was wrong.

lines.japanese:
彼女が発する熱は、個を超えた『何か』を焙るた
めのものだ。
lines.english: The heat she gave off was meant to scorch some ‘thing’ beyond the individual.

lines.japanese:
パチ、という音を忍は幻聴のうちに聞いた。
　爆ぜる音ではないか。
　可燃物一つない冷えた空間に響く。
lines.english: Shinobu heard an imagined snap. Was that the sound of something crackling? It echoed through the cold space, though there was nothing there to burn.

lines.japanese: 「本当に、ごめんなさいね、忍君」
lines.english: “I truly am sorry, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese:
燃える。
　どこかでなにかが燃えている。
lines.english: Burning. Something was burning somewhere.
(This... woman...)

lines.japanese: 知覚を失う。
lines.english: His senses failed him.

lines.japanese:
いつの間にか、だらりと垂れ下がった母親の両腕
が、あずさに絡みついていた。
lines.english: At some point, the mother's arms, hanging limp at her sides, had coiled themselves around Azusa.

lines.japanese:
あずさは魂の抜けた顔を、忍に向けている。
　母親が娘を抱きかかえている。それだけだ。
　後ずさりする。
lines.english: Azusa turned a soulless face toward Shinobu. A mother was holding her daughter. Nothing more. He backed away.

lines.japanese:
あずさのそばを、離れてはいけないと思う。
　離脱してはいけないと理解している。
lines.english: He thought he must not leave Azusa's side. He understood that he must not retreat.

lines.japanese:
心を包む無数の皮膜が、炎でセルロイドのように
融けおちていった。
lines.english: The countless membranes around his heart melted away in the flames like celluloid.

lines.japanese:
熱の当たった箇所がぺろりとむけ、その下の皮膜
も同様にして黒縁の花弁を開き、延々と―――
　紫色の煙をたちのぼらせて、忍の防備を焼き払う。
lines.english: Where the heat struck, a layer peeled back; the membrane below it likewise opened into black-edged petals, one after another, endlessly— violet smoke streaming upward as the fire burned away Shinobu's defenses.

lines.japanese:
言葉が制御できなくなっている。
　意識せず体が動く。自立的な防御としての、後退。
　この感情を、恐怖という。
lines.english: He had lost control of his words. His body moved without conscious thought: a retreat, an autonomous defense. The name of this emotion was fear.

lines.japanese: 「お姉さんに、よろしくね、忍君」
lines.english: “Give my regards to your sister, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 扉が閉まっていく。
lines.english: The door began to close.

lines.japanese:
遮断される直前、母親の髪がどっと爆発的に膨れ
て茨状にあずさに絡みつく幻影が、網膜に投射された。
lines.english: Just before the door cut off his view, an image was projected onto his retinas: the mother's hair exploding outward into a mass of thorns that coiled around Azusa.

lines.japanese: 何か叫んで、忍は目を覆う。
lines.english: Shinobu shouted something and covered his eyes.

lines.japanese:
体は眠ったままである。
　心だけが、目覚めた。
　周囲から物音が聞こえたせいだ。
lines.english: His body remained asleep. Only his mind awoke. He had heard something nearby.

lines.japanese: 「あったあった……」
lines.english: “Found it, found it…”

lines.japanese: （今の……声……あずさ？）
lines.english: (That voice… Azusa?)

lines.japanese: 体がなぜか動かない。
lines.english: For some reason, his body would not move.

lines.japanese:
完全には閉じていないまぶたの隙間、見慣れた制
服が左右に動いている。
lines.english: His eyelids weren’t quite closed. Through the gap, he saw a familiar uniform moving back and forth.

lines.japanese: （あずさの動き方だ……）
lines.english: (That's the way Azusa moves…)

lines.japanese: 少し、微笑ましく思う忍。
lines.english: Shinobu found the sight faintly endearing.

lines.japanese: （なにしてんのかな……忙しそうに）
lines.english: (What's she doing…? She looks busy.)

lines.japanese:
声も出ないし目も開けない。
　霞みかかった意識が、ぼんやりとあずさに注がれる。
lines.english: He could neither speak nor open his eyes. His fogged consciousness drifted toward Azusa.

lines.japanese: 「よかった、ちゃんと凍ってる……さすが」
lines.english: “Good, it’s frozen solid… Nice.”

lines.japanese:
何かがさごそと用意しているらしい。
　視界外。
lines.english: There was a rustling sound as she seemed to prepare something. Out of sight.

lines.japanese:
やがてぱたぱたと足音がして、わずかな隙間をあ
ずさが埋めた。
lines.english: Before long, light footsteps pattered back, and Azusa filled the narrow slit of his vision.

lines.japanese: （目の前に……立ってる？）
lines.english: (Is she… standing in front of me?)

lines.japanese: 「忍くん……」
lines.english: “Shinobu…”

lines.japanese:
返事はできない。
　かすかにまつ毛が震えたが、肉体が目覚めるには
至らない。
lines.english: He could not answer. His eyelashes trembled faintly, but not enough to wake his body.

lines.japanese:
（これ、あれか……
　金縛りの物理的原因とかいう……）
lines.english: (Wasn't this… what they called the physical cause of sleep paralysis…?)

lines.japanese: （体だけ眠っていて動けないってこと……か）
lines.english: (My body is still asleep, so I can't move…?)

lines.japanese: 「すごい汗……うわぁ、熱い……」
lines.english: “You're drenched… Whoa, you're burning up…”

lines.japanese: 額をぬぐう冷水で搾ったタオルが心地よい。
lines.english: The towel she’d wrung out in cold water felt wonderful as she wiped his brow.

lines.japanese:
「確かこういうときは……
　水飲ませて、冷やせば、いいんだよね……」
lines.english: “If I remember right, at times like this… you give them water and keep them cool…”

lines.japanese:
汗をたんねんにぬぐってから、折りたたんだタオ
ルを額に置いた。
lines.english: After carefully wiping away his sweat, she folded the towel and laid it across his forehead.

lines.japanese: そして再び、視界の外に。
lines.english: Then she slipped out of sight again.
“Okay—”

lines.japanese:
すぐに戻ってくる。
　小型の氷まくらと、吸い飲みを持ってきたようだ。
lines.english: She was back in moments. It looked as though she'd brought a small ice pillow and a feeding cup.

lines.japanese:
（……おお……
　なんかあずさがしっかり者になってる……）
lines.english: (…Whoa… Look at Azusa being all dependable…)

lines.japanese: 「水……飲むかな」
lines.english: “Think he'll drink some water…?”

lines.japanese:
忍の口元に、筒先を添えた。
　傾けると、熱い口内に冷水が注がれた。
lines.english: She set the spout to Shinobu's lips. When she tipped it, cold water flowed into his burning mouth.
“Mm… mmm…”

lines.japanese: 体が自然と水を求めた。
lines.english: His body craved the water instinctively.

lines.japanese:
（……うまい……
　水の味を感じるくらいに……うまい）
lines.english: (…So good… So good I can taste the water itself…)

lines.japanese: 「わっ、飲んでる飲んでる。んくんく言ってる」
lines.english: “Oh! He's drinking, he's drinking. He's going glug, glug.”

lines.japanese: （んくんくとか言ってない……）
lines.english: (I am not going glug, glug…)

lines.japanese: あずさはくすくす笑う。
lines.english: Azusa giggled.

lines.japanese: 「可愛い……」
lines.english: “Cute…”
(…Ouch…)

lines.japanese: 吸い飲みはすぐに空になる。
lines.english: The feeding cup emptied in no time.

lines.japanese: 「まだ飲むかな」
lines.english: “Think he wants more?”

lines.japanese: （飲みたい……）
lines.english: (I do…)

lines.japanese: （いいや、起きよう―――）
lines.english: (No. Time to wake up—)

lines.japanese:
忍の瞳が開いた。
　あずさは少し驚いたが、すぐにあたたかな笑み。
lines.english: Shinobu opened his eyes. Azusa looked startled for a moment, then smiled warmly.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「おはよう、あずさ」
lines.english: “Good morning, Azusa.”

lines.japanese:
身を起こす。
　世界は垂直になった。
lines.english: He sat up. The world swung upright.

lines.japanese: （頭、まだ痛いけど……まあ平気か……）
lines.english: (My head still hurts… but I think I'm all right…)

lines.japanese: 「学校の帰り？」
lines.english: “On your way home from school?”

lines.japanese: 「……うん、そうかな」
lines.english: “…Yeah. I suppose so.”

lines.japanese: 「ふわぁ」
lines.english: “Hwaaah.”

lines.japanese: 欠伸。
lines.english: A yawn.

lines.japanese: 「家に行ってもいなかったから、捜してたんだ」
lines.english: “You weren't home, so I went looking for you.”

lines.japanese: 「……学校に来てくれれば良かったのに」
lines.english: “…You could've come to school.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、学校にいたんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, so you were at school.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃ、サボるわけにいかないからねぇ」
lines.english: “Well, yeah. It's not like I can skip.”

lines.japanese: 「ところで！」
lines.english: “Anyway!”

lines.japanese: あずさは顔を引き締める。
lines.english: Azusa’s expression grew serious.

lines.japanese: 「携帯、持ってますか」
lines.english: “Do you have your phone on you?”

lines.japanese: 「えーと……あ、ないや……忘れてる」
lines.english: “Let's see… Oh. No… I forgot it.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、持ってきました」
lines.english: “Here. I brought it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、マイ携帯だ」
lines.english: “Hey, it's my phone.”

lines.japanese: 「家にお伺いしたときに、預かってきたんだよ」
lines.english: “I picked it up when I paid a visit to your house.”

lines.japanese: えっへんと胸を張る。
lines.english: She puffed out her chest proudly.

lines.japanese: （ないよあずさ、胸がない―――）
lines.english: (No, Azusa. You don't have a chest to puff out—)

lines.japanese: 「手放したら駄目っていつも言ってるのにー」
lines.english: “I'm always telling you not to leave it behind.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんごめん、つい」
lines.english: “Sorry, sorry. It slipped my mind.”

lines.japanese: 「外出時はぜったい携帯ね」
lines.english: “If you leave the house, you take your phone. Always.”

lines.japanese: 「わかったよ、あずさ」
lines.english: “All right, Azusa.”

lines.japanese: するとあずさは、やわらかく笑った。
lines.english: At that, Azusa smiled gently.

lines.japanese: 「ん、よしよし」
lines.english: “Mm. Good boy.”

lines.japanese: 「水飲む？」
lines.english: “Want some water?”

lines.japanese: 「もらおうかな」
lines.english: “Maybe I will.”

lines.japanese: 「おっけー」
lines.english: “Okey-doke.”

lines.japanese: あずさが忍のマグカップに、水を入れて戻ってくる。
lines.english: Azusa returned with Shinobu's mug full of water.

lines.japanese: 受け取りながら、
lines.english: As he took it—

lines.japanese: 「みんなは？」
lines.english: “Where is everyone?”

lines.japanese: 「今日はあたしだけしかいないよ」
lines.english: “I'm the only one here today.”

lines.japanese: 「……そっか」
lines.english: “…I see.”

lines.japanese: 少し寂しくも思う。
lines.english: He felt a little lonely.

lines.japanese:
仲間に触れたいという思いを、忍は満たしたいの
だから。
lines.english: Shinobu wanted to satisfy the need he felt to be close to his friends.

lines.japanese:
それでもあずさ一人いてくれるだけで、ずいぶん
と落ち着く。
lines.english: Even so, just having Azusa there put him deeply at ease.

lines.japanese:
手を伸ばす。
　小さな手を、握った。
lines.english: He reached out. And took her small hand.
“…Shinobu?”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、あずさ。看病してくれて」
lines.english: “Thank you for looking after me, Azusa.”

lines.japanese:
「っ……い、いいよ……
　そんな、みずくさいなぁ……」
lines.english: “Y-you don't have to thank me… There's no need to be so formal…”

lines.japanese: 「だから……なんでもしたげるよ」
lines.english: “So… I'll do anything for you.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、あずさのしたいことをして欲しいな」
lines.english: “Then what I want is for you to do whatever you want.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、ならこのままでいいみたいだね」
lines.english: “Ahaha. Then I guess I can carry on as I am.”

lines.japanese: 「好きで看病したんだもん」
lines.english: “I'm taking care of you because I want to.”

lines.japanese: 「……ありがとう」
lines.english: “…Thank you.”

lines.japanese:
ぬくもりがあまりにも貴くて、心が沸き立ってし
まいそうになる。
lines.english: Her warmth was so precious that his heart seemed about to overflow.

lines.japanese: （そう……本当は気付いてる）
lines.english: (Yes… Deep down, I know…)

lines.japanese: （あずさの気持ちには―――）
lines.english: (How Azusa feels—)

lines.japanese: （ただ……怖かった）
lines.english: (I was just… afraid.)

lines.japanese: （あずさに応えることで、壊れることが―――）
lines.english: (Afraid that if I returned her feelings, something would break—)

lines.japanese: （あずさに応えることで、恋われることが―――）
lines.english: (Afraid of being loved if I returned them—)

lines.japanese: （……かつての章二のように……）
lines.english: (…The way Shouji once was…)

lines.japanese:
もしかすると世界には今、忍とあずさしかいない
のかも知れない。
lines.english: Perhaps Shinobu and Azusa were the only two people left in the world now.

lines.japanese:
そうであると知ったなら、忍は迷わず少女を抱く
だろう。
lines.english: If he knew it for a fact, Shinobu would take the girl in his arms without a moment's hesitation.

lines.japanese:
だが実際には、樋口章二が《聖域》と呼んだ関係
は、当面崩壊の心配はなさそうである。
lines.english: In reality, however, the relationship Shouji Higuchi had called their “sanctuary” seemed to be in no immediate danger of collapse.

lines.japanese: 彼らの関係は極めて強固であるためだ。
lines.english: The bond between them was simply too strong.

lines.japanese: 「ところで章二、来ないのかな」
lines.english: “I wonder if Shouji will come.”

lines.japanese: あずさは眉根を寄せる。
lines.english: Azusa knitted her brows.

lines.japanese: 「来ないと思うな」
lines.english: “I don't think he is.”

lines.japanese:
「そうか。言いたいことがあったんだけど……
　またにするよ」
lines.english: “I see. I wanted to tell him something… Another time, then.”

lines.japanese:
あずさは。
　穏やかに、まるで十も歳を重ねたような笑みを見
せた。
lines.english: Azusa— smiled serenely, as though she had aged ten years in an instant.

lines.japanese: 「……ねえねえ、映画開きしたんだって」
lines.english: “…Hey, hey, I heard the movie theater reopened.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese:
かつてあずさに、映画に誘われたことを思い出す。
　あの約束は、まだ履行されていない。
lines.english: He remembered the time Azusa had invited him to a movie. They had yet to keep that promise.

lines.japanese: 「行く？」
lines.english: “Want to go?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ忍くんの調子悪いの、治ったら」
lines.english: “Then let's go when you're feeling better.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ、治すよ。もともと映画行く約束だったし」
lines.english: “Sure. I'll get better. We did promise to go to the movies.”

lines.japanese: 「わー、やたー」
lines.english: “Yaaay!”

lines.japanese: にっこりと笑って、
lines.english: She beamed—

lines.japanese: 両手で顔を覆う。
lines.english: and covered her face with both hands.
“…Azusa?”

lines.japanese: 「……あぁ……あたし……駄目だ、弱くて……」
lines.english: “…Oh… I'm hopeless. I'm so weak…”

lines.japanese:
指の隙間からこぼれる水滴。
　震える肩。
　泣いているように見えた。
lines.english: Tears spilled through her fingers. Her shoulders trembled. She seemed to be crying.

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの？」
lines.english: “What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: ふらつく身体に鞭打って、歩み寄る。
lines.english: He forced his unsteady body forward and crossed to her.

lines.japanese:
「う、ううん……なんでもない……
　強くならないといけないから、慰めないで……」
lines.english: “N-no… It's nothing… I have to be strong, so don't comfort me…”

lines.japanese: 「強くても悲しいことはあるよ、きっと」
lines.english: “Even strong people feel sad sometimes. I'm sure they do.”

lines.japanese: 「強くても慰めはいると思うし……」
lines.english: “And I think even strong people need comfort…”

lines.japanese: 肩に手を置く。
lines.english: He placed a hand on her shoulder.

lines.japanese:
「……こわい、のかな……今、なんで泣いてるのか
　……自分でもよくわからなくて……」
lines.english: “…Maybe I'm scared… I don't even know why I'm crying right now…”

lines.japanese: 「こわいことでもあった？」
lines.english: “Did something frighten you?”

lines.japanese: あずさは首を振る。
lines.english: Azusa shook her head.

lines.japanese: 「何かあったの？」
lines.english: “Did something happen?”

lines.japanese: 「なにもない……なにもないはずなのに……」
lines.english: “Nothing… Nothing should have happened…”

lines.japanese:
「最近、突然……
　胸の奥から、わーってきちゃうの……」
lines.english: “Lately, all of a sudden… something comes rushing up from deep inside me…”

lines.japanese: 「僕もあるよ、それ」
lines.english: “That happens to me too.”

lines.japanese: 「本当？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「たまにね」
lines.english: “Sometimes.”

lines.japanese: 「今日も、そうだったんだ」
lines.english: “It happened to me today too.”

lines.japanese: 「理由はわからないけど、いきなり寂しくなった」
lines.english: “I don't know why, but suddenly I felt lonely.”

lines.japanese:
「今ある世界とか、そこに置かれた幸せとかが……
　壊れるのがこわいんだ」
lines.english: “The world we have now, the happiness inside it… I'm afraid it might all fall apart.”

lines.japanese: 「あは……はは……じゃあ、いっしょだね……」
lines.english: “Aha… haha… Then we're the same…”

lines.japanese: 「みんなこわいんだと思うよ」
lines.english: “I think everyone is afraid.”
“Yeah…”

lines.japanese: 優しく抱きしめて、問いかけて。
lines.english: He held her gently and asked once more.

lines.japanese: 「……こわいこと、あった？」
lines.english: “…Did something frighten you?”

lines.japanese: 「あった……あったよぉ……」
lines.english: “There was… There was…”

lines.japanese: さめざめと泣き出した。
lines.english: She broke into quiet sobs.

lines.japanese:
忍は少女が泣きやむまで、ずっと抱きしめ続けて
いた。
lines.english: Shinobu kept holding her until her tears stopped.

lines.japanese: 「忍くん……今日は、よく喋ってくれるね……」
lines.english: “Shinobu… You’re talking to me a lot today…”

lines.japanese: （そんなこともないと思うが……）
lines.english: (I don't think I've said that much…)

lines.japanese:
（……あるいは、それほどあずさも孤独を感じてい
　たのか―――）
lines.english: (…Or perhaps Azusa had been feeling just that lonely—)

lines.japanese:
両目を押さえたまま、あずさは言葉を口内から押
し出す。
lines.english: Still covering her eyes, Azusa forced the words past her lips.

lines.japanese: 「―――好きだよ」
lines.english: “—I love you.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ありがとう」
lines.english: “Yeah. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 目を隠している手をどける。
lines.english: He drew her hands away from her eyes.

lines.japanese:
瞳が開かれていた。
　目尻が少し赤い。
　赤面して涙を浮かべていたが、少し笑ってもいる。
lines.english: Her eyes were open. The corners of her eyes were a little red. Her cheeks were flushed and her eyes wet with tears, yet she was smiling a little, too.

lines.japanese:
「くすんっ……えへ……

lines.japanese: 「わ・か・っ・た・な」

lines.japanese: 万力のような力。

lines.japanese: 「わ、わかったってっ」

lines.japanese: ようやく解放される。

lines.japanese: 「いじめだ」

lines.japanese: 「よく言うぜ」

lines.japanese: 「しかしまあ……」
lines.english: “Still…”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……本当に、誰とも会話してないな、あいつ」
lines.english: “Yeah… She really isn't talking to anyone.”

lines.japanese:
あずさの明るい態度の裏にある、どこか暗い影。
　感じていないメンツなど、工場にはいない。
lines.english: Somewhere behind Azusa's bright manner lay a dark shadow. Everyone at the factory had sensed it.

lines.japanese:
必死になって隠せば隠すほど、あずさの日常が透
けて見えるのだ。
lines.english: The more desperately she hid it, the more clearly her daily life showed through.

lines.japanese:
それでも少女にとって学校での時間は、もとより
たいして価値のあるものではない。
lines.english: Even so, the hours she spent at school had never held much value for her.

lines.japanese:
（だからこそ知り合った……そうでなければ、出会
　わなかった）
lines.english: (That's why we met… Otherwise, we never would have.)

lines.japanese:
健全な関係にいたなら、きっとあずさは華やかな
団子の一つに加わっていただろう。
lines.english: Had her relationships there been healthy, Azusa surely would have joined one of those bright clusters.

lines.japanese: あずさを見つめる章二の目が、どこか優しい。
lines.english: Shouji watched Azusa with a hint of gentleness in his eyes.

lines.japanese: 「章二は……本当はあずさのことを―――」
lines.english: “Shouji… when it comes to Azusa, you really—”

lines.japanese: 腹部に、拳がめりこんでいた。
lines.english: A fist sank into his gut.
“Ghk…!”

lines.japanese: 「すまないな。手が滑りやがった」
lines.english: “Sorry. My hand went and slipped.”

lines.japanese: 「……お、おまえ……不意を……」
lines.english: “…Y-you… caught me off guard…”

lines.japanese: 「ふっふっふ、オレ様ともあろう者が。許せ」
lines.english: “Heh heh heh. Even a man of my caliber makes mistakes. Forgive me.”

lines.japanese: 「こ、呼吸が……」

lines.japanese:
みぞおちを突かれて、呼吸がままならなかった。

lines.japanese: 「……任せるぞ、相棒」
lines.english: “…I'm counting on you, partner.”

lines.japanese: 「……何、言って……ばか……」
lines.english: “…What… are you saying… idiot…”

lines.japanese:
ダメージが抜けたのは、たっぷり一分も経ってか
らだった。
lines.english: A full minute passed before the pain subsided.

lines.japanese: 「……あのさ」
lines.english: “…Hey.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「僕ら、ここにいたらまずくない？」
lines.english: “Should we really be hanging around here?”

lines.japanese: 「なぜだ？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese: （なぜって……このままじゃ変質者扱いだよ……）
lines.english: (What do you mean, why…? At this rate, they'll think we're perverts…)

lines.japanese: 「おい、おまえたち……どこの学校の者だ！」
lines.english: “Hey, you two… What school are you from?”

lines.japanese: 「ちっ、見つかった」
lines.english: “Tch. We've been spotted.”

lines.japanese: 「遅いくらいだ」

lines.japanese:

lines.japanese: 二人は脱兎の如く駆けだした。

lines.japanese: 「待てぇぇ！」

lines.japanese: 待つはずがないのである。

lines.japanese:
背後からの騒動の気配に、あずさは少しだけ振り

lines.english: Sensing a commotion behind her, Azusa glanced back, but Shinobu and Shouji were already gone.

lines.japanese:
学校の廊下で、忍はふと奇妙なタイミングに遭遇
したのである。
lines.english: In one of the school corridors, Shinobu happened upon a strange lull.

lines.japanese: （人が……いない）
lines.english: (There's… no one here.)

lines.japanese:
日中の学校から、普通喧噪が途絶えることはない。

lines.english: Ordinarily, the noise never ceased in a school during the day. Not unless it was a holiday. And today was not a holiday.

lines.japanese: またその静けさは授業中の雰囲気とも異なっていた。

lines.japanese:
教室に大勢いる時は、一人廊下に出てもそれなり

lines.english: When the classrooms were full, even someone alone in the corridor could feel the press of all those people.

lines.japanese:
まるで閑散としていて、突き抜けた感覚がある。

　巨大な建物の内部は、別世界のようだ。
lines.english: It felt utterly deserted, strangely open. Hollow, perhaps. The vast building's interior seemed like another world.

lines.japanese: 自分を見失いそうになる。
lines.english: He felt in danger of losing himself.
(…I'm scared…)

lines.japanese:
忍は不安とともに生きている。
　時折、ふと考え込んでしまい、戻れなくなること
があるのだ。
lines.english: Shinobu lived with anxiety. Sometimes a thought would catch him unawares, draw him in, and leave him unable to find his way back.

lines.japanese:
（人の人生が８０年として、今はまだ半分も生きて

lines.english: (If people live eighty years, I haven't lived even half of mine yet.)

lines.japanese: （安全ではないけど、とりあえずは平和……だけど）
lines.english: (We aren't safe, but for now, at least, it's peaceful… And yet…)

lines.japanese:

lines.english: (If it ends… No, if it all ends in an instant, maybe that would still be better… But what if, in my lifetime, we enter a long age of upheaval?)

lines.japanese: （どうやって、大切なものを守っていくんだ？）

lines.japanese:
（……ただの子供でしかない自分に、できることじ

lines.japanese: （こんな瞬間、見たくない……）
lines.english: (I don't want to see a moment like this…)

lines.japanese: 逃れるように、教室に入る。
lines.english: As if fleeing from something, he entered a classroom.

lines.japanese:
無人。

lines.english: Empty. Dry air.

lines.japanese:
何か叫んだかも知れない。

lines.english: He might have cried out. Terror had hacked his thoughts into fragments.

lines.japanese: 目を閉じる。
lines.english: He closed his eyes.

lines.japanese:
忍は観測力を失う。
　何も見たくはないと、廊下に飛び出す。
lines.english: Shinobu could no longer observe. Wanting to see nothing, he bolted back into the corridor.

lines.japanese:
踵が地面を叩くと、朝から消えない頭痛が、芯か
ら痛むようだった。
lines.english: Each time his heels struck the floor, the headache that had lingered since morning throbbed deep in his core.

lines.japanese: 無視して走った。

lines.japanese: 「はっ、はっ、はっ……」
lines.english: “Hah, hah, hah…”

lines.japanese: 忍は逃げるように、学校を出て行く。
lines.english: Shinobu ran from the school as though fleeing.

lines.japanese: （工場に行こう）
lines.english: (I'll go to the factory.)

lines.japanese:

lines.english: (Anyone who could live in a world with no one else in it… would have to be broken.)

lines.japanese:

lines.japanese: （まともな方が、奇跡なんだ……）
lines.english: (Being sane at all is a miracle…)

lines.japanese: 一心に、足を動かす。
lines.english: He drove his legs onward, thinking of nothing else.

lines.japanese: 街でも、動いている人影を見なかった気がする。
lines.english: He didn’t think he’d seen anyone moving in the streets, either.

lines.japanese:
世界に人が満ちていても、無人の場所はある。
　常から往来があっても、途絶える瞬間がある。
　正気と狂気は人による定義ではあるが。
lines.english: Though the world teemed with people, there were uninhabited places. Even on a busy road, there were moments when traffic ceased. Granted, sanity and madness were only definitions made by people.

lines.japanese:
世界は、無限の正気と狂気の積み重ねによって成

lines.english: One could even imagine the world as an endless accumulation of sanity and madness.

lines.japanese:
戦時中の日本がそうであったように、持続する狂

lines.japanese: 終わってしまった時、どちらの割合が多いのか。

もしかすると、今まで狂いと思っていたものがま

lines.english: Perhaps emotionless numbers would prove that what had always seemed insane was sound, and what had been accepted as normal was the true aberration.

lines.japanese:
眩暈がした。

lines.english: Dizziness swept over him. Had he pushed himself too hard running? It felt almost like anemia.

lines.japanese: よろめき、ソファに沈み込む。

lines.japanese: （章二……学校いなかったな……沙也加も……）

lines.japanese: 学校には誰もいなかった。
lines.english: There had been no one at school.

lines.japanese:
忍にとってはいつもの光景だったはずの、章二と

lines.japanese: 工場に来てみても、誰もいない。
lines.english: And now he had come to the factory only to find it empty.

lines.japanese: 今日のように―――
lines.english: Like today—

lines.japanese:
人がいるといないのとでは、工場の印象はだいぶ

lines.english: The factory felt very different depending on whether anyone was there.

lines.japanese:
かつて誰かがいた空間というものは、時に精神を

lines.english: Spaces that had once held people could sometimes eat away at the mind.

lines.japanese:
取り残された気分になる。

lines.japanese:
しかし不安はない。

中央の空間に数名の人間が火を囲んでいるだけで、

少年の日には、誰もが自分の居場所を持ちたがる。

lines.english: In boyhood, everyone longed for a place to belong. For Shinobu, this was that place.

lines.japanese:
かつて仲間たちと交わした会話を思い出す。

lines.english: He remembered the conversations he had shared with his friends. One happy, comforting memory after another. But if he let his guard down for even a moment, they came bursting out.

lines.japanese:
『……好きは罪ですか？　私はあなたの弱みが好き

lines.english: “…Is love a sin? I love your weakness. Is ‘love’ a sin?”

lines.japanese:

lines.japanese: そして痛みを解するのも今なのだ。

lines.japanese:

lines.japanese:
目を閉じた。

どこか彷徨うような足取りだ。

lines.japanese: 工場だ。
